events.text: Kulottunga's first Kalinga expedition: Kulottunga Chola I sent his army north and quelled the revolt of Southern Kalinga, then a part of the Vengi province — the precursor to the greater Kalinga war of 1110 sung in the Kalingattupparani.
events.belligerents: Chola empire vs rebels of Southern Kalinga
events.outcome: Revolt suppressed; Chola control over southern Kalinga restored
events.commanders: Generals of Kulottunga I
events.source: HCIP V, p. 243

events.text: Nanyadeva founded Simraungadh: the Karnata warrior established the dynasty of Mithila on 10 July 1097, the date preserved on the Simraungadh stone pillar — the polity this atlas carries as Tirhut.
events.outcome: Karnata (Tirhut) rule over Mithila and the eastern Terai, to 1324
events.source: Added with the 800-1188 layer; researched against Britannica, Banglapedia, Epigraphia Indica and regional gazetteers.

events.text: Kulottunga reconquers Vengi: In late 1099 Kulottunga Chola I wrested the Vengi country back from the Western Chalukyas, who had burnt Vengi and expelled his son Vira-Choda between 1091 and 1093, and held the Andhra province until 1117.
events.belligerents: Chola empire vs Western Chalukyas of Kalyani
events.outcome: Chola victory; Vengi held by the Cholas until 1117
events.commanders: Kulottunga I — officers of Vikramaditya VI
events.source: HCIP V, p. 174

events.text: The Lingaraja at Bhubaneswar: The Somavamshi temple to Tribhuvanesvara, its deul fifty-five metres high; the peak of the Kalinga style.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Uchchala and Sussala storm Srinagar: the two brothers of a collateral branch of the Lohara house, who had caught Harsha's eye by their bravery at the failed siege of Dugdhaghata, fled the capital in 1100 when the king took them for rivals to his son Bhoja. They returned almost at once with the Damaras, forced their way into Srinagar and burnt the royal palace. Harsha took refuge in a hut below the city, learned that Bhoja had been murdered, and was killed in an encounter with his enemies in 1101 — ending the first Lohara dynasty and putting Uchchala on the throne as founder of the second.
events.belligerents: Uchchala and Sussala with the Damaras vs King Harsha of Kashmir
events.outcome: Rebel victory; the palace burnt, and Harsha killed the following year — end of the first Lohara dynasty
events.commanders: Uchchala and Sussala — Harsha of Kashmir
events.source: HCIP V, printed p. 99: "Uchchala and Sussala fled for their lives from the capital in A.D. 1100 as the king suspected them to be the rivals of his son Bhoja for the throne. Shortly afterwards the two brothers, with the help of the Damaras, forced their way into the capital and burnt the royal palace." (Note: Harsha's death and Uchchala's accession fall in 1101, just outside the century.)

events.text: Vikramaditya VI marches on the rebel Silahara Bhoja: the Chalukya emperor of Kalyana took the field in person against Bhoja, the Silahara chief of Karahataka (Karad), who had thrown off his allegiance and attacked the neighbouring Sinda chiefs of Erambarage. The emperor encamped on the Bhimarathi river in 1100, but the punishment failed: Bhoja was still ruling as late as 1108, showing how loosely the great Chalukya empire held its border barons.
events.belligerents: Chalukyas of Kalyana vs Silaharas of Karahataka
events.outcome: Indecisive; Bhoja survived and was still ruling in 1108
events.commanders: Vikramaditya VI — Silahara Bhoja
events.source: HCIP V, p. 176

events.text: Fall of Harsha of Kashmir: The brothers Uchchala and Sussala, with Damara baron support, forced their way into Srinagar and burnt the royal palace; the temple-plundering king Harsha, his son Bhoja already murdered, was hunted down and killed, and Uchchala founded the second Lohara dynasty.
events.belligerents: Uchchala and Sussala with the Damara barons vs King Harsha of Kashmir
events.outcome: Harsha killed; Uchchala crowned, founding the second Lohara dynasty
events.commanders: Uchchala, Sussala — Harsha
events.source: HCIP V, p. 99

events.text: Ramapala's elephant army repulsed at Kanauj: having won back Varendra, the Pala king Ramapala tried to restore his family's old reach westward and sent an elephant corps against the Gahadavalas of Kanauj some time between 1100 and 1109. The young Gahadavala prince Govindachandra beat it back, fixing the Pala frontier and announcing the arrival of the man who would dominate the middle Ganga valley for fifty years.
events.belligerents: Palas of Bengal vs Gahadavalas of Kanauj
events.outcome: Gahadavala victory; Pala westward expansion checked
events.commanders: Ramapala — Govindachandra
events.source: HCIP V, p. 30

events.text: Govindachandra repels the Ghaznavids: When Sultan Mas'ud III's officer Hajib Tughatigin crossed the Ganga and the Ghaznavid army took the Gahadavala king Madanachandra prisoner, prince Govindachandra defeated the Muslims and secured his father's release, announcing the Gahadavala revival at Kannauj.
events.belligerents: Gahadavalas of Kannauj vs Ghaznavid army of Mas'ud III
events.outcome: Ghaznavid raid defeated; Madanachandra freed
events.commanders: Prince Govindachandra — Hajib Tughatigin
events.source: HCIP V, p. 95; undated in source — within Mas'ud III's reign (1099-1115), conventionally c. 1109

events.text: Kulottunga’s Kalinga war: the Chola army under the general Karunakara Tondaiman marched north against Anantavarman Chodaganga of Kalinga — the campaign sung in Jayamkondar’s Kalingattuparani, the first war-poem of its kind in Tamil.
events.belligerents: Chola Empire (Kulottunga I; gen. Karunakara Tondaiman) vs Eastern Ganga dynasty (Anantavarman Chodaganga)
events.outcome: Chola victory in the field; Kalinga plundered, though Ganga power soon recovered
events.source: Cross-referenced against Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, and the Chola Empire literature (Aug 2026).

events.text: Vijayabahu I dies — Drove the Cholas from Ceylon and made Polonnaruwa his capital.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Murder of Uchchala and the Damara coup at Srinagar: Kashmir's king Uchchala was killed by his own city-prefect Chudda, whose brother Radda held the throne for a single night before being cut down by Gargachandra, a powerful Damara baron of Lohara. Gargachandra installed Uchchala's half-brother Salhana as a puppet and beat off Uchchala's brother Sussala, who had rushed from Lohara to seize the crown.
events.belligerents: Kashmiri crown factions: Chudda and Radda vs the Damara baron Gargachandra vs Sussala of Lohara
events.outcome: Gargachandra prevailed and made Salhana king; Sussala repulsed
events.commanders: Radda and Chudda — Gargachandra — Sussala
events.source: HCIP V, p. 100

events.text: The Chennakesava at Belur: Vishnuvardhana’s temple to Vijayanarayana, begun after Talakad; the Hoysala style in soapstone.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Battle of Kannegal: The Hoysala Vishnuvardhana's general Gangaraja made a night attack on the army of the Chalukya emperor Vikramaditya VI, encamped at Kannegal under twelve samantas, and routed it — the high-water mark of the Hoysala bid for independence before Vikramaditya's counterstroke forced them back to vassalage.
events.belligerents: Hoysalas of Dorasamudra vs Western Chalukya imperial army
events.outcome: Hoysala victory; Chalukya suzerainty nevertheless reimposed by 1120
events.commanders: Gangaraja (for Vishnuvardhana) — the twelve samantas of Vikramaditya VI
events.source: HCIP V, p. 175 (Sravana Belgola inscription of 1118); battlefield location approximate

events.text: Vikramaditya VI seizes Vengi: When Vikrama Chola left the Andhra viceroyalty for the Chola capital to secure his succession, the aged Vikramaditya VI annexed the Vengi country, at last severing the Eastern Chalukya and Chola realms — his greatest victory over Kulottunga I.
events.belligerents: Western Chalukyas of Kalyani vs Chola empire
events.outcome: Chalukya occupation of Vengi, held until Vikramaditya's death in 1126
events.commanders: Vikramaditya VI — viceroyal officers of Kulottunga I

events.text: Ramapala dies — The Pala who won back Varendra from the Kaivartas; the Ramacharita is his epic.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Sussala crushes Bhikshachara at Lohara: Driven from Srinagar in 1120 by Harsha's grandson Bhikshachara and the Damaras, King Sussala inflicted a crushing defeat on the pretender's army as it advanced on the Lohara fortress and swiftly recovered the throne of Kashmir.
events.belligerents: Sussala of the second Lohara dynasty vs Bhikshachara and the Damara barons
events.outcome: Bhikshachara's army destroyed; Sussala restored in Kashmir
events.commanders: Sussala — Bhikshachara
events.source: HCIP V, p. 100

events.text: The Hoysaleswara at Halebidu: The twin Siva temple of the Hoysala capital, built by the merchants of Dwarasamudra.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Kulottunga I dies — Fifty years on the Chola throne; joined the Vengi and Chola lines.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Vikramaditya VI dies — Fifty years at Kalyani; Bilhana’s Vikramankadevacharita is his life.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Battle of Multan: Muhammad Bahlim, the Ghaznavid governor of the Punjab, fortified Nagaur and declared independence, plundering neighbouring Indian princes; Sultan Bahram Shah marched against the rebel and defeated him at Multan, Bahlim and his sons perishing in the flight.
events.belligerents: Ghaznavid Sultan Bahram Shah vs the rebel governor Muhammad Bahlim
events.outcome: Rebellion crushed; the Punjab restored to direct Ghaznavid rule under Salar Husain
events.commanders: Bahram Shah — Muhammad Bahlim
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 95-96; undated in source, conventionally c. 1128 (Bahram r. 1118-1152)

events.text: Jayasimha of Kashmir executes Bhikshachara: after repeated attempts by Harsha's grandson to win back the Kashmiri throne, King Jayasimha finally trapped and killed him in 1130. It removed the one claimant with a hereditary case against the second Lohara line, and let Jayasimha turn to the far harder task of breaking the Damara barons who had made the last thirty years a bloodbath.
events.belligerents: Jayasimha of Kashmir vs Bhikshachara and his Damara allies
events.outcome: Bhikshachara killed; the rival claim to Kashmir extinguished
events.commanders: Jayasimha — Bhikshachara
events.source: HCIP V, p. 101

events.text: Vishnuvardhana's great raid on the Chalukya heartland: the Hoysala king led his army deep into his overlord's territory during the reign of Somesvara III, taking Banavasi, storming the hill-fort of Uchchangi and laying siege to Panungal (modern Hangal), held by the Kadamba chief Mallikarjuna. The Chalukya army eventually routed the Hoysalas, but the raid showed the empire could no longer control its own vassals.
events.belligerents: Hoysalas of Dvarasamudra vs the Chalukyas of Kalyana and their Kadamba vassals
events.outcome: Hoysalas ultimately routed, but Chalukya prestige badly damaged
events.commanders: Vishnuvardhana — Somesvara III; Kadamba Mallikarjuna
events.source: HCIP V, p. 177

events.text: Basava is born — At Basavana Bagewadi; the vachana poet and reformer.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Lothana's revolt in Lohara: Sussala's half-brother Lothana rose in the mountain principality of Lohara and destroyed the army Jayasimha sent against him — one of the worst reverses of the reign. Lothana's triumph was brief: later the same year his own supporters deposed him, and Jayasimha's half-brother Mallarjuna took the fort instead, leaving Kashmir's western gateway in hostile hands.
events.belligerents: Jayasimha of Kashmir vs Lothana of Lohara
events.outcome: Royal army destroyed; Lothana then deposed by his own partisans
events.commanders: Jayasimha's unnamed general — Lothana
events.source: HCIP V, p. 101

events.text: Jayasimha recovers Lohara from Mallarjuna: a year after his army was wrecked in the same mountains, the Kashmiri king took the fortress of Lohara from his half-brother Mallarjuna. Holding Lohara mattered enormously: it commanded the Pir Panjal route into the valley and had been the launching point of every serious rebellion since 1101. Jayasimha followed up by deposing Vikramaditya of Vallapura and installing his own nominee Gulhana.
events.belligerents: Jayasimha of Kashmir vs Mallarjuna
events.outcome: Jayasimha took Lohara and reinstalled his authority in the hill principalities
events.commanders: Jayasimha — Mallarjuna
events.source: HCIP V, p. 101

events.text: Kulottunga II drives the Gangas off the Godavari: after Vikramaditya VI died in 1126 the Eastern Ganga king Anantavarman Chodaganga had pushed west and taken the country up to the Godavari. Some time before 1134 the Chola emperor Kulottunga II, helped by his feudatories Manda II and the Velananti chief Rajendra-Choda, expelled the Gangas from the Godavari district and restored Chola authority in coastal Andhra.
events.belligerents: Cholas and their Velananti feudatories vs the Eastern Gangas of Kalinga
events.outcome: Chola victory; Gangas pushed back out of the Godavari delta
events.commanders: Kulottunga II, Velananti Rajendra-Choda — Anantavarman Chodaganga
events.source: HCIP V, p. 206

events.text: Siege of Sirahsila: the exiled Lothana built a formidable coalition against Jayasimha of Kashmir — the Damara chief Alamkarachakra of Karnaha, the king's own half-brother Vigraharaja, and Bhoja son of Salhana, encouraged by Viddasiha of the Darad country. Jayasimha penned them in the island fort of Sirahsila. Alamkarachakra bought peace by handing over Lothana and Vigraharaja; Bhoja escaped but later surrendered. HCIP V does not give the year precisely, placing it after 1132.
events.belligerents: Jayasimha of Kashmir vs Lothana's coalition of Damaras, princes and Darad allies
events.outcome: Coalition broken; Lothana and Vigraharaja surrendered to the king
events.commanders: Jayasimha — Lothana, Alamkarachakra, Vigraharaja, Bhoja
events.source: HCIP V, p. 101

events.text: Jayasimha Siddharaja conquers Malwa: After a long-drawn war in which he had earlier captured and released the Paramara Naravarman, the Chaulukya Jayasimha Siddharaja took Naravarman's son Yasovarman prisoner and annexed Avanti (Malwa) to Gujarat some time before 1138.
events.belligerents: Chaulukyas of Gujarat (with Chahamana Asaraja of Nadol) vs Paramaras of Malwa
events.outcome: Yasovarman captured; Malwa annexed to the Chaulukya kingdom
events.commanders: Jayasimha Siddharaja, Asaraja of Nadol — Yasovarman Paramara
events.source: HCIP V, p. 76 ('before A.D. 1138'); date c. 1135-36, disputed

events.text: Ramanuja dies — By tradition at Srirangam, aged 120; the philosopher of Vishishtadvaita.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Vishnuvardhana dies — The Hoysala who built Belur and Halebidu and took the Gangavadi from the Cholas.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Chalukya and Hoysala armies partition Malwa: about 1143 the Chalukya emperor Jagadekamalla II, acting with the Hoysala prince Narasimha, invaded Malava, destroyed the power of the Paramara king Jayavarman and set a man named Ballala on the throne of Dhara. It was the sharpest northward thrust the Deccan made in this century, and it left Malwa as a puppet state fought over by Gujarat, the Deccan and the Paramaras themselves.
events.belligerents: Chalukyas of Kalyana and Hoysalas vs the Paramaras of Malava
events.outcome: Jayavarman deposed; the nominee Ballala installed at Dhara
events.commanders: Jagadekamalla II and Hoysala Narasimha I — Paramara Jayavarman
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 70, 178

events.text: Jayasimha Siddharaja dies — The Chaulukya at Gujarat’s height; patron of Hemachandra, builder of the Sahasralinga tank.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Katudeva seizes Nadol: the Chahamana principality of Nadol in southern Marwar changed hands twice in two years. Asaraja's son Katudeva occupied Nadol in 1143-44, but Rayapala, son of the previous ruler Ratnapala, won it back before 1145. The squabble left the house so weakened that by 1154 Kumarapala of Gujarat could hand Nadol to his own governor.
events.belligerents: Rival branches of the Chahamanas of Nadol
events.outcome: Katudeva held Nadol briefly; Rayapala recovered it before 1145
events.commanders: Katudeva — Rayapala
events.source: HCIP V, p. 86

events.text: Jagadekamalla plunders Lata: continuing the same northern campaign, the Chalukya emperor sacked Lata, the coastal strip around Broach, and won a victory over the Gurjara king — the Chaulukya Kumarapala of Gujarat. It was a raid rather than a conquest, but it opened the long-running Deccan quarrel with Gujarat that Kumarapala, Bijjala and their successors would keep alive for forty years.
events.belligerents: Chalukyas of Kalyana vs the Chaulukyas of Gujarat
events.outcome: Lata plundered; no permanent conquest
events.commanders: Jagadekamalla II — Kumarapala
events.source: HCIP V, p. 178

events.text: Govindachandra takes the Pala country up to Monghyr: some time before 1146 the Gahadavala king of Kanauj and Banaras overran everything the Palas still held as far east as Monghyr on the Ganga, reducing Madanapala's kingdom to a rump. It was the deepest Gahadavala penetration into Bihar and left the Palas caught between Kanauj in the west and the rising Senas in the east.
events.belligerents: Gahadavalas of Kanauj vs the Palas of Bengal and Bihar
events.outcome: Gahadavala conquest of Pala Bihar up to Monghyr
events.commanders: Govindachandra — Madanapala
events.source: HCIP V, p. 32

events.text: Kumarapala defeats Arnoraja and Ballala: Facing a simultaneous invasion by the Chahamana Arnoraja from the north and Ballala of Ujjain from the east on behalf of the pretender Bahada, the new Chaulukya king wounded Arnoraja in battle and forced a marriage-sealed peace, while his generals killed Ballala and re-annexed Malwa up to Bhilsa.
events.belligerents: Chaulukya Kumarapala of Gujarat vs Chahamana Arnoraja of Sakambhari and Ballala of Ujjain
events.outcome: Arnoraja wounded and forced to peace; Ballala killed; Malwa recovered for Gujarat
events.commanders: Kumarapala, generals Vijaya and Krishna, Paramara Yasodhavala — Arnoraja, Ballala
events.source: HCIP V, p. 77; early in Kumarapala's reign, c. 1145 (accession 1143-45)

events.text: Kumarapala deposes the Paramara of Mount Abu: fresh from beating the Chahamana Arnoraja, the Chaulukya king turned on Vikramasimha, the Paramara chief of Chandravati on Mount Abu, who had gone over to his enemies during the war. Kumarapala threw him into prison and installed his nephew Yasodhavala instead. Yasodhavala repaid the favour by killing Ballala of Ujjain in battle for his overlord.
events.belligerents: Chaulukyas of Gujarat vs the Paramaras of Mount Abu
events.outcome: Vikramasimha deposed and imprisoned; Yasodhavala installed as a loyal vassal
events.commanders: Kumarapala — Paramara Vikramasimha
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 72, 77

events.text: The revolt of Sumvara in Saurashtra: while Kumarapala was busy in Malwa a chief named Sumvara rose in Saurashtra, and the veteran Chaulukya minister Udayana lost his life trying to put him down. Kumarapala sent a second army which brought Sumvara to heel; the Chahamana prince Ahladana of Nadol gave decisive help and was rewarded with Kiratakupa near Barmer and other territory.
events.belligerents: Chaulukyas of Gujarat vs Sumvara of Saurashtra
events.outcome: Revolt crushed at the cost of the minister Udayana's life
events.commanders: Udayana, then Kumarapala with Chahamana Ahladana — Sumvara
events.source: HCIP V, p. 77

events.text: Anantavarman Chodaganga dies — Seventy years on the Eastern Ganga throne; began the Jagannath temple at Puri.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Kumarapala's Sapadalaksha campaign: Avenging an insult to his queen, Jayasimha's daughter, Kumarapala led an aggressive expedition against the Chahamana Arnoraja, devastated the Sapadalaksha country around Ajmer and defeated him a second time, though he allowed him to keep his throne.
events.belligerents: Chaulukyas of Gujarat vs Chahamanas of Sakambhari
events.outcome: Sapadalaksha devastated; Arnoraja defeated but retained as ruler
events.commanders: Kumarapala — Arnoraja
events.source: HCIP V, p. 77; chronology p. 873

events.text: The Airavatesvara at Darasuram: Rajaraja II’s temple, a stone chariot with wheels and horses; the last of the great Chola temples.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Battle on the Kalindi: the Pala king Madanapala fought a severe battle near the Kalindi river in the Malda district against an invading army, almost certainly the Senas under Vijayasena. He drove the enemy back to the river, but the success was temporary — some time after the eighth year of his reign he had to surrender Varendra, the Pala homeland in north Bengal, and it never returned to his family.
events.belligerents: Palas of Bengal vs the Senas of Radha
events.outcome: Tactical Pala success, strategic defeat: Varendra lost soon after
events.commanders: Madanapala — Vijayasena
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 32-33

events.text: Sack of Ghazni by Ala-ud-din Jahansuz: Avenging his brothers Qutb-ud-din and Saif-ud-din, the Ghurid Ala-ud-din Husain defeated Sultan Bahram Shah in three successive engagements, stormed Ghazni and gave the imperial city to arson and plunder for seven days and nights — earning the name 'Jahansuz', the World-Burner.
events.belligerents: Ghurids (Shansabanis of Ghur) vs Ghaznavid Sultan Bahram Shah
events.outcome: Bahram fled to Hindustan; Ghazni destroyed, fatally breaking Ghaznavid power (Bahram briefly recovered the ruins before dying in 1152)
events.commanders: Ala-ud-din Husain Jahansuz — Bahram Shah
events.source: HCIP V, p. 96; undated in source, conventionally 1150-51

events.text: Vigraharaja IV conquers Delhi from the Tomaras: The Chahamana Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva) conquered Dhillika (Delhi) from the Tomaras and seized Hansi, fighting repeated battles with the Muslims in the Punjab; his Delhi Siwalik pillar inscriptions boast that he made Aryavarta once more the land of the Aryas.
events.belligerents: Chahamanas of Sakambhari vs Tomaras of Delhi (and Ghaznavid garrisons of the Punjab)
events.outcome: Delhi and Hansi annexed; Chahamana empire extended to the Siwalik hills
events.commanders: Vigraharaja IV — the Tomara ruler of Dhillika
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 82-83; undated in source — within his known dates 1153-1163, c. 1152-64 (disputed) Date: Satish Chandra, History of Medieval India, p. 63 gives 1151 explicitly; The Struggle for Empire (HCIP V), p. 82 bounds it 1153-63. The atlas follows Satish Chandra and records the dispute.

events.text: Vijayasena wrests Varendra from the Palas: About the middle of the twelfth century the Sena king overthrew Bhojavarman of Vikramapura, then invaded Varendri; despite a reverse near the Kalindi river he wrested North Bengal from the Pala Madanapala, making the Senas masters of Gauda, Vanga and Radha.
events.belligerents: Senas of Bengal vs Palas (Madanapala) and Varmans of East Bengal
events.outcome: Sena conquest of North and East Bengal; Pala rule reduced to a remnant in Bihar
events.commanders: Vijayasena — Madanapala; Bhojavarman
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 36-37; 'about the middle of the twelfth century', c. 1150s

events.text: Kakatiya Prola II captures Taila III: When the Kakatiyas of Telingana revolted, the Chalukya emperor Taila III marched on Warangal with the Santara Jagaddeva but was taken prisoner by Prola II, who released him out of professed devotion — a humiliation that shattered Chalukya prestige and invited Bijjala's usurpation.
events.belligerents: Kakatiyas of Telingana vs Western Chalukya empire
events.outcome: Taila III captured and released; Chalukya authority fatally discredited
events.commanders: Prola II — Taila III, Santara Jagaddeva
events.source: HCIP V, p. 179; undated in source — before 1156, c. 1153-57 (disputed)

events.text: Bijjala's usurpation of Kalyani: Emboldened by Taila III's capture by the Kakatiyas, the Kalachuri feudatory Bijjala, aided by the Silahara Vijayaditya of Karahataka and the general Racha, seized the throne of the Deccan in 1156 and occupied Kalyani before 1160, beginning the twenty-five-year Kalachuri usurpation.
events.belligerents: Kalachuris of Mangalavada and allied feudatories vs Western Chalukya empire
events.outcome: Bijjala sovereign of the Deccan (nominal Chalukya sway acknowledged until Taila III's death in 1163)
events.commanders: Bijjala, Silahara Vijayaditya, Dandadhinatha Racha — Taila III
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 179-180

events.text: Rawal Jaisal founded Jaisalmer: the Bhati capital moved from thrice-sacked Lodhruva to a new fort on Trikuta hill, named for its founder.
events.outcome: Jaisalmer replaces Lodhruva as the Bhati seat; the state endures to 1947
events.source: Added with the 800-1188 layer; researched against Britannica, Banglapedia, Epigraphia Indica and regional gazetteers.

events.text: Bijjala's southern campaign: the Kalachuri usurper of Kalyana spent his early years as sovereign subduing the south of the Deccan. Encamped at Balligave in Banavasi before 1162, he destroyed Tagarate in the Shimoga country, defeated the Santara chief Jagaddeva of Pomburcha, and besieged and destroyed the great hill fort of Gutti in Anantapur. Only after this was his hold on the Chalukya inheritance secure.
events.belligerents: Kalachuris of Kalyana vs the Santaras of Pomburcha and the chiefs of the southern Deccan
events.outcome: Kalachuri victory; Tagarate and Gutti destroyed
events.commanders: Bijjala — Santara Jagaddeva
events.source: HCIP V, p. 180

events.text: Kumarapala's Konkan war: Between 1160 and 1162 the Chaulukya king despatched his minister Ambada with a large army against the Silahara Mallikarjuna of Konkan; assisted by the Paramara Dharavarsha and the Chahamana prince Somesvara (who claimed the kill), the Gujarat army slew Mallikarjuna and annexed his kingdom.
events.belligerents: Chaulukyas of Gujarat with Paramara and Chahamana allies vs Silaharas of North Konkan
events.outcome: Mallikarjuna killed; Konkan annexed to Gujarat
events.commanders: Ambada, Dharavarsha, Somesvara — Mallikarjuna
events.source: HCIP V, p. 77 (also p. 83); dated 1160-62

events.text: The Jagannath temple at Puri: Begun by Anantavarman Chodaganga and finished under Anangabhima; the Rath Yatra runs from its gate.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Bijjala defeats the Hoysalas on the Tungabhadra: the Kalachuri king inflicted a reverse on Hoysala Narasimha I on the banks of the Tungabhadra, checking the southern power that had been expanding since Vishnuvardhana. Bijjala also brought the Pandya chief Vijaya Pandya to heel and fought successfully against the Cheras, the Chola Rajaraja II and the Velananti chiefs of Andhra.
events.belligerents: Kalachuris of Kalyana vs the Hoysalas of Dvarasamudra
events.outcome: Kalachuri victory; Hoysala expansion northward checked
events.commanders: Bijjala — Hoysala Narasimha I
events.source: HCIP V, p. 180

events.text: Rudradeva pacifies the Kakatiya kingdom: on succeeding Prola II the Kakatiya king faced a general revolt of his feudatories. He subdued Domma and Meda of the Pakhal country, stripped Malligideva of Polavasa, and burnt the city of Chododaya of Kondapalli, whose rival Bhima fled into the forest abandoning Vardhamanapura. By 1162 Telingana was under a single hand for the first time.
events.belligerents: Kakatiyas of Warangal vs their rebel feudatories
events.outcome: Kakatiya victory; the Telingana chiefs brought under one authority
events.commanders: Rudradeva (Rudra I) — Domma, Meda, Malligideva, Chododaya
events.source: HCIP V, p. 199

events.text: The Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda: Rudradeva’s Kakatiya temple to Siva, Vishnu and Surya, dated 1163.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Basava dies — c. 1167 at Kudalasangama; the vachana poet and founder of the Lingayat movement.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Bijjala dies — The Kalachuri usurper of Kalyani, assassinated; the Lingayat uprising followed.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Kalachuri Jayasimha of Chedi turns back a Turushka raid: the Kalachuri king of Tripuri, who had already fought successfully against Kumarapala of Gujarat and against his namesake Bijjala of the Deccan, repulsed an attack by the Turushkas early in his reign. HCIP V identifies this as the same Muslim raid, led by Khusrav Malik of Lahore, that the Gahadavala Vijayachandra beat back, though whether the two kings acted together is unknown.
events.belligerents: Kalachuris of Tripuri vs a Ghaznavid raiding force
events.outcome: Kalachuri victory; the raid repulsed
events.commanders: Kalachuri Jayasimha — Khusrav Malik's forces
events.source: HCIP V, p. 64

events.text: Kilhana burns Panchapura: Prithviraja II of Sakambhari posted his maternal uncle, the Guhila chief Kilhana, at Asika (Hansi) to keep the Muslims of the Punjab in check. Kilhana burned the city of Panchapura, identified with Panchapattana on the Sutlej, and carried off its ruler as a prisoner — his adversary apparently being Khusrav Malik, the last Ghaznavid, who was then also fighting the Gahadavalas.
events.belligerents: Chahamanas of Sakambhari vs the Ghaznavids of Lahore
events.outcome: Chahamana victory; Panchapura burnt and its ruler captured
events.commanders: Guhila Kilhana of Hansi — Khusrav Malik's forces
events.source: HCIP V, p. 83

events.text: Vijayachandra repels the Muslims: the Gahadavala king of Kanauj and Banaras, whose known dates are 1168 and 1169, beat back a Muslim invasion probably led by Khusrav Malik, the last Ghaznavid ruler of Lahore. It was the last time a Gahadavala turned back a Turkish army; twenty-five years later his son Jayachandra would die facing Muizz-ud-din at Chandawar.
events.belligerents: Gahadavalas of Kanauj vs the Ghaznavids of Lahore
events.outcome: Gahadavala victory; the invasion repulsed
events.commanders: Vijayachandra — Khusrav Malik
events.source: HCIP V, p. 54

events.text: Pandyan Civil War and the sack of Madurai: about 1169 two claimants, Parakrama Pandya and Kulasekhara Pandya, went to war for Madurai. Kulasekhara, backed by the Cholas, besieged and took the city and killed his rival along with members of his family. The help Parakrama had begged from Parakramabahu I of Ceylon arrived too late — and turned a succession quarrel into a twenty-year international war.
events.belligerents: Parakrama Pandya vs Kulasekhara Pandya, backed by the Cholas
events.outcome: Kulasekhara took Madurai and killed Parakrama Pandya
events.commanders: Kulasekhara Pandya — Parakrama Pandya
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 245, 264

events.text: The Sinhalese landing at Ramesvaram: Parakramabahu I sent an army under the generals Lankapura and Jagadvijaya across the strait into the Pandya country, with orders not to stop until Madurai was taken and given to a prince of Parakrama Pandya's house. They won a string of engagements against Kulasekhara's lieutenants and installed the dead king's son Vira Pandya at Madurai — the high-water mark of Ceylonese power on the mainland.
events.belligerents: Ceylon under Parakramabahu I vs Kulasekhara Pandya and the Cholas
events.outcome: Initial Sinhalese success; Vira Pandya installed at Madurai
events.commanders: Lankapura and Jagadvijaya — Kulasekhara Pandya
events.source: HCIP V, p. 264

events.text: Lankapura's head nailed to the gates of Madurai: the Chola counter-stroke came under the general Pallavarayan. The Pallavarayanpettai inscription of Rajadhiraja II's eighth regnal year records that Lankapura was defeated and killed, his head fixed to the gate of Madurai, and Kulasekhara restored to the Pandya throne. The conversion of the Pandya country into a Ceylonese province was averted.
events.belligerents: Cholas and Kulasekhara Pandya vs the Sinhalese army of Parakramabahu I
events.outcome: Decisive Chola victory; Lankapura killed and Kulasekhara reinstated
events.commanders: Pallavarayan for Rajadhiraja II — Lankapura
events.source: HCIP V, p. 265; Sastri, A History of South India, ch. on the later Cholas

events.text: Kumarapala dies — The Chaulukya who took the Jain vows under Hemachandra and banned animal slaughter in Gujarat.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Muizz-ud-din Muhammad takes Multan and Uch: Entering India by the Gomal pass, Shihab-ud-din (Muizz-ud-din) Muhammad of Ghur wrested Multan and Uch from their Qaramitah (Ismaili) chiefs in 1175 — the opening move of the Ghurid conquest of Hindustan.
events.belligerents: Ghurids vs Qaramitah (Ismaili) chiefs of Multan and Uch
events.outcome: Multan and Uch annexed to the Ghurid dominion; by 1182 the Sumra chief of lower Sindh also submitted
events.commanders: Muizz-ud-din Muhammad bin Sam — the Qaramitah chiefs
events.source: HCIP V, p. 117; chronology p. 873

events.text: Vindhyavarman wins Malwa back for the Paramaras: for nearly twenty years Malava had been a province of Gujarat, its Paramara princes reduced to petty 'Mahakumaras' ruling Bhopal and the Narmada districts. In the seventh decade of the century Vindhyavarman, son of Jayavarman, defeated the Chaulukya Mularaja II and recovered the ancestral kingdom, restoring the Paramaras at Dhara for another sixty years.
events.belligerents: Paramaras of Malava vs the Chaulukyas of Gujarat
events.outcome: Paramara restoration; Malwa lost to Gujarat
events.commanders: Vindhyavarman — Mularaja II
events.source: HCIP V, p. 70

events.text: Battle of Kasahrada: The Battle of Kasahrada, also known as Battle of Kayadara or Battle of Gadararaghatta, was fought in 1178 at modern Kasahrada in Sirohi district near Mount Abu.
events.belligerents: Chaulukya dynasty, Feudal states, Paramaras of Chandravati Chauhans of Nadol Chahamanas of Jalor vs Ghurid Empire
events.outcome: Chaulukyan victory Mularaja II defeated Mohmmad Ghori
events.commanders: Mularaja II, Kelhanadeva, Kirtipala — Muhammad of Ghur
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Palnadu: The Battle of Palnadu took place sometime in the years 1178–1182 CE, between a Haihaya king called Nalagamaraju, who ruled the then Gurazala kingdom, and his step-brother.
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)
events.belligerents: Haihaya chiefs of Palnadu - Nalagama of Gurajala with the Velanati Chodas vs Malideva of Macherla with Kakatiya dynasty (Rudradeva)

events.text: Ghurid capture of Peshawar: Turning to the northern route after his disaster at Kasahrada, and invited by Chakradeo of Jammu against the Ghaznavid Khusrav Malik, Muizz-ud-din Muhammad invaded the Punjab and took Peshawar in 1178, opening his decade-long reduction of the last Ghaznavid kingdom.
events.belligerents: Ghurids (allied with Chakradeo of Jammu) vs Ghaznavids of Lahore
events.outcome: Peshawar annexed; the Ghurid vice closed on Lahore (Sialkot 1185, Lahore 1186)
events.commanders: Muizz-ud-din Muhammad — officers of Khusrav Malik
events.source: HCIP V, p. 118; chronology p. 873

events.text: Muizz-ud-din sacks Kiradu and takes Nadol: on the desert march that ended in his defeat at Kasahrada, the Ghurid sultan reached Kiradu near Barmer in Marwar, plundered its temple of Somesvara, and then seized and plundered Nadol, capital of a collateral branch of the Chahamanas. News of Nadol's fall reached Ajmer, where the minister Kadambavasa persuaded the young Prithviraja III to let the invader exhaust himself against Gujarat first.
events.belligerents: Ghurids vs the Chahamanas of Nadol
events.outcome: Ghurid success; Kiradu plundered and Nadol occupied
events.commanders: Muizz-ud-din Muhammad — Chahamana Kelhana

events.text: Prithviraja III storms Gudapura: Early in his reign the young Chahamana king marched against his rebel cousin Nagarjuna, son of Vigraharaja IV, besieged and took the city of Gudapura from which Nagarjuna fled, and hung the severed heads of the rebels on the gates of Ajmer as a warning.
events.belligerents: Prithviraja III of Ajmer vs the rebel prince Nagarjuna
events.outcome: Revolt crushed; Gudapura taken, Nagarjuna's family captured
events.commanders: Prithviraja III — Nagarjuna, Devabhata
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 106-107; shortly after 1178, c. 1180; Gudapura unidentified (coordinates approximate, Ajmer region)
Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)
events.text: Qila Rai Pithora: Prithviraj Chauhan throws a second wall round Lal Kot, c. 1180; the city that Muhammad of Ghor’s slaves took in 1192 and built the Qutb inside.

Muizz-ud-din at the gates of Lahore: raiding India almost every year, the Ghurid sultan reached Lahore in 1181. Khusrav Malik, the last Ghaznavid, bought him off with a treaty and surrendered one of his sons as a hostage. It was the first of three descents on Lahore — 1181, 1184 and 1186 — by which the Ghurids strangled the Ghaznavid kingdom without a pitched battle.
events.belligerents: Ghurids vs the Ghaznavids of Lahore
events.outcome: Ghurid diplomatic victory; a Ghaznavid prince surrendered as hostage
events.commanders: Muizz-ud-din Muhammad — Khusrav Malik
events.source: HCIP V, p. 97

events.text: Somesvara IV restores the Chalukyas at Kalyana: Taila III's son, who had spent the Kalachuri usurpation in obscurity, ascended the throne in 1181-82 and with his general Brahma defeated the Kalachuri rulers Ahavamalla and Singhana within two or three years, recovering Kalyana and the ancestral kingdom. The restoration was real but brief: by 1189 the Yadava Bhillama had taken it all.
events.belligerents: Chalukyas of Kalyana under Somesvara IV vs the Kalachuris
events.outcome: Chalukya restoration; Kalyana and most of the Deccan recovered
events.commanders: Somesvara IV and his general Brahma — Kalachuri Ahavamalla
events.source: HCIP V, p. 182

events.text: Battle of Mahoba: Prithviraja III defeats Paramardi — In his 1182 digvijaya the Chahamana king invaded Jejakabhukti, captured Sirswa on the Pahuj, defeated the Chandella Paramardi and plundered Mahoba and Kalanjara — the war remembered in the Alha-Udal ballads of the Banafar heroes who died defending Mahoba; the Chandellas recovered their capital by 1183.
events.belligerents: Chahamanas of Ajmer vs Chandellas of Jejakabhukti
events.outcome: Chandella army routed; Mahoba and Kalanjara plundered, though Chandella rule was restored within a year
events.commanders: Prithviraja III — Paramardi; the brothers Alha and Udal (tradition)
events.source: HCIP V, pp. 107-108 (Madanpur inscriptions of 1182); chronology p. 874

events.text: Prithviraja III crushes the Bhadanakas: some time before 1182 the young Chahamana king invaded the country of the Bhadanakas, probably the Rewari, Bhiwani and old Alwar tracts south-west of Delhi. Their chief met him with a powerful elephant force and was severely defeated. The campaign secured the approaches to the Delhi region before Prithviraja turned east against the Chandellas in his digvijaya of 1182.
events.belligerents: Chahamanas of Ajmer vs the Bhadanakas
events.outcome: Chahamana victory; the Bhadanaka country subdued
events.commanders: Prithviraja III — the unnamed Bhadanaka chief
events.source: HCIP V, p. 107

events.text: Fall of Sialkot: Returning from his failed 1184 assault on Lahore, Muizz-ud-din Muhammad captured the fort of Sialkot and garrisoned it under Husain son of Kharmil; the Ghaznavid Khusrav Malik besieged it as soon as the Sultan left but was repulsed, sealing the fate of Lahore the next year.
events.belligerents: Ghurids vs Ghaznavids of Lahore (with Khokar tribesmen)
events.outcome: Sialkot taken and held against Khusrav Malik's counter-siege; Lahore fell in 1186
events.commanders: Muizz-ud-din Muhammad, Husain b. Kharmil — Khusrav Malik

events.text: Parakramabahu I dies — Reunited Ceylon; the Parakrama Samudra is his sea.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Five days of murder at Polonnaruva: Mahendra VI of the Kalinga clan killed King Vijayabahu II and seized the Ceylonese throne. Five days later Kirtinihsanka, better known as Nihsankamalla, himself Kalinga-born and Vijayabahu's Uparaja, killed Mahendra and took the crown. He ruled nine years, built temples and tanks, set up milestones along the highroads, and claimed victories over the Cholas and Pandyas.
events.belligerents: Rival Kalinga-descended claimants to the throne of Ceylon
events.outcome: Nihsankamalla seized the throne after killing the usurper Mahendra VI
events.commanders: Mahendra VI — Nihsankamalla
events.source: HCIP V, p. 265

events.text: Battle of Ingalaguppe: After Bhillama V's Seuna (Yadava) army overran the Hoysala kingdom as far as Seringapatam, Ballala II organised a fresh army and confronted the invaders at Ingalakupe (Ingalaguppe), inflicting in 1188-89 a severe defeat that drove the Yadavas out of the Hoysala country and opened Ballala's conquest of the Krishna frontier.
events.belligerents: Hoysalas of Dorasamudra vs Seunas (Yadavas) of Bhillama V
events.outcome: Decisive Hoysala victory; Bhillama withdrew north, losing the Banavasi-Belvola marches to Ballala II by 1192
events.commanders: Ballala II — Bhillama V
events.source: HCIP V, p. 186; chronology p. 874 (dated 1188-1189)

events.text: Battle of Nettur: The Battle of Nettur was an engagement between the Chola Emperor Kulothunga Chola III and Vira Pandya, the claimant to the Pandya throne in 1188.
events.belligerents: Chola Empire and Pandyan kingdom vs Pandyan troops loyal to Vira Pandya
events.outcome: Chola victory
events.commanders: Kulothunga Chola III, Vikrama Pandya — Vira Pandya
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07) (Note: no source in our library gives the site of Nettur; the coordinate is the Nettur near Thalassery and is approximate.)

events.text: The Qutb Minar is begun: Aibak lays the first storey of the victory tower at Delhi; Iltutmish adds three more, Firuz Shah the fifth.

events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent

events.text: Nalanda is sacked: c. 1193-1200, Bakhtiyar Khalji’s raiders destroy the great monastery-university of Magadha, and Odantapuri and Vikramashila with it; the libraries burn. Minhaj describes the taking of a "fortress" whose inmates were all shaven-headed - usually read as Odantapuri. The Tibetan pilgrim Dharmasvamin found Nalanda nearly deserted in 1235.
Ganapati's Coastal Andhra Campaign: Ganapati’s Coastal Andhra Campaign was a major campaign initiated by Kakatiya ruler Ganapati to expand the boundaries of Kakatiya dynasty into Coastal Andhra.
events.belligerents: Kakatiyas Kota Vamsa Natavadi Malyala Chiefs vs Velanati Chodas, Ayya Chiefs
events.outcome: Kakatiya victory, Ganapatideva conquered Velanadu region
events.commanders: Ganapati (Kakatiya dynasty), Vakkadimalla Rudra, Malyala Chaunda — Pruthviswara, Ayya Pinni Choda

events.text: Siege of Kalinjar (1203): The Siege of Kalinjar was a important military campaign of the Ghurid Empire under the leadership of Qutb al-Din Aibak and Iltutmish against the Chandel Empire of Jejakabhukti.
events.belligerents: Ghurid Empire vs Chandel Empire of Jejakabhukti
events.outcome: Ghurid victory
events.commanders: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, Iltutmish — Paramardivarman, Ajaya-Deva

events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent

events.outcome: Chandela victory

events.text: The Ramappa temple at Palampet: Recherla Rudra’s Kakatiya temple, built on sandbox foundations with floating bricks in its sikhara.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Kalinga Magha's conquest of Polonnaruwa: an invasion from the Kalinga coast with a largely south Indian mercenary army deposed and blinded the last king of Polonnaruwa. Magha held the north until about 1236, and the Sinhalese political centre moved permanently to the south-west - the end of the great irrigation civilisation of the dry zone.
events.source: BharatRajya research pass, Sri Lanka (see scripts/add_srilanka_battles.py)

events.outcome: Polonnaruwa sacked; the dry-zone kingdom never recovered

events.text: The Pandyas sack Thanjavur: Maravarman Sundara Pandya stormed the Chola country, burned Thanjavur and Uraiyur, and drove Rajaraja III into exile — vengeance for a century of Chola overlordship, and the blow the dynasty never recovered from.
events.belligerents: Pandya dynasty (Maravarman Sundara) vs Chola Empire (Rajaraja III)
events.outcome: Pandya victory; the Chola heartland devastated, Chola kingship restored only as a dependent
events.source: Cross-referenced against Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, and the Chola Empire literature (Aug 2026).

events.text: Veera Ballala II dies — The Hoysala who took the imperial title and held the Deccan between the Yadavas and the Cholas.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Mongol invasions of India
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Chagatai Khanate
events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate Victory
events.commanders: Delhi Sultans Iltutmish, Balban, Alauddin Khalji and Tughlaq rulers by campaign — Chinggisid and Chagatai leaders including Genghis Khan, Duwa, Qutlugh Khwaja, Taraghai and related commanders

events.text: Battle of Bhutala: The Battle of Bhutala took place in modern-day Rajasthan between Maharawal Jaitrasimha of Mewar and Sultan Iltutmish of the Delhi sultanate somewhere between 1222 and 1229 A.D.
events.belligerents: Rajput Confederacy, Guhila dynasty, Vaghela dynasty, Paramaras, Chahamanas vs Delhi sultanate
events.outcome: Rajput victory
events.commanders: Jaitrasimha, Viradhavala, Dharavarsa — Iltutmish
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Kadava capture of Rajaraja III: Kopperunjinga takes the emperor prisoner — the Kadava chief defeated Rajaraja III and held him captive at Sendamangalam until Hoysala Narasimha II marched to his rescue — a Chola emperor imprisoned by his own feudatory.
events.belligerents: Kadava chiefdom (Kopperunjinga) vs Chola Empire (Rajaraja III), relieved by the Hoysalas
events.outcome: Rajaraja III restored by Hoysala arms; Chola sovereignty visibly hollow
events.source: Cross-referenced against Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, and the Chola Empire literature (Aug 2026).

events.text: Iltutmish dies — The sultan who finished the Qutb Minar and named his daughter his heir.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Moinuddin Chishti dies — At Ajmer; the Gharib Nawaz, founder of the Chishti order in India.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Madhvacharya is born — At Pajaka near Udupi.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Razia Sultan dies — Killed near Kaithal with her husband Altunia, fleeing the nobles who had deposed her.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Battle of Katasin: The Battle of Katasin was fought in 1243 CE between Narasingha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty and Tughral Tughan Khan, the governor of the Mamluk dynasty of Delhi, at Katasin.
events.belligerents: Eastern Ganga dynasty vs Delhi Sultanate
events.outcome: Eastern Ganga dynasty victory
events.commanders: Narasingha Deva I — Tughral Tughan Khan, Fakr-Ul-Mulk Karimuddin Laghri
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.outcome: Eastern Ganga Victory

events.text: Singhana II dies — The Yadava at Devagiri’s widest reach.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: The Javaka invasions of Chandrabhanu: the ruler of Tambralinga in the Malay peninsula landed twice on the northern coast. Both attempts were repelled, the second with Pandya help.
events.source: BharatRajya research pass, Sri Lanka (see scripts/add_srilanka_battles.py)

events.outcome: Both invasions repelled

events.text: The sun temple at Konark: Narasimhadeva I’s chariot of Surya, twelve pairs of wheels and seven horses, on the shore; the "Black Pagoda" of the sailors.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Amir Khusrau is born — At Patiyali on the Ganga.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Battle of Mudugur: The Battle of Mudugur was a mid-13th century conflict fought between the forces of the Pandyan Empire under Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I and a coalition.

events.outcome: Pandyan victory The Pandyas captured Nellore and incorporated it into the Pandyan Empire
events.commanders: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I — Ganapati-deva, Manumasiddhi II
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Srirangam (1262 CE): The Battle of Srirangam was a major conflict between the Pandya dynasty under Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I and the Hoysala Empire led by Vira Someshvara.
events.belligerents: Pandya dynasty vs Hoysala Empire
events.outcome: Pandyan victory
events.commanders: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I — Vira Someshwara
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Ganapati Deva dies — Sixty-three years on the Kakatiya throne; Warangal’s builder.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I dies — The Pandya who took Kanchi and the Chola country; the empire’s zenith.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: The Kesava temple at Somanathapura: The Hoysala general Somanatha’s three-shrined temple, the most complete of its kind.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Jnaneshwar is born — At Apegaon on the Godavari.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Balban's conquest of Bengal: Ghiyath al-Din Balban's campaign in Bengal (1277–1281) was a major expedition to reconsolidate the Delhi Sultanate's authority over Bengal.
events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Bengal
events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory
events.commanders: Balban, Amin Khan, Tirmati Khan — Tughral Tughan Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: The Chola empire ends: Maravarman Kulasekhara Pandya defeated the Hoysalas at Kannanur Kuppam and, in the same war, the last Chola emperor Rajendra III disappears from the record — four hundred and thirty years after Vijayalaya took Thanjavur.
events.belligerents: Pandya dynasty (Maravarman Kulasekhara) vs Hoysala Kingdom and the last Cholas (Rajendra III)
events.outcome: Pandya victory; the Chola state ceases to exist
events.source: Cross-referenced against Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India, and the Chola Empire literature (Aug 2026).

events.text: Battle of Beas River: The Battle of Beas River took place between the Chagatai Khanate and the Mamluk Sultanate of Delhi on 9 March 1285.
events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate (Balban; Prince Muhammad, who fell) vs the Chagatai Mongols
events.outcome: Mamluk victory Mongol forces withdrew Balban’s son Muhammad Khan killed in Multan
events.commanders: Unknown — Ghiyas ud din Balban, Muhammad Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Balban dies — The slave-sultan of the iron hand; broken by the death of his son Muhammad on the Mongol frontier.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Rudrama Devi dies — The Kakatiya queen, killed in battle against the Kayastha chief Ambadeva (Chandupatla inscription).
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Capture of Jhain: The Capture of Jhain was a military expedition carried out by the Delhi Sultanate under Jalal-ud-din Khalji against the Kingdom of Ranthambore.
events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Chauhans of Ranthambore
events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory
events.commanders: Jalaluddin Khalji — Gurdan Saini
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory
events.commanders: Alauddin Khalji — Mahalakadeva
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory

events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Khalji invasion of Mithila: The Khalji invasion of Mithila took place between 1297–1298 as a military expedition led by the Delhi Sultanate against the Karnats of Mithila in present-day Northern Bihar.
events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Karnats of Mithila
events.outcome: Dehli Sultanate victory
events.commanders: Sheikh Ismail — Shaktisimhadeva
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory
events.commanders: Kadar — Ulugh Khan, Zafar Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.outcome: Delhi-Soomra victory
events.commanders: Saldi — Zafar Khan, Chanesar II
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Gujarat: Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Gujarat, also known as the Muslim conquest of Gujarat, began in 1299 when the Delhi Sultanate ruler Alauddin Khalji sent an army.
events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory Fall of Vaghelas
events.commanders: Alauddin Khalji, Ulugh Khan, Nusrat Khan — Karna II
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Chagatai Mongols
events.outcome: Delhi victory
events.source: Curated sweep (Sarkar; Majumdar; Schwartzberg)

events.text: Hammira Deva dies — The Chauhan of Ranthambore, killed when Alauddin took the fort after a year’s siege.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Rebellions against Alauddin Khalji: Alauddin Khalji, the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate in India, faced three rebellions in 1301 while engaged in the conquest of Ranthambore.
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.outcome: Delhi victory
events.source: Curated sweep (Sarkar; Majumdar; Schwartzberg)

events.text: Mongol invasion of India (1303): a Chagatai army under Taraghai reached Delhi itself while two of the Sultanate's field armies were away; Alauddin Khalji held the city and the Mongols withdrew — the first of two Chagatai invasions three years apart.

events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory
events.commanders: Taraghai — Alauddin Khalji

events.text: Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Malwa: In 1305, the Delhi Sultanate ruler Alauddin Khalji sent an army to capture the Paramara kingdom of Malwa in central India.
events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Paramara dynasty
events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory End of Paramara Dynasty
events.commanders: Alauddin Khalji, Ayn al-Mulk Multani — Mahalakadeva, Gogadeva
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.belligerents: Delhi Sultanate vs Chagatai Mongols
events.outcome: Delhi victory
events.source: Curated sweep (Sarkar; Majumdar; Schwartzberg)

events.text: Mongol invasion of India (1306): Duwa sent a fresh Chagatai expedition under Kopek to answer the reverse of 1305; it was met and broken up in the Punjab river country by Malik Kafur and Malik Tughluq — a separate invasion from that of 1303.

events.outcome: Delhi victory; Mongol forces expelled from India.

events.outcome: Khalji victory

events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: The sack of Ghumli: Jam Barmaniyaji Jadeja stormed the Jethwa capital in the Barda hills, avenging his father Jam Unaji's defeat of 1309. Rana Bhanji Jethwa fled to Ranpur and Ghumli, capital of western Saurashtra since the Saindhavas, was never rebuilt.

events.outcome: Jadeja victory; Ghumli destroyed
events.source: Wikipedia: Ghumli; Jethwa dynasty

events.text: Alauddin Khalji dies — Conqueror of Gujarat, Ranthambore, Chittor and the south; his general Malik Kafur was killed weeks later.

events.outcome: Tughluq victory

events.text: Prataparudra II dies — The last Kakatiya, taken at Warangal by Ulugh Khan; drowned himself in the Narmada on the road to Delhi.

events.outcome: Delhi Sultanate victory

Ming–Kotte War: Zheng He carries off Vira Alakesvara — the Ming admiral's fleet took the last king of the Gampola line, ruling from Kotte, captive to China, the only occasion on which a Chinese expedition removed a South Asian ruler. events.text: Battle of Khed: The Battle of Khed took place on 12 October 1707, between Shahu I and the forces of Tarabai led by Dhanaji Jadhav.
events.belligerents: Forces of Shahu I vs Forces of Tarabai
events.outcome: Shahu's victory
events.commanders: Shahu I, Parsoji Bhonsle, Malharraje Korde — Dhanaji Jadhav, Parshuram Pant Pratinidhi, Balaji Vishwanath
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 47: 'The old soldier refused to take arms against his legitimate sovereign and carried with him the major part of the army. The remnant was too small to make a stand against the combined forces and fled to Satara. (Battle of Khed, 12 October 1707).'

events.belligerents: Bahadur Shah I vs Azam Shah
events.outcome: Bahadur Shah I victory
events.commanders: Bahadur Shah I Jahandar Shah, Azim-ush-Shan, Farrukh-Siyar — Azam Shah Bidar Bakht

events.text: Siege of Dannemarksnagore (1707): The siege of Dannemarksnagore took place in 1707 at the Danish colony of Dannemarksnagore in Bengal, between the Danes and the Mughal subahdar of Bengal, Azim-ush-Shan.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire Bengal Subah vs Danish India
events.outcome: Inconclusive
events.commanders: Azim-ush-Shan — Jacob Panck
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Guru Gobind Singh dies — At Nanded on the Godavari, of a wound from an Afghan assassin; the tenth and last living Guru.
events.source: HCIP VIII, The Maratha Supremacy p. 126: 'After the assassination of Guru Govind Singh in 1708, the Sikhs got a leader in Banda, his chosen disciple.' Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 5 places him at Nander in September 1708.

events.text: Rajput Rebellion (1708–1710): The Rajput rebellion began in 1708, due to the harsh treatment of the Rajput Rajas by the Mughal emperor.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Marwar, Kingdom of Mewar and Kingdom of Jaipur vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Rajput victory Mughal emperor sued for peace.
events.commanders: Ajit Singh of Marwar, Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber, Amar Singh II of Mewar, Durgadas Rathore — Bahadur Shah I
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Shahu crowned at Satara: after Khed, Shahu took Satara from Tarabai's garrison and ascended the Maratha throne in January 1708; Tarabai withdrew to Panhala and Rangna, and the Maratha state split into two lines.
events.source: HCIP VIII (The Maratha Supremacy) p. 47: 'It was on a Saturday in January 1708, that the victorious entry was made'; p. 48: 'After a week's time Shahu ascended the Gadi in ceremony and appointed his new ministers.' Chronology p. 813: '1708, January  Raja Shahu ascends the Maratha throne at Satara.'

events.outcome: Sikh victory; crusading forces defeated and dispersed.

events.outcome: Mughal victory
events.commanders: Jalal Khan Orakzai, Dindar Ali Khan, Hazbar Khan — Banda Singh Bahadur

events.outcome: Rajput victory

events.text: Bahadur Shah I dies — At Lahore on 27 February 1712, the last Mughal emperor who 'held the reins of administration fast in his hands'; the war of succession that followed made the Sayyid brothers king-makers.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 15-16: 'About the middle of January 1712 his health began to decline and he died on 27 February, 1712... With the death of Bahadur Shah disappeared even the last semblance of the glory and greatness of the Mughuls.'

events.text: Battle of Jammu (1712): The Battle of Jammu was fought between the Sikhs under the command of Banda Singh Bahadur against the Mughal forces near the hills of Jammu on 22 January 1712.
events.belligerents: First Sikh State vs Mughal Empire, Hindu rulers of the Deva dynasty of Jammu
events.outcome: Mughal victory
events.commanders: Banda Singh Bahadur — Rustamdil Khan, Muhammad Amin, Aghar Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Balaji Vishwanath becomes Peshwa, beginning the Peshwa-led Maratha expansion
events.source: Stewart Gordon

events.text: Battle of Agra (1713): Farrukhsiyar, backed by the Sayyid brothers of Barha, defeats his uncle the emperor Jahandar Shah near Agra and takes the Mughal throne; Jahandar is betrayed by Asad Khan and put to death with Zulfiqar Khan.
events.belligerents: Farrukhsiyar and the Sayyid brothers vs Jahandar Shah and Zulfiqar Khan
events.outcome: Farrukhsiyar victory; Jahandar Shah fled to Delhi, was betrayed and killed, and the Sayyid brothers became the power behind the throne
events.commanders: Farrukhsiyar, Sayyid Abdullah Khan, Sayyid Husain Ali — Jahandar Shah, Zulfiqar Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII (The Maratha Supremacy) p. 17: 'Near Agra he confronted the hastily assembled hosts of his uncle. Treachery in his camp, combined with improper disposition of his forces; brought defeat upon the head of Jahandar Shah, who, with his mistress, fled to Delhi in a bullock cart.'; chronology p. 814: '1713, January Farrukh-siyar ascends the Mughul throne'

events.text: Raid on Dannemarksnagore: The raid on Dannemarksnagore took place in 1713 at the Danish colony of Dannemarksnagore in Bengal, between the Danes and a local Mughal zamindar.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire Bengal Subah vs Danish India
events.outcome: Mughal victory
events.commanders: zamindar — Rasmus Attrup
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Second Battle of Lohgarh: The Second Siege of Lohgarh, also known as the Second Siege of Lohgarh and Saudhara, was fought in 1713 by Sikh forces led by Banda Singh Bahadur and Mughal forces.
events.belligerents: Khalsa vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Saudhara: Mughal victory; Saudhara captured by the Mughals.
events.commanders: Banda Singh Bahadur — Abd al-Samad Khan, Zakariya Khan, Zain-ud-din Ahmed Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Palace coup at Kolhapur: Rajasbai, Rajaram's second wife, imprisons Tarabai and her son Shivaji II and puts her own son Sambhaji II on the throne. The Kolhapur line continues under Sambhaji II.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 23: 'During the monsoon of 1714 Rajasbai contrived to put Tarabai and her son Shivaji in confinement and place her own son Sambhaji in the Chhatrapati's seat.' HCIP VIII p. 54: 'About this time Tara Bai ... lost her power in Kolhapur and was thrown in confinement.'

events.text: Rudra Singha dies — The Ahom king (r. 1696–1714) who brought his neighbours under Ahom rule and planned a league of eastern rajas to drive out the Mughals; after him the kingdom declined.
events.source: Acharyya, History of Medieval Assam p. 131 (chronology of Ahom kings): 'Sukhrungpha or Rudra Singha ... 1696 1714'; p. 275: 'the Ahom king Rudra Singha, a man of great ability and ambition, organised a confederacy of the Rajas of Eastern India with a view to oust the Mughals. After this king, the history of the Ahoms is one of internal strifes.' (Place of death, Gauhati, is web-only.)

events.text: The agreement of Lonavla: Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath meets Kanhoji Angre at Valvan near Lonavla and wins him from Tarabai's side to Shahu's. Kanhoji keeps the fleet, his Konkan territory and the title of Sarkhel.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 26: 'they had a cordial meeting at Valvan, a suburb of Lonavla, early in January 1714.' HCIP VIII p. 54: 'On being confirmed in command of the fleet, his territory in Konkan and his title of Sarkhel, he agreed to renounce Shambhuji ... and maintain the cause of Shahu.'

events.text: Battle of Gurdas Nangal
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 6: '[Baj Singh] was taken prisoner along with Banda in December, 1715.' HCIP VIII p. 18: 'Banda ... was compelled to evacuate Lohgarh and retreat to Gurdaspur ... The place was stormed and Banda was forced into submission.'
events.belligerents: First Sikh State vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Mughal victory
events.commanders: Banda Singh Bahadur / First Sikh State — Farrukhsiyar; Abdus Samad Khan and Mughal commanders

events.text: Battle of Pilsud: The Battle of Pilsud was fought between Sawai Jai Singh and the Marathas under Kanhoji Bhonsle and Khanderao Dabhade.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Jaipur, Bundelkhand, Bundi, Raghogarh vs Maratha Confederacy Afghan chieftains
events.outcome: Rajput victory
events.commanders: Jai Singh II, Chhatrasal Bundela, Budh Singh Hada — Kanhoji Bhonsle, Khanderao Dabhade, Ganga Rao
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Banda Singh Bahadur dies — Executed at Delhi with hundreds of his followers after the fall of Gurdas Nangal.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 6: 'He was taken prisoner along with Banda in December, 1715. Banda was executed on June 9, 1716.' HCIP VIII p. 18: 'The place was stormed and Banda was forced into submission, brought to Delhi where he was brutally put to death.'

events.text: Murshid Quli Khan made full subahdar of Bengal (September 1717): already diwan and ruler of Orissa, he becomes governor of Bengal in his own right, rules it free of Delhi and moves the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 104: 'In September, 1717, he was made full subahdar of Bengal ... He transferred the capital of Bengal from Dacca to Murshidabad, which was named after him.' Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 44: 'in 1717 the substantive governor in addition to his diwan-ship.'

events.text: Farrukhsiyar deposed and strangled: the Sayyid brothers seize the emperor in the Delhi palace (February 1719), imprison and torture him and have him strangled in April — the first Mughal sovereign killed at the behest of a noble; the puppets Rafi-ud-Darajat and Rafi-ud-Daulah follow.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 19-20: 'He was overpowered, arrested, and consigned to prison... At last, executioners were sent and they strangled him to death in April 1719. This was the first instance of a sovereign of the Mughul dynasty losing his life at the behest of a noble.'

events.text: Bajirao I becomes Peshwa: Shahu gives the robes of office at Masur to Balaji Vishwanath's twenty-year-old son on 17 April 1720, over the objections of older ministers.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 63: 'Baji Rao, the eldest son of Balaji Vishwanath, who was about twenty years old, succeeded him in the Peshwaship on 17 April, 1720 ... conferred the robes of the Peshwaship on Baji Rao at Masur.'

events.text: Balaji Vishwanath dies — the first Peshwa, who won Shahu his throne and the Deccan chauth grants of 1719; called 'the second founder of the Maratha State'.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 61: 'he retired to Saswad near Poona and died there on 2 April, 1720 ... Balaji Vishwanath has been truly called the second founder of the Maratha State.'

events.text: Battle of Balapur: The Battle of Balapur marked a civil conflict among Mughal leaders, triggered by the uprising of the Sayyid Brothers.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire, (under Nizam) vs Sayyid Brothers, Maratha Confederacy, Kingdom of Rohilkhand
events.outcome: Nizam's victory
events.commanders: Nizam-ul-Mulk, Iwaz Khan, Ghiyas Khan — Mughals allies:, Sayyid Hussain Ali Khan Barha, Sayyid Salabat Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Hasanpur: after the murder of Sayyid Husain Ali, Emperor Muhammad Shah's army meets Sayyid Abdullah Khan's forces fifty miles south of Delhi (13–14 November 1720); Abdullah is crushed and captured, ending the Sayyid ascendancy.
events.belligerents: Muhammad Shah (Mughal Empire) vs Sayyid Abdullah Khan
events.outcome: Muhammad Shah victory; Sayyid Abdullah Khan defeated and taken prisoner, poisoned two years later
events.commanders: Muhammad Shah, Muhammad Amin Khan, Haidar Quli Khan — Sayyid Abdullah Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 23: 'the imperial army reached Hasanpur, fifty miles south of Delhi on 14 November, 1720... But ‘Abdullah suffered a crushing defeat at the battle of Hasanpur. He was taken prisoner'; chronology p. 815 dates the battle 13 November 1720

events.text: Battle of Ratanpur (1720): The Battle of Ratanpur or Battle of Pandhar or Battle of Husainpur or Battle of Khandwa in June 1720 A.D.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire Deccan Subah vs Mughal Empire Sayyid Brothers
events.outcome: Nizam's victory
events.commanders: Nizam ul Mulk, Iwaz Khan, Ghiyas Khan — Dilawar Ali Khan, Sher Khan, Babar Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Fatehpur Sikri: The Battle of Fatehpur Sikri occurred near Fatehpur Sikri on 26 September 1721 between Mughal forces and those of the Jats.
events.belligerents: Jat Confederacy vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Mughal victory
events.commanders: Muhkam Singh Sinsinwar, Shardul Singh — Nilkanth Nagar
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Haidar Ali born — the Mysore soldier who rose under Nanjaraj, made himself master of the kingdom in 1761 and fought the Company, the Marathas and the Nizam. (Birth year uncertain: Rao gives '1717? 1722'.)
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore II p. 205 (block 205): 'two sons, Muhammad Sabas Sahib and Haidar Ali (b. 1717? 1722)'; p. 206: 'Haidar's place of birth is not known for certain. It was either Budikote ... or Kolar'; Rao III p. 393-394: died December 1782 'at the age of sixty'.

events.text: Saadat Khan founds the Nawabate of Awadh
events.source: R. C. Majumdar

events.text: Battle of Shakarkheda (Sakharkherda): Nizam-ul-Mulk, with Maratha help, defeats and kills Mubariz Khan, the emperor's governor of Hyderabad. The victory lets him take Hyderabad and rule the Deccan independently.
events.belligerents: Hyderabad, Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Hyderabad victory; Mubariz Khan defeated and slain, Hyderabad occupied by early 1725
events.commanders: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah, Peshwa Bajirao I — Mubariz Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 120: 'A decisive battle was fought in October 1724 at Sakharkharda in Berar where Mubariz Khan was defeated and slain.' p. 67: 'the Nizam defeated his rival Mubariz Khan at Shakarkharda (1 October, 1724) with the help of his Maratha allies.'

events.text: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah founds the state of Hyderabad in the Deccan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 120: 'A decisive battle was fought in October 1724 at Sakharkharda ... taking possession of Hyderabad by the beginning of 1725. "From this period may be dated", writes Irvine, "Nizam-ul-Mulk's virtual independence and the foundation of the present Hyderabad State."' The HCIP VIII chronology (p. 816) dates independence to 1725. The books put it in 1724–25.

events.text: Baji Rao's Karnatak expeditions: two campaigns (Nov 1725–May 1726 against Chitradurga, Nov 1726–Apr 1727 to Srirangapatna) carry Maratha tribute-collection into the far south; the Raja of Mysore buys the army off.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mysore
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Raja of Srirangapatna submits and pays a tribute of 21 lakhs
events.commanders: Baji Rao I, Fatehsinh Bhosle — Dodda Krishnaraja Wodeyar I
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 88 (block 73): 'the first from November, 1725 to May 1726 and the second from November 1726 to April 1727 ... named after Chitaldurg and ... Shrirangapattan'; p. 91-92 (block 75): 'The Raja of Shrirangapattan also offered his submission by paying a tribute of 21 lacs in cash.'

events.text: Battle of Aras: near Aras on 8 February 1725, Pilaji Gaekwad deserts Rustam Ali Khan, the Mughal governor of Surat. Hamid Khan and Kanthaji Kadam Bande then overwhelm Rustam Ali, and Mughal Gujarat's chauth is shared out among the Maratha captains.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Kanthaji Kadam Bande, Pilaji Gaekwad), Hamid Khan vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Maratha and Hamid Khan victory; Rustam Ali Khan overwhelmed after his Maratha ally changed sides
events.commanders: Hamid Khan, Kanthaji Kadam Bande, Pilaji Gaekwad — Rustam Ali Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 281: 'The two forces sighted each other near Aras on 7 February, 1725 ... When, on the next day, issues were joined, Rustam Ali Khan found himself deserted by his Maratha ally and was overwhelmed by the joint forces of Hamid Khan and Kanthaji Kadam Bande.'

events.text: Gharib Niwaz’s invasions of Burma: Manipur’s greatest king throws off Burmese overlordship and leads repeated raids into the Burmese plains (1725, 1735, 1738, 1739, 1749).
events.belligerents: Manipur vs Toungoo (Burmese) kingdom
events.outcome: Manipur victory; 'several successful expeditions into Burma' — reversed after his death, when from 1755 Burma dominated Manipur
events.commanders: Gharib Niwaz (Pamheiba) — Toungoo kings
events.source: HCIP IX p. 1027: 'Gharib Niwaz, the most powerful ruler of Manipur, led several successful expeditions into Burma in 1725, 1735, 1738, 1739 and in 1749. Due to disunity among the successors of Gharib Niwaz, however, Manipur lost her independence.'

events.text: Maratha–Portuguese War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Confederacy vs Portuguese Empire / Portuguese India
events.outcome: Inconclusive
events.commanders: Shahu I and Peshwa Baji Rao I / Maratha commanders — Portuguese Estado da Índia viceroys/governors at Goa

events.text: Murshid Quli Khan dies — First independent Nawab of Bengal, who moved the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad and remade the revenue system through contractors who became the zamindars.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 106: 'After the death of Murshid Quli Khan, on 30 June, 1727, without any male issue, his son-in-law Shuja-ud-din Muhammad Khan ... ascended the masnad of Bengal.' Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 44: 'When he died (30th June, 1727)'.

events.text: Battle of Amjhera: Chimaji Appa surprises Girdhar Bahadur, the Mughal governor of Malwa, at Amjhera on 29 November 1728. He destroys the Mughal army, and the Mughal administration of Malwa does not recover.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Girdhar Bahadur and Daya Bahadur slain, Mughal army annihilated
events.commanders: Chimaji Appa — Girdhar Bahadur, Daya Bahadur
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 81: 'surprised the Subahdar Girdhar Bahadur in his camp at the border town of Amjhera (November 29, 1728) ... the Mughul force was annihilated, its commanders Girdhar and his cousin Daya Bahadur ... were slain ... It was a complete victory for Chimnaji'; p. 145: 'The Mughul administrative control ... had been rapidly breaking up since the battle of Amjhera (November, 1728)'.

events.text: Battle of Palkhed: Baji Rao I outmanoeuvres the Nizam — a masterclass of mobile warfare
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 69: 'The Nizam found himself challenged for action in a waterless tract near Palkhed on 25 February. Starved of food and water, the Nizam's army would not fight ... a treaty was concluded at Mungi-Paithan in pargana Shevgaon on 6 March, 1728. The main articles were the recognition of Raja Shahu as Chhatrapati'.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Nizam, cut off from food and water near Palkhed on 25 February 1728, sued for terms and by the treaty of Mungi-Shevgaon (6 March 1728) recognised Shahu as Chhatrapati with the chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six subahs
events.commanders: Peshwa Bajirao I — Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I, Iwaz Khan

events.text: Battle of Bundelkhand: The Battle of Jaitpur was fought between the Maratha Empire under Peshwa Baji Rao I, on behalf of Chhatrasal Bundela, the ruler of Bundelkhand; and the Mughal Empire.
events.belligerents: Panna, Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire (Muhammad Khan Bangash)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Baji Rao relieved Chhatrasal and defeated Muhammad Khan Bangash, receiving a jagir in Bundelkhand
events.commanders: Chhatrasal, Peshwa Bajirao I, Chimaji Appa — Muhammad Khan Bangash, Qaim Khan Bangash
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 817: '1729, March 22 Peshwa Baji Rao, on a request from Chhatrasal Bundela for help, defeats Muhammad Khan Bangash and obtains a Jagir in Bundlekhand (pp. 83, 139, 40).'

events.text: Kanhoji Angre dies — admiral (Sarkhel) of the Maratha fleet, who fought off the English, Portuguese and Siddis along the Konkan coast.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 817: '1729, June 20 Death of Kanhoji Angria'; Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II chronology p. 133: '1729, July 4 Kanhoji Angria dies.' (HCIP VIII p. 299 prints the year as '20 June, 1720', a misprint given its own chronology; the books differ on the day.)

events.text: Maratha–Portuguese War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Confederacy vs Portuguese Empire / Portuguese India supported by British Empire / British East India Company
events.outcome: Status quo ante bellum
events.commanders: Shahu I, Peshwa Baji Rao I and Chimaji Appa / Maratha commanders — Portuguese Estado da Índia governors; British East India Company support by episode

events.text: Novas Conquistas
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Mysore, Maratha Empire, Kolhapur State, Sawantwadi State vs Portuguese Empire / Portuguese India with support from Soonda and Sawantwadi as listed
events.outcome: Portuguese Victory
events.commanders: Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan of Mysore; Maratha, Kolhapur and Sawantwadi chiefs by phase — Portuguese governors of Goa / Estado da Índia; Soonda and Sawantwadi allies by phase

events.text: Battle of Shirol: Shahu's forces rout the army of Sambhaji II of Kolhapur in March 1730. The Nizam had just been beaten, and Sambhaji had no ally left, so the defeat led to the Treaty of Warna.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Kolhapur
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Kolhapur army routed
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 231: 'After the defeat of the Nizam, the Kolhapur prince was isolated; his army was routed at Shirole in March, 1730; after negotiations and a personal meeting of the two cousins, the treaty of Warna was concluded in April, 1731.'

events.text: Battle of Dabhoi: The Battle of Dabhoi was fought on 28 April 1731, and it was a major confrontation between the Trimbak Rao Dabhade and Baji Rao I due to political interference of the Peshwas.
events.belligerents: Trimbakrao's Maratha faction vs Bajirao's Maratha faction
events.outcome: Bajirao I's victory
