events.commanders: Trimbak Rao Dabhade, Udaji Pawar, Maloji Pawar — Peshwa Bajirao I, Chimaji Appa, Pilaji Jadhavrao
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 818: '1731, April 1 Armies led by Trimbak Rao Dabhade Senapati and the Peshwa clash against each other at Dabhoi and the army led by the Senapati is defeated and he is slain'. HCIP gives 1 April; the row's text, following Wikipedia, gives 28 April 1731.

events.text: Battle of Thikriwala: The Battle of Thikriwala, also known as the Battle of Barnala, was a battle involving Ala Singh and allied Sikh forces against a confederacy of neighbouring Muslim Rajputs.
events.belligerents: Patiala State, Dal Khalsa vs Muslim Rajput Alliance, Mughal Faujdari
events.outcome: Victory of Ala Singh and Dal Khalsa
events.commanders: Ala Singh, Nawab Kapur Singh, Baba Darbara Singh — Rai Kalha of Rai Kot, Asad Ali Khan, Jamal Khan of Malerkotla
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Chhatrasal Bundela dies — At Panna, aged eighty-two; the founder of Bundela independence who called in Baji Rao against the Mughals and left him a third of his kingdom.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 817: '1731, December 14 Death of Chhatrasal Bundela at Panna at the age of 82 (p. 140).'

events.text: The Treaty of Warna: Shahu and Sambhaji II divide the Maratha kingdom on 13 April 1731. The land from the Warna south to the Tungabhadra goes to Kolhapur, which becomes a separate principality.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 71: 'the treaty of Warna was concluded on 13 April, 1731. The territory held by Shambhuji was recognised as his State'; p. 232: 'Kolhapur remained an integral part of the Maratha empire until the treaty of Warna (in 1731) formed it into an independent principality.'

events.text: Pilaji Gaekwad dies — founder of the Gaekwad house of Baroda, murdered at Dakor on the orders of Abhay Singh, the Mughal governor of Gujarat.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 131: 'Abhay Sinh managed to encompass Pilaji's murder by treacherous means at Dakor on 14th April 1732.' HCIP VIII p. 280: 'Songarh henceforth became the cradle of the Gaikwar house.'

events.text: Bajirao's Janjira campaign: from May to December 1733 the Peshwa's army besieges the Siddi island fortress of Janjira. English ships reinforce the island and the Maratha fleet holds back, so the siege is abandoned. A truce then puts the Peshwa's nominee on the Janjira masnad and confines the Siddi to a smaller territory.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Siddis of Janjira
events.outcome: Truce; the island fortress was not taken, but the Peshwa's nominee Abdur Rahman was seated on the Janjira masnad and the Siddi's territory shrank
events.commanders: Peshwa Bajirao I, Pratinidhi, Sekhoji Angre — the Siddi chiefs
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 77: 'Capt. McNeil arrived on the scene with a powerful squadron and the attack on Janjira had to be abandoned'; p. 78: 'Truce was declared and on December 1, Abdur Rahman, the Peshwa's nominee, was seated on the Janjira masnad ... The results of the campaign were not altogether unsubstantial. The Sidi was driven back to the sea, his territory dwindled'.

events.text: The Jantar Mantar of Jaipur: Jai Singh II’s observatory, the largest stone sundial in the world.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Battle of Basarke: The Battle of Basarke, also known as Battle of Basarke and Hujra Shah, was fought on 23 October 1736 between the Sikh forces led by Nawab Kapur Singh and the Mughal forces.
events.belligerents: Dal Khalsa vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory; the Buddha Dal defeated at Basarke.
events.commanders: Nawab Kapur Singh — Zakariya Khan, Lakhpat Rai, Haibat Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Charai (Charhai Kamarle, near Revas): in April 1736 Chimaji Appa destroys the army of Siddi Sat, who had desecrated the Parashuram shrine. By the treaty of 25 September 1736 the Siddi becomes a tributary of the Maratha state.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Siddis of Janjira
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Siddi Sat's force destroyed and the Siddi made tributary
events.commanders: Chimaji Appa, Manaji Angre — Siddi Sat
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 301: 'Sidi Sa'at's force was destroyed in the battle of Charhai Kamarle by Chimnaji Appa in April, 1736'; chronology p. 819: 'A treaty concluded between the Sidi chief and Chimnaji Appa ... The Sidi becomes a tributary of the Maratha State.'

events.text: Chanda Sahib takes Madurai: the Arcot Nawab's son-in-law seizes Trichinopoly from Rani Minakshi, then Madurai and Dindigul; the queen takes her own life and the Madurai Nayak line ends.
events.belligerents: Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs Madurai Nayak
events.outcome: Carnatic victory; Chanda Sahib becomes master of the Nayak kingdom and Rani Minakshi commits suicide
events.commanders: Chanda Sahib, Safdar Ali — Rani Minakshi, Bangaru Tirumala
events.source: HCIP VIII (The Maratha Supremacy) p. 312-313: 'Chanda Sahib advanced to Trichinopoly a second time in 1736, captured Madura and Dindigul and became master of the Nayak kingdom, while Rani Minakshi committed suicide in despair.' (p. 336 n. 3: the chronicles give conflicting versions of the sequence.)

events.text: Baji Rao's raid on Delhi: Peshwa Baji Rao I appears before the Mughal capital on 29 March 1737; when the defenders sally out, his commander Satvoji Jadhav lures them from their guns and routs them, and the Peshwa withdraws as suddenly as he came.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Mughal sally near Delhi routed, the Turani party discredited at court
events.commanders: Baji Rao I, Satvoji Jadhav — imperial garrison of Delhi
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 89: 'the defenders sallied out to attack the Peshwa’s troops. The Peshwa’s commander, Satvoji Jadhav, lured the Mughul force beyond the protection of its artillery and then enveloping it, completely routed it.'; chronology p. 819: '1737, March 30 Peshwa’s commander, Satvoji Jadhav, routs the Mughul army near Delhi'

events.text: Battle of Delhi (1737): Bajirao I raids to the gates of Delhi. On 30 March his commander Satvoji Jadhav draws the Mughal force away from its guns and routes it, and the Peshwa then withdraws.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Mughal sortie routed outside Delhi
events.commanders: Peshwa Bajirao I, Satvoji Jadhav — Mughal nobles of the capital
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 89: 'The Peshwa's commander, Satvoji Jadhav, lured the Mughul force beyond the protection of its artillery and then enveloping it, completely routed it'; chronology p. 819: '1737, March 30 Peshwa's commander, Satvoji Jadhav, routs the Mughul army near Delhi.'

events.text: Battle of Bhopal: Bajirao I's Marathas surround and starve the Nizam-ul-Mulk's Mughal army outside Bhopal (December 1737 – January 1738); by the Treaty of Bhopal that follows, the Mughals cede Malwa to the Marathas.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 91: 'the Nizam begged for terms on 7 January, 1738, at Duraha Sarai, and signed a convention promising the Peshwa: (i) the subahdari of the province of Malwa ... (iv) promise of 50 lakhs of rupees to meet his war expenses. The victory of Bhopal marks the zenith of the Peshwa's triumphant career.'
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory — the Nizam concedes Malwa

events.text: Battle of Khyber Pass (1738): The Battle of Khyber Pass was an engagement fought on 26 November 1738 between the Afsharid Iran of Nader Shah and the Mughal vassal state of Peshawar.
events.belligerents: Afsharid Iran vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Afsharid victory
events.commanders: Nader Shah, Morteza Mirza Afshar — Subahdar Nasir Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Nadir Shah's invasion of India
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 820: '1739, February 24 Emperor Muhammad Shah is made a captive by Nadir Shah (p. 92)... 1739, March 21 Nadir Shah proclaimed sovereign of Delhi... Nadir Shah orders a general massacre of Delhi population'
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire vs Afsharid Persia
events.outcome: Afsharid victory; Muhammad Shah captured after Karnal, Delhi occupied and sacked, the Mughal treasury carried off
events.commanders: Muhammad Shah of the Mughal Empire — Nader Shah Afshar

events.text: Battle of Karnal: Nadir Shah shatters the Mughal army and goes on to sack Delhi
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 820: '1739, February 24 Emperor Muhammad Shah is made a captive by Nadir Shah (p. 92).'
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire vs Afsharid Persia
events.outcome: Afsharid victory; the Mughal army broken and Muhammad Shah made captive (24 February 1739)
events.commanders: Muhammad Shah; Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I; Saadat Khan — Nader Shah Afshar

events.text: Battle of Vasai: Chimaji Appa storms the Portuguese northern capital for the Marathas
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 96: 'Bassein capitulated on 5 May, 1739 ... The fall of Bassein marked the end of Portuguese rule in north Konkan ... The Marathas acquired besides Bassein, eight cities, twenty fortresses and the island of Salsette.' Chronology p. 819 dates the Maratha seizure of Thana and Salsette, the opening of the campaign, to March 1737.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Portuguese Empire / Portuguese India
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Chimaji Appa under Shahu I and Peshwa Baji Rao I — Portuguese commanders of Bassein/Vasai and Estado da Índia authorities

events.text: Nader Shah's Sindh expedition: The Sindh expedition was one of Nader Shah's last campaigns during his war in northern India.
events.belligerents: Persian Empire vs Kalhora dynasty
events.outcome: Afsharid victory
events.commanders: Nader Shah — Noor Mohammad Kalhoro
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Saadat Khan dies — Founder of the Awadh nawabate, by his own hand at Delhi during Nadir Shah's occupation.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 113: 'Sa‘adat Khan, an immigrant from Khorasan and originally known as Mir Muhammad Amin, was the founder of the kingdom of Awadh... But, for some undesirable transactions with Nadir, he committed suicide on 20 March, 1739.'

events.text: Sack of Delhi: Nadir Shah carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 820: '1739, March 20 Nadir Shah, the Persian invader, enters Delhi with his army (pp. 33, 93)... 1739, March 21 ... Due to a rumour, a tumult breaks out and Nadir Shah orders a general massacre of Delhi population'
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire vs Afsharid Persia
events.outcome: Afsharid victory; general massacre of Delhi's people on 21 March, the Peacock Throne and the treasury carried off
events.commanders: Muhammad Shah of the Mughal Empire — Nader Shah Afshar

events.text: Shuja-ud-din Muhammad Khan dies — Nawab of Bengal (1727–39), to whom Bihar was added; his son Sarfaraz lost the masnad to Alivardi within a year.
events.source: Books disagree on the day: HCIP VIII p. 108: 'After the death of Shuja-ud-din on 30 March, 1739'; Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 44: 'On the death of Shuja (13th March, 1739)'.

events.text: Travancore–Dutch War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Travancore vs Dutch Empire / Dutch East India Company
events.outcome: Travancore victory
events.commanders: Marthanda Varma of Travancore — Dutch East India Company commanders including Eustachius De Lannoy

events.text: Bajirao I dies — Of fever at Raverkhedi on the Narmada, 36 miles from Khargon, on campaign; remembered, in Temple's words, as 'the fighting Peshwa'.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 97: 'While encamped at Raverkhedi 36 miles from Khargon he contracted fever on 23 April; after a short illness he passed away on Monday, 28 April, 1740 ... he is remembered to this day among the Marathas as the fighting Peshwa'.

events.text: Balaji Bajirao (Nanasaheb) becomes Peshwa: Shahu appoints Bajirao I's nineteen-year-old son on 25 June 1740.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 170: 'He succeeded Baji Rao I on 25 June, 1740. He was only nineteen at the time'.

events.text: Battle of Damalcheruvu: Raghuji Bhosle's Marathas, sent by Shahu to protect Tanjore, destroy the Arcot Nawab's army in the pass on 20 May 1740; Nawab Dost Ali and his son fall, and Arcot is taken.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Nawab Dost Ali and his son Hasan Ali killed, his Diwan captured, Arcot occupied
events.commanders: Raghuji Bhosle, Fatehsinh Bhosle — Dost Ali Khan
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 253 (block 205): 'Dost Ali, his son Hasan Ali and several prominent commanders lost their lives ... This happened on 20th May 1740.' HCIP VIII p. 313: 'the defeat and death of Dost Ali in the pass of Damalcheruvu'.

events.text: Battle of Giria: Alivardi Khan seizes the masnad of Bengal
events.belligerents: Alivardi Khan vs Sarfaraz Khan
events.outcome: Alivardi Khan victory; Sarfaraz Khan killed by a chance shot, Alivardi takes the masnad of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 45: 'defeated and slew Sarafraz at the battle of Gheria (10th April, 1740), and made himself Nawab of the three provinces'; HCIP VIII p. 109: 'In a furious contest between the armies of the two parties at Gheria on 10 April, 1740, there were heavy casualties in Sarfaraz’s army and he died from a chance shot on his forehead.'

events.text: Chimaji Appa dies — Bajirao I's brother and general, the victor of Amjhera and of Bassein.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 192: 'Chimnaji Appa died at Poona on 17th December. This premature death was severely mourned by the whole nation.'

events.text: Battle of Colachel: Travancore under Marthanda Varma routs the Dutch VOC — a rare decisive Indian defeat of a European power
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Travancore vs Dutch East India Company (VOC)
events.commanders: Marthanda Varma — Eustachius De Lannoy (captured)
events.outcome: Travancore victory; many Dutchmen captured, D'Lannoy among them
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 229: 'In the famous battle fought at Colachel (10th August 1741) the forces of Marthanda Varma won a resounding victory over the Dutch ... A disaster of the first magnitude for the Dutch'

events.text: Battle of Gangwana: The battle of Gangwana was a military engagement fought between the Kingdom of Marwar and a combined army of the Jaipur Kingdom and the Mughal Empire in 1741.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Jaipur, Reinforced By, Mughal Empire vs Rathores of Bakht Singh
events.outcome: Inconclusive
events.commanders: Jai Singh Kachwaha, Gopal Singh Jadon, Ummaid Singh Sisodia — Bakht Singh Rathore
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Phulwari: Alivardi Khan routs Rustam Jang’s son-in-law Baqar Ali on the plain four miles north of Balasore on 3 March 1741 and takes Orissa from Sarfaraz’s kinsmen.
events.belligerents: Bengal (Nawab) — Alivardi Khan vs Rustam Jang (Murshid Quli II), deputy governor of Orissa
events.outcome: Alivardi Khan victory; Rustam Jang flees by sea to Masulipatam and Alivardi occupies Katak
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan — Baqar Ali, Rustam Jang
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 45: 'on 3rd March, 1741, a battle was precipitated by Rustam’s impetuous son-in-law, Baqar Ali, who ... attacked Alivardi on the plain of Fulwari (four miles north of Balesar town), but was routed after a severe fight.' HCIP VIII p. 109: Rustam Jang 'was ultimately overpowered and fled to the Deccan.'

events.text: Malwa passes to the Marathas: Jai Singh, as Mughal governor, makes Peshwa Balaji Rao deputy governor of Malwa in July 1741 and grants him its chauth and sardeshmukhi in September. With this, Malwa is cut off from the Mughal empire in law as well as in fact.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 145: 'when in July 1741 the Peshwa (Balaji Rao) was granted the deputy-governorship of Malwa. Thus, Malwa ceased to be a part of the empire ... it was finally and completely cut off from the Mughul empire.' Chronology p. 821.

events.text: Siege of Trichinopoly
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 255: 'Chanda Saheb ... delivered the place to Raghuji on 14th March (Ramnavami). It was a grand success for the Marathas ... Chanda Saheb was taken into custody.' HCIP VIII p. 313.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Thanjavur (Maratha) vs Chanda Sahib (Trichinopoly)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Chanda Sahib surrenders Trichinopoly on 14 March 1741 and is taken prisoner, and Murari Rao is left in charge
events.commanders: Raghuji Bhosle, Murari Rao Ghorpade — Chanda Sahib, Bade Sahib

events.text: Battle of Katwa (1742): The Battle of Katwa was a decisive engagement fought on 27 September 1742 between the forces of Nawab Alivardi Khan of Bengal and the Maratha general Bhaskar Pandit.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Kingdom of Nagpur
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory; Alivardi bridges the Ajay by night and surprises Bhaskar’s camp at Katwa — the Marathas flee leaving tents and baggage, and are driven beyond the Chilka lake by December 1742
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan, Zain ud-Din Ahmed Khan, Mahdi Nisar Khan — Bhaskar Ram Kolhatkar
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 58: 'The surprise was complete. The Marathas fled without waiting to ascertain the strength of the attacking force ... the Nawab’s victory was complete, the Marathas had to leave all their tents, equipment and property behind.' HCIP VIII chronology p. 821: '1742, September 27 Ali Vardi Khan raids the Maratha camp under the command of Bhaskar Ram'.

events.text: First Maratha invasion of Bengal: The First Maratha invasion of Bengal occurred in 1742, led by Bhaskar Pandit under the command of Raghuji Bhonsle, the Maratha ruler of Nagpur.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Kingdom of Nagpur
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan, Shaikh Masum Khan, Mir Khairullah Khan — Raghoji I Bhonsle, Bhaskar Pandit, Shesh Rao
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Maratha invasions of Bengal: The Maratha invasions of Bengal (1742–1751) were a series of raids by the Maratha forces in the Bengal Subah, after the successful campaign in the Carnatic region.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Raghuji Bhonsle of Nagpur) vs Bengal (Nawab)
events.commanders: Raghuji I — Alivardi Khan Balaji Baji Rao, Pilaji Jadav, Malhar Holkar
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I pp. 101–102: 'finally in May or June 1751 a peace was signed ... (2) From the Bengal revenue twelve lakhs of Rupees a year would be paid to Raghuji as chauth for that province. (3) ... The frontier of Bengal was fixed at and including the river Suvarnarekha'; p. 101: 'as a financial speculation his invasion of the eastern provinces had failed.' HCIP VIII p. 110 gives the same terms.
events.outcome: Maratha victory; by the treaty of May–June 1751 Alivardi pays twelve lakhs a year as chauth of Bengal and Orissa south of the Subarnarekha passes to Raghuji’s men — though Alivardi won the pitched battles and Sarkar judges Raghuji’s venture a financial failure

events.text: Nana Phadnavis born — minister of the Peshwas, who led the Barbhai regency and ran the Maratha state for a quarter-century.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 358: 'born on 12th February 1742 he was only 58 years and one month in age'.

events.text: Nizam-ul-Mulk recovers Trichinopoly: the Nizam marches into the Karnatak, restores order at Arcot and after six months forces Murari Rao's Maratha garrison out of Trichinopoly, ending the Maratha hold won in 1741.
events.belligerents: Hyderabad vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Hyderabad victory; Murari Rao evacuates Trichinopoly and Mughal authority is re-established in the Karnatak
events.commanders: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I — Murari Rao Ghorpade
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 313: 'He then proceeded to Trichinopoly which he contrived to secure, after six months of desultory operations.' p. 336 n. 4: 'Murar Rao, was left in charge of Trichinopoly till he was forced by Nizam-ul-Mulk to evacuate it in the latter part of 1743.'

events.text: First Carnatic War
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 317-319, 321: 'There was mutual exchange of prisoners and places taken in the war. The English got back Madras'.
events.belligerents: French India vs East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
events.outcome: Inconclusive — Aix-la-Chapelle brought a 'mutual exchange of prisoners and places'; Madras was restored to the English in August 1749
events.commanders: Anwaruddin Khan, Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I and French commanders Joseph François Dupleix / La Bourdonnais — British East India Company commanders including Stringer Lawrence; George II's Britain

events.text: The massacre at Mankara: Alivardi Khan invites Bhaskar Pandit to a peace interview near Berhampore on 31 March 1744 and has him and twenty-one Maratha generals cut down, ending the third Maratha incursion.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Kingdom of Nagpur
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory; won by treachery — Bhaskar and his generals killed at the interview and their army routed, after which Bengal had fifteen months’ peace
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan, Mir Jafar, Mustafa Khan — Bhaskar Ram Kolhatkar, Alibhai Qarawwal, Shahamat Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 66: 'an auspicious day (the second day of the Bengali new-year, 31 March, 1744) was fixed for the interview. The place selected for the meeting was the plain of Mankara ... the Nawab ... cried out, “Kill these wretched misbelievers.”'; p. 67: 'The three eastern provinces enjoyed peace and happiness for fifteen months after the death of Bhaskar.'

events.text: Battle of Bhagalpur (1745): Battle of Bhagalpur in 1745 was a military conflict between Marathas under Raghuji I of Nagpur and Nawab Alivardi Khan in the Bihar province of Bengal Subah.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Nagpur State
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan, Dost Mohammad Khan, Jaswantnagar — Raghuji Bhonsle
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Naubatpur (1745): The Battle of Naubatpur was a military confrontation during the Maratha invasions of Bengal in 1745.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Kingdom of Nagpur Afghan rebels
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan, Mir Jafar, Shamshir Khan — Raghoji I, Mahimaji Baba, Sankaraji Baba
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Madhavrao I born — the Peshwa who restored Maratha power after Panipat.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II chronology p. 463: '1745, February 16 Madhavrao born.'

events.text: Siege of Barabati (1745): The Siege of Barabati (1745) was a significant military engagement during the Maratha invasions of Bengal.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Kingdom of Nagpur
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Durlabh Ram, Mir Abdul Aziz — Raghuji I, Mir Habib
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Zakariya Khan dies — Mughal governor of Lahore for two decades, the persecutor of the Sikhs whose death let them return to Amritsar in numbers.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 73: 'Zakariya Khan died on 1st July, 1745. He was succeeded by weak-[lings]'; p. 27: 'On Zakariya Khan's death the Sikhs began visiting Amritsar in large numbers.'

events.text: Battle of Adyar (San Thome): a small French force scatters the Nawab of Arcot's army, exposing Indian armies to European tactics
events.belligerents: French India vs Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
events.outcome: French India victory; Mahfuz Khan's army broken by Paradis's small force
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 318-319: 'He sent a strong force under his eldest son Mahfuz Khan to wrest Madras from the unfaithful French ... The French fire was too hot and quick for the Muhammadans.'

events.text: French capture of Madras: La Bourdonnais bombards Fort St George, which surrenders on 21 September 1746; Dupleix then refuses the ransom and holds the town until the peace.
events.belligerents: French India vs East India Company
events.outcome: French India victory; Fort St George surrenders on 21 September 1746
events.commanders: La Bourdonnais, Dupleix — Nicholas Morse
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 318: 'The French erected batteries, and after a short bombardment received the surrender of the Fort from the English (September 21).'

events.text: Siege of Alorna: The siege of Alorna in 1746 was a military engagement that took place in India, fought by Portuguese forces under the command of the Viceroy of India, Dom Pedro Miguel de Almeida.
events.belligerents: Portuguese Empire vs Maratha Empire Sawantwadi State
events.outcome: Portuguese victory
events.commanders: Dom Pedro Miguel de Almeida Portugal e Vasconcelos Colonel Pierripont Fleet general António de Figueiredo e Utra — Gomo Saunto
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Tiracol: The Battle of Tiracol was a military engagement fought by Portuguese forces under the command of the Viceroy of India Dom Pedro Miguel de Almeida Portugal e Vasconcelos.
events.belligerents: Portuguese Empire vs Maratha Empire Sawantwadi State
events.outcome: Portuguese victory
events.commanders: Dom Pedro Miguel de Almeida Portugal e Vasconcelos Colonel Pierrepont Fleet general António de Figueiredo e Utra — Ramachandra Savant I Bhonsle
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: The Chhota Ghallughara (Small Carnage): after Sikhs killed Jaspat Rae of Eminabad, his brother Lakhpat Rae, chief minister at Lahore, with Governor Yahiya Khan hunted down and massacred large numbers of Sikhs; Kapur Singh led the survivors into Malwa.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire (Lahore: Yahiya Khan, Lakhpat Rae) vs Khalsa (Sikhs)
events.outcome: Mughal victory; the Sikh bands massacred and dispersed, survivors withdraw into Malwa
events.commanders: Yahiya Khan, Lakhpat Rae — Nawab Kapur Singh
events.source: Hari Ram Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 74: 'Lakhpat Rae vowed vengeance. With the approval of Yahiya Khan, he persecuted the Sikhs and massacred large numbers of them. The Sikhs called it Chhota Ghallughara or a small carnage. Kapur Singh led the survivors into Malwa.' (Place: the Kahnuwan marshes of Gurdaspur is tradition, not in the book; coordinates approximate.)

events.text: Travancore annexes Kayamkulam: after the Treaty of Mannar (1742) is broken, Ramayyan Dalawa takes the Kayamkulam fort and palace; the Raja flees and his kingdom is absorbed, completing Marthanda Varma's hold on the old Quilon lands.
events.belligerents: Travancore vs Kayamkulam
events.outcome: Travancore victory; Kayamkulam annexed and its Raja flees
events.commanders: Marthanda Varma, Ramayyan Dalawa — Raja of Kayamkulam
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 230: 'The Raja thereafter fled from his kingdom. The Travancore army captured the Kayamkulam fort and palace ... Immediately after the annexation of Kayamkulam (1746)'.

events.text: Ahmad Shah Abdali founds the Durrani (Afghan) Empire: after Nadir Shah's murder the Abdali contingent chose Ahmad as its leader; he crowned himself at Qandahar, took Ghazni and Kabul, and by November 1747 had seized Peshawar as his base for invading Hindustan.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 126: 'Abdali killed the leading conspirators and took possession of Qandahar, where he crowned himself with full pomp and struck coins in his own name.' p. 127: 'The Abdali now established his own rule in Peshawar, which city served as a very convenient starting point for the invasion of Hindustan.'

events.text: Battle of Rajamahal: The Battle of Rajamahal was a military engagement fought in 1747 in Jaipur, India.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Jaipur vs Kingdom of Mewar, Supporters of Madho Singh, Holkar State
events.outcome: Jaipur victory
events.commanders: Ishwari Singh, Narayandas — Jagat Singh, Madho Singh, Khanderao Holkar
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Nadir Shah is murdered — the Persian conqueror who sacked Delhi in 1739; his Afghan general Ahmad Abdali took the Afghan contingent home and made himself king.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 74: 'Nadir Shah was murdered in June, 1747. His general, Ahmad Abdali, assumed kingship of Afghanistan under the title of Ahmad Shah Durrani.' Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 125 places the camp at Kuchan.

events.text: Ali Muhammad Khan Rohilla dies — Founder of Rohilla power in Katehr (Rohilkhand), months after re-establishing himself there against Mughal rule.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 823: '1748, February All Muhammad Rohilla... returns to Rohilkhand with his followers and re-establishes himself in March/April 1748, overthrowing Mughul rule... 1748, September 15 Death of Ali Muhammad Rohilla (p. 136)'

events.text: Battle of Bagru: The Battle of Bagru was a military engagement fought between multiple Indian kingdoms in 1748 near the town of Bagru, Jaipur, India.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Jaipur, Reinforced By, Kingdom of Bharatpur vs Forces of Madho Singh, Reinforced By, Holkar Clan
events.outcome: Madho Singh and allied victory; Ishvari Singh signs peace with the Marathas.
events.commanders: Ishwari Singh, Suraj Mal — Madho Singh, Malhar Rao Holkar, Gangadhar Tatya
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Lahore (1748): The Battle of Lahore was fought between Afghan forces of the Durrani Empire under Ahmad Shah Durrani and Mughal forces under Shah Nawaz on 11 January 1748.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani, Jahan Khan — Shah Nawaz, Kaura Mal, Adina Beg Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Manupur: The Battle of Manupur took place on 11 March 1748 between the forces of the rising Durrani Empire led by Afghan Emperor Ahmad Shah Durrani and the armies of the Mughal Empire.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Mughal Empire, Kingdom of Jaipur, Malerkotla State
events.outcome: Mughal victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani, Jahan Khan, Taqi Khan Shirazi — Qamar ud-Din, Moin ul-Mulk, Safdar Jang
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Rani Sarai: The Battle of Rani Sarai, also known as the Battle of Kaladiara, fought on 16 April 1748 near Rani Sarai, eight miles west of Barh in Bihar, was a decisive engagement.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Afghan rebels (Shamshir Khan, Murad Sher Khan), with Janoji’s Marathas standing off
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory; Shamshir Khan and Murad Sher Khan killed and Bihar recovered — the Marathas watched from the flank and slipped away
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan — Janoji, Mir Habib, Shamshir Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I pp. 91–92: 'It was the 16th of April 1748. Alivardi advanced to the village of Ranisarai, eight miles west of Barh ... The Marathas could be seen on the left hand some distance behind, waiting to plunder whichever side should lose the day. Ignoring the Maratha light horse as beneath his notice and pointing to the Afghans as “There are my enemies,” the Nawab advanced'; HCIP VIII p. 110: 'The Afghans were ultimately vanquished by ‘Ali Vardi in a battle with them at Ranichak or Ranisarai, near Barh, in 1748.'

events.text: Muhammad Shah dies — At Delhi on 25 April 1748, weeks after his army's victory at Manupur; the emperor of Nadir Shah's sack, whose thirty-year reign saw the provinces break away.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 823: '1748, April 25 Death of Mughul emperor Muhammad Shah (pp. 38, 184).'

events.text: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I dies — At Burhanpur, aged seventy-seven; founder of the Hyderabad state.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 122: 'Nizam-ul-Mulk died on 21 May, 1748, at the age of seventy-seven.' (The book does not name the place; Burhanpur remains web-only.)

events.text: Siege of Amritsar (1748): The siege of Amritsar was a siege that took place in March 1748.
events.belligerents: Dal Khalsa vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Nawab Kapur Singh, Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Tara Singh Waeeyan — Salabat Khan, Nijabat Khan, Qutab-ud-Din
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Pondicherry (1748): Admiral Boscawen's fleet and army attack the French capital before the rains, but Dupleix's new works hold and the English withdraw with heavy loss.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs French India
events.outcome: French India victory; the English siege is withdrawn and Dupleix's reputation 'stood greatly enhanced'
events.commanders: Admiral Boscawen, Stringer Lawrence — Dupleix
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 319: 'the English attack could make no impression and had to be withdrawn with considerable loss through sickness and lack of caution. Dupleix's reputation stood greatly enhanced after this set-back for the English.'

events.text: Siege of Ram Rauni: The Siege of Ram Rauni was a siege of the Sikh fort of Ram Rauni at Amritsar in 1748 by Mughal forces under Mir Mannu.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire, Subah of Lahore vs Sikh Confederacy
events.outcome: Sikh victory; the Sikhs granted one-fourth of the revenue of Pargana Patti.
events.commanders: Mir Mannu, Adina Beg Khan, Sadiq Beg Khan — Jai Singh Kanhaiya, Jassa Singh Ramgarhia
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: The Dal Khalsa is formed: at the Baisakhi gathering at Amritsar on 29 March 1748 Nawab Kapur Singh organised the Sikh bands into a single army, the Dal Khalsa, under Jassa Singh Ahluwalia — the start of the misl confederacy.
events.source: Hari Ram Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 13: 'On March 29, 1748, the day of Baisakhi, all the members of the Khalsa brotherhood had gathered at Amritsar ... He named this organisation the Dal Khalsa. He placed it under the command of Jassa Singh Ahluwalia.' Also p. 17: 'The misls as members of the Dal Khalsa were organised on March 29, 1748.'

events.text: Battle of Ambur: French-backed Chanda Sahib wins the Carnatic succession
events.belligerents: French India, Chanda Sahib, Muzaffar Jang vs Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
events.outcome: French India victory; Nawab Anwar-ud-din defeated and slain, Chanda Sahib installed at Arcot (August 1749)
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 321: 'At Ambur, 50 miles to the west of Arcot, Anwar-ud-din was defeated and slain ... Chanda Sahib was formally installed as the Nawab of the Karnatak by Muzaffar Jang.'

events.text: Battle of Multan (1749): The Battle of Multan, also known as the Battle of Daurana Langana, was fought in September 1749 by Kaura Mal's Mughal forces assisted by Jassa Singh Ahluwalia's Sikhs.
events.belligerents: Kaura Mal's forces vs Shah Nawaz Khan's forces
events.outcome: Kaura Mal victory
events.commanders: Diwan Kaura Mal, Asmat Khan, Abdul Aziz Khan — Shah Nawaz Khan, Khawajah Shah, Zahad Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Chhatrapati Shahu dies — the Maratha king whose forty-year reign saw the Peshwas carry Maratha power into Hindustan; after him, real power passed to the Peshwa.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 181: 'Shahu died on 15 December, 1749 ... Ram Raja being weak and incompetent and being a puppet in the hands of Tara Bai, the power of the State gradually fell into the hands of the Peshwa.'

events.text: Second Carnatic War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: France/French East India Company, Mughal Empire, Mysore, Nawab of Arcot (Chanda Sahib), Hyderabad (Muzaffar Jang) vs Great Britain/British East India Company, Maratha Empire, Nawab of Arcot (Wallajah), Hyderabad (Nasir Jung)
events.outcome: Stalemate
events.commanders: Dupleix, Chanda Sahib and Muzaffar Jang; Mysore/French aligned commanders — Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah, Nasir Jung, Robert Clive and Stringer Lawrence; British EIC

events.text: Siege of Cuttack (1749): The Siege of Cuttack occurred in May 1749 during the Fifth Maratha invasion of Bengal, when Alivardi Khan, Nawab of Bengal, sought to reconquer Orissa.
events.belligerents: Bengal Subah vs Maratha Empire Kingdom of Nagpur
events.outcome: Bengal Subah victory; Barabati surrenders to Alivardi about the start of June 1749, but Mir Habib retakes Katak within a week of the Nawab’s leaving
events.commanders: Alivardi Khan, Dost Muhammad Khan, Mir Kazim Khan — Mir Habib, Sabaji, Sayyid Nur
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I pp. 96–97: 'He entered the city of Katak (c. 18 May), and fifteen days later received the surrender of Barabati. Thus, the reconquest of Orissa was complete ... Six or seven days after Alivardi had marched out of Katak, Mir Habib reappeared before that town ... Thus, Alivardi’s work was undone within a week.'

events.text: Tipu Sultan is born — At Devanahalli, Haidar Ali’s son.
events.source: C. Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 561-562 n. (block 492): 'Kirmani dates it November 19, 1749 ... Wilks in 1753 ... Kirkpatrick ... 1747, while the Haid. Nam. would refer it to 1752 ... Kirmani's date is adopted in this work as the more specific and reliable.' Conventional modern date 20 Nov 1750 (milestone M492); the row's 1751 has no book behind it.

events.text: Battle of Ram Chatauni: the wazir Safdar Jang's huge army, invading the Bangash country, is broken by Ahmad Khan Bangash's Afghans north of Etah; Safdar Jang is wounded and disgraced and the Afghans overrun Oudh and besiege Allahabad.
events.belligerents: Farrukhabad (Bangash) vs Mughal Empire, Awadh (wazir Safdar Jang), Bharatpur (Suraj Mal)
events.outcome: Farrukhabad (Bangash) victory; Safdar Jang's army routed after his wings had first beaten the Afridi division
events.commanders: Ahmad Khan Bangash, Rustam Khan Afridi (killed) — Safdar Jang, Suraj Mal, Ismail Beg Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 246-247: '§ 6. Safdar Jang defeated at Ram Chatauni. At three hours after sunrise, on the 18th of September 1750, the wazir’s army advanced upon the enemy'; HCIP VIII p. 113 and chronology p. 824: '1750, September 13 Safdar Jang is defeated by the Afghans at Ram Chatauni' (Sarkar himself gives 13 Sep. on p. 253 and 18 Sep. on p. 246)

events.text: Fall of Gingee and death of Nasir Jang: Bussy and d'Auteuil storm Gingee by night; in December the French advance into Nasir Jang's camp, the Nizam is shot dead by one of the Pathan Nawabs, and the captive Muzaffar Jang is raised to the throne — the height of Dupleix's power.
events.belligerents: French India, Muzaffar Jang vs Hyderabad (Nasir Jang)
events.outcome: French India victory; Nasir Jang killed and Muzaffar Jang made Subahdar (December 1750)
events.commanders: Bussy, d'Auteuil — Nasir Jang
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 322: 'their assault and capture of the place in the course of a night attack greatly raised their fame ... Nasir Jang was shot dead through the heart by one of the Nawabs and Muzaffar Jang was released from prison and promptly elevated to the throne ... (December, 1750).'

events.text: Ishwari Singh of Jaipur kills himself: with Malhar Holkar's army a day's march away, Sawai Jai Singh's heir took poison on the night of 12 December 1750; the Marathas seated his brother Madho Singh, and on 10 January 1751 the citizens of Jaipur rose and massacred some 1,500 Maratha visitors.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 187: 'It was the 12th of December, 1750 ... At midnight he swallowed the poison and caused the cobra to sting him.' p. 189: 'Some fifteen hundred Marathas were slain and about a thousand wounded.' Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 252: 'Ishwari Singh ... escaped their rising pressure by committing suicide (December 1750). The Marathas occupied the city of Jaipur and placed Madho Singh on the gadi.'

events.text: The Sangola settlement: in October 1750 Peshwa Balaji Rao makes an agreement with the new Chhatrapati, Ramraja, at Sangola that fixes the powers of the ministers and sardars. In November Tarabai confines Ramraja, and from then on power at Satara rests with the Peshwa.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 182: 'the Peshwa arrived at a settlement at Sangola in October, 1750 with Ram Raja ... On 24 November, 1750, Ram Raja was put in confinement by his grand-mother Tara Bai. He thus ceased to be an active or directive factor'; chronology p. 824.

events.text: The Trippadidanam: on 3 January 1750 Marthanda Varma dedicates the enlarged kingdom of Travancore to Sri Padmanabha; thereafter its kings rule as the god's servants (Padmanabhadasas).
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 232-233: 'the dedication (Trippatidanam) of the newly expanded kingdom of Travancore to his tutelary deity, Sri Padmanabha ... The event took place on Wednesday, January 3, 1750'.

events.text: Battle of Arnee: The Battle of Arnee occurred on 3 December 1751 during the Second Carnatic War.
events.belligerents: Great Britain, British East India Company, Maratha Empire vs Kingdom of France, Drapeau_du_régiment_de_la_Compagnie_des_Indes_en_1756.svg French East India Company, Nawab of Arcot (Chanda Sahib)
events.outcome: British-Maratha victory
events.commanders: Robert Clive, Murari Rao — Chanda Sahib, Raza Sahib
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of the Venna (Damaji Gaekwad's revolt): answering Tarabai's call, Damaji Gaekwad marches on Satara. On 15 March 1751 the Peshwa's troops defeat him on the Venna and trap his force. On 30 April the Peshwa plunders his camp and imprisons him, and Damaji later gives up half of Gujarat.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Peshwa Balaji Rao) vs Damaji Gaekwad and Tarabai's party
events.outcome: Peshwa victory; Damaji Gaekwad defeated, confined and made to cede half his Gujarat holdings
events.commanders: Peshwa Balaji Bajirao — Damaji Gaekwad
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 283: 'The Peshwa's forces challenged the Gaikwar on the Venya river near Satara, defeated him and trapped his force in Satara on 15 March, 1751 ... the Peshwa plundered his camp on 30 April and confined Damaji Gaikwar'. (An earlier action at Bahadurpura in Khandesh, 18 Feb 1751, went Damaji's way: 'Brushing aside the Peshwa's troops'.)

events.text: Orissa passes to the Marathas: by Alivardi’s treaty of May–June 1751, Mir Habib governs Orissa south of the Subarnarekha for Raghuji Bhonsle’s army and Bengal pays twelve lakhs a year as chauth; after Mir Habib’s murder (24 August 1752) the Bhonsles rule Orissa outright.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I pp. 101–104: 'Mir Habib would now become a servant of Alivardi and act as naib-nazim (deputy governor) of Orissa on his behalf ... It is a mistake to say that Alivardi ceded Orissa to the Marathas ... the weakness of Alivardi’s successors ... enabled the Marathas to turn their fiscal right over Orissa into full political sovereignty'; HCIP VIII p. 110 and chronology p. 824 ('ceding Orissa to the Marathas and agreeing to pay Rs. 12 lakhs as chauth').
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Raghuji Bhonsle of Nagpur) vs Bengal (Nawab)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Orissa’s revenue and then its government pass to Nagpur. HCIP VIII (chronology p. 824) calls it 'ceding Orissa'; Sarkar I p. 104 says 'It is a mistake to say that Alivardi ceded Orissa' — it was a revenue assignment turned into rule after 1752

events.text: Siege of Arcot: The siege of Arcot took place at Arcot, India, and involved forces of the British East India Company led by Robert Clive allied with Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs French India, Chanda Sahib
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Raza Sahib raises the 50-day siege on 24 November 1751
events.commanders: Robert Clive, Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah, Murari Rao — Joseph François Dupleix, Charles Godeheu, Chanda Sahib
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 324: 'The subsequent siege of Arcot by Raza Sahib, assisted by French troops lasted 50 days ... Murar Rao definitely went over to the side of the English. On the 24th of November the enemy raised the siege and retreated'.

events.text: Siege of Fatehgarh and the rout of the Rohillas: Safdar Jang brings in Jayappa Sindhia and Malhar Holkar; on 18 April 1751 the Marathas crush Sadullah Khan's Rohilla relief army across the Ganges, Ahmad Bangash abandons Fatehgarh, and the Marathas loot the Bangash country.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Awadh (Safdar Jang), Bharatpur vs Farrukhabad (Bangash), Rohilkhand (Rohillas)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; over ten thousand Afghans slain or wounded, Fatehgarh occupied on 19 April, the Bangash and Rohilla chiefs driven to the foothills
events.commanders: Malhar Rao Holkar, Jayappa Sindhia, Safdar Jang, Suraj Mal — Ahmad Khan Bangash, Sadullah Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 255-256: 'After a great battle defeat fell in the end on the Afghans. Sadullah and Mahmud fled away with their bare lives... over ten thousand of their men were slain or wounded... In the morning (19th April), the Marathas occupied Fatehgarh'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 824: 'The combined armies of Mughuls and the Marathas inflict severe defeats on the Rohillas'

events.text: Battle of Chingleput: The Battle of Chingleput was a short siege in early 1752, during the Second Carnatic War.
events.belligerents: British East India Company, Nawab of Arcot vs French East India Company
events.outcome: British–Arcot victory
events.commanders: Robert Clive — Unknown
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Kaveripak: Clive, back from Arcot, beats the French and Raza Sahib's force that had been ravaging the country round Madras.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs French India, Chanda Sahib
events.outcome: East India Company victory
events.commanders: Robert Clive — Raza Sahib and French officers
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 324: 'In February 1752, Clive won the victory of Kaveripauk.'

events.text: Battle of Lahore (1752): The Battle of Lahore was battle which took place between the invading Ahmed Shah Abdali and Mir Mannu, the Mughal governor of Punjab in 1752.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Afghan victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani — Ahmad Shah Bahadur, Moin-ul-Mulk, Kaura Mal
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Chanda Sahib dies — the Nawayat adventurer who took Madurai, was Dupleix's Nawab of Arcot from 1749, and was killed after surrendering to the Tanjore general at Srirangam.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 325: 'Ultimately Chanda Sahib was killed, it is said, at the instigation of Muhammad Ali (June 1752).'

events.text: Durrani conquest of Kashmir & Punjab: Ahmad Shah Abdali takes them from the Mughals
events.source: Jadunath Sarkar
events.belligerents: Durrani (Afghan) Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory — Punjab and Kashmir ceded

events.text: Naval Battle of Calicut
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Portuguese Empire / Portuguese India
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Maratha naval forces, likely Angre-family/Maratha commanders; exact leader uncertain — Portuguese Estado da Índia naval commanders

events.text: Partition of Gujarat: Damaji Gaekwad gives the Peshwa half of Gujarat, pays arrears and tribute, and becomes the Peshwa's subordinate tributary.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 283: 'From this date, the Gaikwar became a subordinate tributary of the Peshwa ... The partition of Gujarat took place in 1752.' Chronology p. 824: '1752, March Gujarat partitioned between the Peshwa and Damaji Gaikwar.'

events.text: Surrender at Srirangam and death of Chanda Sahib: Law's French army, cut off on Srirangam island by Lawrence and Clive, surrenders; Chanda Sahib gives himself up to the Tanjore general and is killed, ending the French siege of Trichinopoly.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab), Mysore, Thanjavur (Maratha) vs French India, Chanda Sahib
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the French force surrenders and Chanda Sahib is put to death (June 1752)
events.commanders: Stringer Lawrence, Robert Clive, Muhammad Ali — Jacques Law, Chanda Sahib
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 325: 'Ultimately Chanda Sahib was killed, it is said, at the instigation of Muhammad Ali (June 1752). Thus ended the French siege of Trichinopoly. No such blow had fallen on the French since they entered the field of Indian politics.'

events.text: The Treaty of Bhalki: Salabat Jang's Diwan Ramdas, backed by Bussy, invades Maratha territory in 1751 and fails. In November 1752 the Nizam makes peace with Peshwa Balaji Rao at Bhalki and cedes western Berar.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 182: 'Ramdas was not successful and concluded a treaty at Shingwa ... Then Salabat Jang made peace with the Peshwa at Bhalki in November, 1752.' Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 325: 'cemented by a formal exchange of visits ... on 24th November 1752. The main part of this treaty of Bhalki was the cession of the whole western half of Berar'.

events.text: Battle of Kandarpi Ghat: The Battle of Kandarpi Ghat occurred between the Nawab of Bengal and Raj Darbhanga in October 1753.
events.belligerents: Raj Darbhanga (Khandwala dynasty) vs Bengal (Nawab)
events.outcome: Khandwala victory
events.commanders: Narendra Singh, Mitrajit Singh, Umrao — Bhikhari Mahtha, Zainuddin Khan, Ram Narayan Singh
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Seringham: The Battle of Seringham was fought on the island of Srirangam by 1,000 troops of the British East India Company commanded by Stringer Lawrence.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Great Britain East India Company Maratha Empire Thanjavur Marathas vs France French East India Company Nawab of Arcot
events.outcome: British–Maratha victory
events.commanders: Stringer Lawrence, Robert Clive, Captain Dalton — Law, d'Auteil, Chanda Sahib
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of the Golden Rock: Lawrence checks the French–Mysore alliance at Trichinopoly
events.belligerents: East India Company, Thanjavur (Maratha) vs French India, Mysore
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Lawrence's surprise attack on the rock position throws the French and Mysoreans into panic
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 328: 'The latter however launched an unexpected attack against a strong rock position which struck the French with panic and created dissensions between them and their allies.'

events.text: Muin-ul-Mulk (Mir Mannu) dies — Mughal viceroy of the Punjab from 1748 who beat Abdali at Manupur and then held Lahore for him; after him the province fell into anarchy.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 17: 'He died on November 3, 1753. Then Panjab plunged into anarchy ... In three years from 1753 to 1756 nine changes took place in the office of the governor.'

events.text: Nawab Kapur Singh dies — leader of the Sikhs through the persecutions and founder of the Dal Khalsa in 1748.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 76: 'He died in October, 1753. His tomb stands near the temple of Baba [Atal] ...' and '[he] was the founder of the Dal Khalsa in 1748.'

events.text: Siege of Ahmedabad (1753): Raghunathrao and Damaji Gaekwad besiege Ahmedabad, capital of Gujarat's Muslim rulers for three centuries, and Jawan Mard Khan Babi surrenders it on 20 March 1753.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Jawan Mard Khan Babi surrendered the city and retired to Radhanpur
events.commanders: Raghunathrao, Damaji Gaekwad — Jawan Mard Khan Babi
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 284: 'The capital of Musalman kings for over three centuries was stoutly defended by Jawan Mard Khan Babi. After a long investment Babi surrendered the capital city on 20 March and retired to his jagir at Radhanpur.' Chronology p. 825 dates it 1753, March 20.

events.text: The Delhi civil war of 1753: the dismissed wazir Safdar Jang, with Suraj Mal's Jats, besieges the capital from March to November against Emperor Ahmad Shah, Imad-ul-Mulk and Najib Khan; his grand assault fails and he withdraws to Awadh.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire (Ahmad Shah, Imad-ul-Mulk, Najib Khan's Rohillas, Maratha contingent) vs Awadh (Safdar Jang), Bharatpur (Suraj Mal)
events.outcome: Mughal Empire victory; Safdar Jang's attacks repulsed and he lost the wazirship and retired to Awadh, though Sarkar notes the imperialists 'gained no decisive victory'
events.commanders: Imad-ul-Mulk, Najib Khan — Safdar Jang, Suraj Mal, Rajendragiri Gosain (killed)
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 310-311: '§ 19. Grand battle of 29 September... He then took horse, charged and routed the Jats... But though the imperialists repulsed every attack of Safdar Jang and steadily pushed him further away from the capital, they gained no decisive victory.'; HCIP VIII p. 113-114: 'a civil war between the emperor and Safdar Jang from March 1753 and ultimately he departed for Awadh in November 1753'

events.text: The Treaty of Mavelikkara: ratifying the accord of 1748, the Dutch renounce interference in Kerala's quarrels, abandon their other princely allies and agree to live at peace with Travancore.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 230: 'by the treaty of 1748, ratified later by the treaty of Mavelikkara (1753), the Dutch had undertaken to follow a strict policy of non-involvement in native disputes ... The treaty was a tremendous gain to Marthanda Varma'.

events.text: Ahmad Shah deposed; Alamgir II enthroned: on 2 June 1754 the new wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, backed by Malhar Holkar, brings Aziz-ud-din out of the princes' prison and crowns him Alamgir II, and has Ahmad Shah arrested (he was later blinded).
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 338: '§ 18. Fall of Emperor Ahmad Shah... they entered the Diwan-i-am, where this prince was seated on the throne... and he was proclaimed Padishah Alamgir II. The new Emperor immediately ordered his predecessor to be brought under arrest.'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 825: '1754, June 2 Imad-ul-Mulk, with the help of the Marathas, deposes Mughul emperor Ahmad Shah'

events.text: Battle of Ambalapuzha: the northern confederacy under Cochin, backing the dispossessed Rajas of Ambalapuzha, Tekkumkur and Vadakkumkur, is routed by Travancore; the Cochin commander Idikkela Menon is executed and Cochin sues for peace.
events.belligerents: Travancore vs Cochin
events.outcome: Travancore victory; the Cochin army routed, its commander executed, Karappuram conquered
events.commanders: Prince Rama Varma, Ramayyan Dalawa, D'Lannoy — Palliyil Idikkela Menon
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 231: 'In a decisive battle that ensued the Cochin forces were routed and put to flight ... Idikkela Menon, the Commander of the Cochin forces, was captured and executed ... The Cochin Raja sued for peace.' (Menon's text gives both 'end of 1756' and '3rd January 1754'; p. 240 dates the battle 1754.)

events.text: Battle of Kumher: The Battle of Kumher was a conflict between the Kingdom of Bharatpur, led by Maharaja Suraj Mal, and the Mughal Empire, supported by its allies, including the Marathas.
events.belligerents: Bharatpur vs Maratha Empire, Mughal Empire (Imad-ul-Mulk), Jaipur
events.outcome: Bharatpur victory; Kumher held for four months (Jan.–May 1754), Khande Rao Holkar killed, the besiegers withdrew on the promise of a 30-lakh indemnity
events.commanders: Maharaja Suraj Mal — Imad-ul-Mulk, Amir Bakshi, Har Govind Natani
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 324-325: 'Khande Rao having made covered lanes approached the walls... the fort opened fire and he was killed by a zamburak shot'; II p. 437: 'After four months (Jan.-May, 1754) the fort remained untaken, and the besiegers were glad to go away on receiving promise of an indemnity of 30 lakhs of Rupees.'

events.text: Battle of Merta (1754): Jayappa Sindhia, pursuing Bijay Singh of Marwar from Ajmer, beat the Rathors at Merta on 15 September 1754 and drove him into Nagaur, which he then besieged.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Jayappa Sindhia) vs Jodhpur (Marwar)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Bijay Singh falls back to Nagaur and is besieged
events.commanders: Jayappa Sindhia — Bijay Singh
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 383: 'Jayappa immediately followed Bijay Sinh to Merta in August and in a stiff action inflicted a severe defeat on the Rathors on 15th September 1754. Thereupon Bijay Sinh fell back still further north to Nagore.'

events.text: Safdar Jang dies — Nawab of Awadh and former Mughal wazir, beaten at Ram Chatauni and in the Delhi civil war; his son Shuja-ud-Daula succeeds.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 114: 'Safdar Jang died in October 1754 and his son Shuja-ud-daulah became subahdar of Awadh.'

events.text: Seven Years' War / Third Carnatic War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: France and allies including French East India Company; Mughal Empire from 1757 vs Great Britain and allies including British East India Company; Portugal from 1761
events.outcome: Status quo ante in Europe; colonial transfers
events.commanders: French commanders Thomas Arthur de Lally and Bussy; French East India Company; allied Indian rulers by phase — British commanders Eyre Coote, Robert Clive and EIC leaders; Portugal as later ally

events.text: The surprise at Sikandrabad: Malhar Holkar's light horse fall on Emperor Ahmad Shah's camp in the Doab on the night of 25–26 May 1754; the emperor flees to Delhi leaving his mother and harem in Maratha hands, and within a week Imad-ul-Mulk deposes him.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Malhar Rao Holkar), with Imad-ul-Mulk vs Mughal Empire (Emperor Ahmad Shah)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the imperial camp dispersed in panic and the royal ladies captured
events.commanders: Malhar Rao Holkar — Emperor Ahmad Shah, wazir Intizam-ud-daulah
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 334: '§ 11. Malhar surprises imperial camp at Sikandrabad, 26 May 1754. But in the night between, spies brought the news that 20,000 Maratha light horse under Malhar had arrived within 24 miles of the camp.'; Sarkar II p. 437 dates Holkar's raid 25 May

events.text: Fall of Suvarnadurg: under a treaty of 19 March 1755, the Peshwa and the Bombay Company attack Tulaji Angre, and Suvarnadurg and three other forts fall by 7 April. The Peshwa's land army then overruns Anjanwel, Govalkot and Ratnagiri.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Maratha Empire (Peshwa) vs Tulaji Angre (Kolaba Angres)
events.outcome: East India Company and Maratha victory; Suvarnadurg and three castles taken
events.commanders: Commodore William James, Ramaji Mahadeo — Tulaji Angre
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 305: 'A treaty was concluded on 19 March, 1755 ... By 7 April, 1755, Suvarnadurg and three other castles to the north had fallen to the joint attack'; p. 183: 'It is to the eternal discredit of Balaji that he destroyed the naval power of Tulaji Angria with the help of the British.'

events.text: Jayappa Sindhia is assassinated — the Sindhia chief besieging Bijay Singh in Nagaur was stabbed in his camp by men who came in with the Jodhpur envoys; the murder soured Maratha–Rathor relations for a generation.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 384: 'On the morning of Friday 25th July, 1755, the Jodhpur Vakil ... visited Jayappa's camp ... Suddenly two beggars ... ran at Jayappa ... and stabbed him, wounding him mortally, so that in an hour he died.' HCIP VIII chronology p. 826: '1755, July 25 Jayappa Sindia assassinated.'

events.text: Raghuji Bhonsle I dies — founder of the Bhonsle kingdom of Nagpur, which reached from Berar to Orissa.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 244: 'Raghuji died on 14 February, 1755 at the age of 60'; p. 243: 'a kingdom extending from Berar in the west to Orissa in the east'.

events.text: The Treaty of Pondicherry (Godeheu's treaty): Dupleix's successor and the Madras Governor agree that both Companies renounce Indian offices and stop fighting for their Nawabs; the truce is never ratified and the Seven Years' War overtakes it.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 329: 'The provisional treaty of January 1755 between himself and the English Governor declared that both the Companies should renounce all Indian governments and dignities and not interfere in the disputes of the Indian powers'.

events.text: Alivardi Khan dies — Nawab of Bengal from 1740, who held off ten years of Maratha raids and the Afghan revolts, and left the masnad to his grandson Siraj-ud-daulah.
events.source: Books disagree on the day: HCIP VIII p. 111: ''Ali Vardi died on 10 April, [1756] and was succeeded as the subahdar of Bengal by his favourite grandson and heir-designate Siraj-ud-daulah' (the scan reads '1750', evidently for 1756); HCIP VIII chronology p. 826: '1756, April 21 Death of Ali Vardi Khan, Subahdar of Bengal.'

events.text: Badan Singh dies — At Dig, the founder of the Bharatpur Jat state, long blind and a figurehead while Suraj Mal ruled for him.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 433: 'Badan Singh died at Dig on [?]th June 1756; but for many years before it he was a quiescent figure, stationary at his capital... The policy of his State in war and diplomacy was shaped and its campaigns were led by' Suraj Mal (day of month illegible in the scan)

events.text: Battle of Manihari: Siraj-ud-daulah marches on Purnea and kills his cousin and rival Shaukat Jang, whom Mir Ja‘far had egged on to claim the masnad.
events.belligerents: Bengal (Nawab) — Siraj-ud-daulah vs Shaukat Jang, Nawab of Purnea
events.outcome: Siraj-ud-daulah victory; Shaukat Jang killed on 16 October 1756
events.commanders: Siraj-ud-daulah — Shaukat Jang
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 112: 'By marching from Calcutta towards Purnea, on 24 September, 1756, Siraj-ud-daulah defeated and killed him in a battle at Manihari on 16 October, 1756.' (also chronology p. 826)

events.text: Battle of Vijaydurg: The Battle of Vijaydurg was fought between Tulaji Angre, the Admiral of the Maratha Navy, and the combined forces of the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Maratha Empire (Peshwa) vs Tulaji Angre (Kolaba Angres)
events.outcome: East India Company and Maratha victory; Tulaji Angre surrendered to the Peshwa's commander on 12 February 1756 and the English occupied Vijaydurg, restoring it to the Peshwa in October for Bankot
events.commanders: Charles Watson, Sir William James, Robert Clive — Tulaji Angre
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 826: '1756, February 12 Tulaji Angria surrenders to the Maratha commander when attacked by the joint forces of the Marathas and the English'; p. 306: 'Vijayadurg was restored to the Peshwa on 12 October, 1756. In lieu of it, the English obtained Bankot'; p. 183: 'he destroyed the naval power of Tulaji Angria with the help of the British.'

events.text: Cattle War: The Cattle War, also commonly referred to as the Perumal War or the Perumal Naik-War, was a colonial conflict between the Danish East India Company and the Thanjavur Marathas.
events.belligerents: Danish India, French India vs Thanjavur
events.outcome: Thanjavurian victory
events.commanders: Hans Georg Krog, Castonier, Hesselberg — Pratap Singh, Perumal Naik, Manosiappa
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

HCIP VIII p. 112: 'On 4 June, 1756, the factory of the English at Kasimbazar was stormed by the Nawab’s soldiers, and starting for Calcutta on 5 June, the Nawab captured Calcutta on 20 June ... But Holwell’s story of the ‘Black Hole’ has been proved by modern researches to be untrue.' Holwell’s figure of 123 is from Holwell’s narrative (web); books disagree.
events.text: The fall of Calcutta and the 'Black Hole': Siraj-ud-daula storms the Kasimbazar factory (4 June) and takes Fort William (20 June 1756). Holwell said 123 prisoners died overnight in the fort’s guardroom; HCIP rejects the story as untrue. Plassey followed within the year.
Battle of Bobbili: The Battle of Bobbili, comprising the attack on the fort of Bobbili on 24 January 1757, was a significant event in the princely state of Vizianagaram.
events.belligerents: French India, Vizianagaram vs Bobbili
events.outcome: French India victory; Bussy storms Bobbili and puts the defenders to the sword
events.commanders: Marquis de Bussy-Castelnau, Pusapati Vijayarama Gajapati Raju I — Gopala Krishnarayudu, Tandra Paparayudu, Devulapalli Peddanna
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 332: 'except at Bobbili where, at the instigation of the crafty Vijayarama Raju of Vijayanagaram, he put to the sword all the brave defenders.'

events.text: Battle of Chaumuha and the sack of Mathura: sent by Ahmad Shah Abdali to put the Jat country 'to the edge of the sword', Jahan Khan and Najib break Jawahir Singh's stand at Chaumuha eight miles north of Mathura (28 February 1757) and massacre the pilgrims of Mathura, Vrindavan and Gokul.
events.belligerents: Durrani (Afghan) Empire, Rohilkhand (Rohillas) vs Bharatpur
events.outcome: Durrani victory; after nine hours' fighting the Jat army broke and Mathura was sacked
events.commanders: Jahan Khan, Najib Khan — Jawahir Singh
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 117-118: 'Outside the village of Chaumuha, eight miles north of Mathura, Jawahir Singh barred the invader’s path with less than 10,000 men and offered a desperate resistance (28th February.) From sunrise the battle raged for nine hours... and the broken remnant of the Jat army took the road to their homes.'

events.text: Battle of Delhi (1757): The Battle of Delhi in 1757, also referred to as the Second Battle of Delhi, was fought on 11 August 1757 by the Maratha Confederacy under the command of Raghunath Rao.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Rohilkhand (Rohillas) — Najib Khan
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Raghunath Rao forced Najib to evacuate Delhi, Najib making peace on 9 September
events.commanders: Raghunathrao, Malharrao Holkar, Manaji Paygude — Najib-ud-Daula, Mian Qutb Shah, Mulla Aman Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 827: '1757, August 11 Raghunath Rao, the Maratha general, attacks Delhi and captures it (p. 188)... 1757, September 9 Najib Khan Rohilla makes peace with the Marathas (p. 188).'; Sarkar II contents: 'Raghunath attacks Delhi, 146—Najib evacuates Delhi, 151'

events.text: Battle of Mahilpur (1757): The Battle of Mahilpur was fought between the combined forces of Adina Beg Khan and Sikh Misls and the Durrani Empire in December 1757.
events.belligerents: Sikh Misls, Adina Beg vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh-Adina Beg victory
events.commanders: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Baghel Singh, Vadbhag Singh Sodhi — Murad Khan, Buland Khan, Sarfraz Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Narela (1757): The Battle of Narela took place on 16 January 1757, at Narela, on the outskirts of Delhi, between the Maratha Army led by Antaji Mankeshwar and an army of Ahmad Shah Abdali.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Sardar Jahan Khan — Antaji Mankeshwar
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Plassey: Clive defeats Siraj-ud-Daulah through betrayal, seizing Bengal for the Company
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 339: 'On 23 June, 1757, took place one of the decisive events in world history. Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah ... found himself deserted in the field of battle by the general under whom was ranged the major part of his forces ... From the military point of view the battle of Plassey was an insignificant engagement. The English gathered an undeserved victory on account of the Nawab’s order of recall to his attacking troops ... After Plassey, the 24 Parganas were added to their Zamindari.'
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Bengal (Nawab), with French gunners
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Siraj-ud-daulah, deserted by Mir Ja‘far’s divisions and recalling his attacking troops, flees — militarily 'an insignificant engagement', politically a revolution that made Mir Ja‘far Nawab and gave the Company the 24 Parganas
events.commanders: Robert Clive and East India Company forces — Siraj ud-Daulah of Bengal; Mir Jafar faction; French officer St. Frais

events.text: Battle of Sindkhed: the Peshwa's army under Dattaji Scindia besieges Ramchandra Jadhav in Sindkhed. After four days of fighting (12–16 December 1757), Nizam Ali's attempt to break the siege fails, and on 17 December he asks for terms. Peace is made at Sakharkherda.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Nizam Ali acknowledged defeat and sued for terms
events.commanders: Vishwasrao, Dattaji and Jankoji Scindia — Nizam Ali, Ibrahim Khan Gardi, Ramchandra Jadhav
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 334: 'A fierce battle was fought continuously for four days at the gate of Sindkhed ... Victory remained with the Marathas ... On 17th December Nizam Ali acknowledging defeat sent Vithal Sundar to the Maratha camp begging for terms.' HCIP VIII p. 182: 'A peace was made at Sakharkharda'.

events.text: Capture of Chandernagore: Clive and Admiral Watson take the French settlement on the Hooghly on 23 March 1757, three months before Plassey, removing the French from Bengal.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs French India
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Fort d’Orléans surrenders and Chandernagore is taken
events.commanders: Robert Clive, Charles Watson — Pierre Renault
events.source: web-only; library silent (HCIP VIII and Sarkar do not narrate it). Famous and uncontested (23 March 1757); it matters because it removed the French from Bengal before Plassey.

events.text: Maratha conquest of North-west India
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory — Delhi and Sirhind taken
events.commanders: Raghunath Rao, Malhar Rao Holkar and Dattaji/Jankoji Scindia under Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao — Ahmad Shah Durrani and Timur Shah Durrani

events.text: Maratha invasion of Mysore (1757): the Peshwa's army besieges Srirangapatna; Nanjaraj promises 32 lakhs, pays six and pledges fifteen taluks — the crisis that brings Haidar Ali to command of the field army.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mysore
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Mysore promises 32 lakhs and hands over fifteen taluks as security
events.commanders: Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao — Karachuri Nanjaraj
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 453: 'The Marathas again invaded in 1757 and Nanjaraj agreed to pay them 32 lakhs, but could pay only six, and for the payment of the balance handed over fifteen taluks as security.'

events.text: Mysore invasion of Calicut: The Mysore invasion of Calicut was the result of the Calicut's attack on Palghat in 1756–1757.
events.belligerents: Mysore, Palghat (Palakkad Rajas) vs Calicut (Zamorin)
events.outcome: Mysore victory; the Zamorin restores his Palghat conquests and pays an indemnity of 12 lakhs
events.commanders: Hyder Ali, Makhdoom Ali — Zamorin Raja
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 243: 'The prompt and effective action taken by the combined forces of Mysore and Palghat put the Calicut forces to flight. The Zamorin was also forced to restore his Palghat conquests and to pay a war indemnity of 12 lakhs of rupees to Mysore.'

events.text: Siraj-ud-daulah dies — The last independent Nawab of Bengal, caught after Plassey and put to death at Murshidabad by Mir Ja‘far’s son Miran (July 1757).
events.source: web-only; library silent on his death (HCIP VIII p. 339 says only that he 'lost his nerves and fled'). Famous and uncontested; the last independent Nawab of Bengal.

events.text: The Treaty of Alinagar: after Clive and Watson retake Calcutta, Siraj-ud-daulah restores the Company’s trade rights and factories, promises compensation and lets it fortify Calcutta and coin sicca rupees (9 February 1757).
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 112: 'Adverse circumstances now forced Siraj-ud-daulah to conclude the treaty of ‘Alinagar on 9 February, 1757, by which trade rights and factories of the English East India Company were restored to them ... the English were granted permission by him to fortify Calcutta and to coin sicca rupees.'

events.text: Adina Beg Khan dies — the survivor who played Mughals, Afghans, Sikhs and Marathas against each other and ended as Maratha-backed governor of the Punjab; confusion followed at once.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 77: 'Adina Beg Khan enjoyed his highest glory for five months only. On 13 October 1758 he died after a prolonged illness ... Immediately afterwards, confusion broke out in the Panjab.' (Place of death not given in the book; coordinates approximate, Hoshiarpur district.)

events.text: Afghan-Maratha War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire and Sikh Confederacy vs Durrani Empire and Rohilkhand
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Sadashivrao Bhau, Raghunath Rao, Malhar Rao Holkar, Dattaji/Jankoji Scindia; Sikh leaders including Jassa Singh Ahluwalia by phase — Ahmad Shah Durrani; Najib-ud-Daula; Shuja-ud-Daula; Rohilla and Afghan allies

events.text: Maratha capture of Lahore & Peshawar: the empire at its zenith
events.source: Stewart Gordon
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory — the high-water mark, held barely a year

events.text: Marthanda Varma dies — the 'Maker of Modern Travancore', victor of Colachel, who annexed the neighbouring chiefdoms and dedicated the kingdom to Sri Padmanabha.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 233: 'He is rightly regarded as the Maker of Modern Travancore ... Karthika Tirunal Rama Varma (1758-1798) ... succeeded Marthanda Varma on the throne'; p. 266: 'Marthanda Varma (1729-1758)'.

events.text: Siege of Madras (1758–59): Lally occupies the Black Town and bombards Fort St George for ten weeks from 12 December, but raises the siege when Pocock's fleet appears in February 1759.
events.belligerents: French India vs East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Lally precipitately raises the siege
events.commanders: Comte de Lally, Bussy — Stringer Lawrence, William Draper, George Pigot
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 334: 'Lally began the long-pending siege of Madras (December 12) ... When the English fleet under Admiral Pocock was sighted off the coast, Lally precipitately raised the siege and moved to Arcot'.

events.text: Alamgir II murdered: fearing the emperor would become Abdali's tool, the wazir Imad-ul-Mulk has him lured to the Kotla of Firuz Shah and killed on 29 November 1759, and Intizam-ud-daulah strangled the next day; Prince Ali Gauhar, in Bihar, proclaims himself Shah Alam II.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 213: '§ 8. Imad murders Alamgir II. and Intezam-ud-daulah... He got the harmless crowned puppet murdered on 29th November and his long powerless old rival Intizam-ud-daulah strangled the next day.'

events.text: Battle of Kakkor: The Battle of Kakkor was fought by the Maratha Holkar principality of Indore, led by the veteran Gangadhar Tatya, who was sent into battle by Malhar Rao Holkar.
events.belligerents: Indore State vs Jaipur
events.outcome: Holkar victory
events.commanders: Malharrao Holkar, Gangadhar Tatya — Pratap Singh Naruka, Thakur Jodhsingh Nathawat, Thakur Gulab Singh
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Taraori (1759): The Battle of Taraori in 1759 was a military engagement between the Durrani Empire and the Maratha Empire and the Mughals in the fields of Taraori.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Maratha Empire, Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani, Sardar Jahan Khan, Shah Pasand Khan — Dattaji Rao Scindia, Imad-ul-Mulk
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Shukartal: Dattaji Sindhia besieges Najib Khan's entrenched camp on the Ganges from September to December 1759; Najib holds out until Abdali's return to the Punjab forces the Marathas to raise the siege.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Dattaji Sindhia) vs Rohilkhand (Rohillas) — Najib Khan
events.outcome: Rohilla victory; the Maratha siege failed and Dattaji raised it on 8 December
events.commanders: Dattaji Sindhia, Govind Ballal Bundele — Najib Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 207: '§ 5. Dattaji’s siege of Shukartal; fighting.'; p. 216: 'There was nothing left for Dattaji now but to raise his futile siege (8th December.)'

events.text: The Dutch defeat in Bengal (Chinsurah–Biderra): a Dutch expedition from Batavia, encouraged by Mir Ja‘far, is beaten by Clive’s forces on the Hooghly, ending any Dutch challenge in Bengal.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Dutch India
events.outcome: East India Company victory; 'the Dutch were badly defeated and humbled'
events.commanders: Robert Clive, Francis Forde — Dutch commanders from Batavia
events.source: HCIP VIII pp. 341–342: 'An expedition was despatched from Batavia, but delayed so long ... that Clive got sufficient time for preparations ... with the result that the Dutch were badly defeated and humbled (December 1759).' (Web accounts date the land battle at Biderra to 25 November 1759.)

events.text: Battle of Barari Ghat: The Battle of Barari Ghat बुराडी घाट was a military engagement between the Durrani-Rohilla Afghans and the Maratha army in which the Maratha army was defeated.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire, Kingdom of Rohilkhand vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Durrani-Rohilla victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shāh, Najib-ud-Daula, Sardar Qutb Shah — Dattaji Rao Scindia, Sabaji Rao Scindia, Jankoji Rao Scindia
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 222: '§ 12. Battle of Barari-ghat; Dattaji slain. Here Sabaji was surprised at his post on 9th January 1760. Najib crossed the river unperceived'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 828 dates it 10 January 1760

events.text: Battle of Kunjpura: The Battle of Kunjpura was fought on 17 October 1760, and it was a significant engagement during the Maratha-Afghan Wars.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Durrani Empire, Kingdom of Rohilkhand
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Sadashiv Rao Bhau, Ibrahim Khan Gardi, Mahadaji Scindia — Najabat Khan, Abdus Samad Khan, Momin Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Masumpur: on his second invasion of Bihar the new emperor Shah Alam II beats Raja Ram Narayan, the Nawab’s deputy, four miles east of Fatuha on 9 February 1760.
