events.belligerents: Mughal Empire (Shah Alam II, Kamgar Khan) vs Bengal (Nawab) — Ram Narayan, with East India Company sepoys
events.outcome: Mughal victory; Ram Narayan defeated and wounded, three of his commanders go over, four companies of Company sepoys cut off with Captain Cochrane
events.commanders: Shah Alam II, Kamgar Khan — Ram Narayan, Captain Cochrane
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II pp. 539–540: 'Ram Narayan ... had issued from Patna and given battle to the imperialists at Masumpur on 9th February; but three of his divisional commanders treacherously went over to the enemy ... Ram Narayan had to retreat to his fort defeated and wounded. Four companies of English sepoys were cut off with all their three European officers, including Captain Cochrane.'

events.text: Battle of Meerut: The Battle of Meerut was a military skirmish initiated by Emperor Ahmed Shah Durrani in an attempt to capture Govind Pant Bundela, who had taken refuge in Meerut.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Durrani Empire victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani, Atai Khan — Govind Pant Bundela
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Sherpur (Sirpur): Major Caillaud and Miran defeat Shah Alam II near Bakhtiyarpur on 22 February 1760; the emperor’s raid on Murshidabad that followed failed.
events.belligerents: East India Company and Bengal (Nawab) vs Mughal Empire (Shah Alam II)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Shah Alam beaten but, the Nawab’s cavalry refusing to pursue, retires unbroken to Bihar city
events.commanders: John Caillaud, Miran — Shah Alam II, Kamgar Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 540: 'Major Caillaud pushed up and on the 22nd completely defeated him at Sherpur. The refusal of the Nawab’s cavalry to obey the English commander enabled the Emperor to retire unbroken to Bihar city.' HCIP VIII p. 342: 'The Shahzada was beaten in an engagement at Sirpur, but Miran would not follow up the victory.'

events.text: Battle of Sikandarabad: The Battle of Sikandrabad was a military engagement between the Afghan Durranis and the Marathas near the city of Sikandrabad.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire, Kingdom of Rohilkhand vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory; Malhar Rao Holkar's army routed by Jahan Khan
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah, Sardar Jahan Khan, Najib Khan — Malharro Holkar
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 828: '1760, March 4 The Maratha army under the command of Malhar Rao Holkar is defeated by Ahmad Shah Abdali’s forces at Sikandrabad (pp. 192, 254).'; Sarkar II contents: 'Malhar Holkar routed by Jahan Khan, 228'

events.text: Battle of Udgir: Sadashivrao Bhau routs the Nizam's army near Udgir on 3 February 1760. By the treaty of 11 February, the Nizam cedes territory worth sixty lakhs together with Burhanpur and Asirgarh, Daulatabad, Ahmadnagar and Bijapur.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Nizam ceded 60 lakhs of territory and four fortress-capitals
events.commanders: Sadashivrao Bhau, Vishwasrao, Ibrahim Khan Gardi — Nizam Ali, Salabat Jang
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 337: 'On 3rd February a stiff action was fought in which the Asaf Jahi forces were so completely routed that Nizam Ali sent ambassadors seeking terms. He agreed to surrender to the Peshwa territory worth sixty lacs'. HCIP VIII p. 183: 'The Nizam's forces were completely defeated ... Final victory was gained on 3 February, 1760.'

events.text: Battle of Wandiwash: Eyre Coote defeats Lally, deciding the Anglo-French contest for India
events.belligerents: East India Company vs French India
events.commanders: Sir Eyre Coote — Comte de Lally
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Lally loses heavily and Bussy is captured (January 1760)
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 335: 'In the battle which followed, Coote won a decisive victory, while Lally lost heavily in men and guns, Bussy himself being among the prisoners taken (January 1760).'

events.text: Capture of Delhi (1760): The Capture of Delhi, fought in 1760, pitted the forces of the Maratha Empire against those of the Durrani Empire led by Yakub Ali Khan.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Bharatpur State vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Maratha and Jat victory
events.commanders: Sadashiv Rao Bhau, Malhar Rao Holkar, Jankoji Rao Scindia — Yakub Ali Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 828: '1760, August 2 Sadashiv Rao Bhau, the commandant of the Marathas, captures Delhi (p. 193)'; Sarkar II p. 252: '§ 7. The Bhau captures Delhi.'

events.text: Dattaji Sindhia dies — Killed at Barari Ghat on the Jamuna fighting Najib's Rohillas and Abdali's Afghans, a year before Panipat.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 222: '§ 12. Battle of Barari-ghat; Dattaji slain.'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 828: '1760, January 10 Dattaji Sindia is killed in the battle of Buradi Ghat against Ahmad Shah Abdali' (Sarkar dates the battle 9 January)

events.text: Mir Qasim made Nawab of Bengal: by a treaty of 27 September 1760 the Calcutta Council makes Mir Qasim diwan and heir, in return for Burdwan, Midnapur and Chittagong; Mir Ja‘far, refusing, resigns and Mir Qasim is installed (October 1760).
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 344: 'On 27 September a treaty was signed between Mir Qasim and the English by which the English agreed to appoint Mir Qasim to the post of Diwan and promised him the succession to Mir Ja‘far, while Mir Qasim agreed to cede to the English the districts of Burdwan, Midnapur and Chittagong ... Mir Ja‘far after some hesitation resigned his office altogether.' Sarkar II p. 542 dates the elevation 20 October 1760.

events.text: Siege of Pondicherry: the British take France's capital in India; the Compagnie's power is broken
events.belligerents: East India Company vs French India
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Lally surrenders unconditionally (January 1761) and the fortifications are razed
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 335: 'After more than four months of desperate resistance, Lally ... surrendered unconditionally (January 1761). The English ruthlessly demolished all the fortifications of the city.'

events.text: Battle of Gujranwala (1761): The Battle of Gujranwala was fought between the Durrani Empire and the Sikh Confederacy in September 1761.
events.belligerents: Sikh Misls vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Charat Singh, Hari Singh Dhillon — Khawaja Abid Khan, Nur-ud-din
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Mangrol (Bhatwara): Malhar Rao Holkar, with the Sindhia family contingent and Zalim Singh's Kota troops, destroyed Madho Singh's Jaipur army between Mangrol and Bhatwara on 29 November 1761, ending the anti-Maratha coalition that Panipat had encouraged in Rajputana.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Holkar), Kota vs Jaipur
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Jaipur army destroyed and its camp and guns taken. (Tod's Rajput tradition credits the Kota contingent at 'Butwarro'; Sarkar rejects it.)
events.commanders: Malhar Rao Holkar, Zalim Singh (Kota) — Raj Singh, diwans Kaniram and Nandlal
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 507: 'Next day the battle raged from the morning and ended near sunset in the total destruction of the Jaipur army.' p. 508: 'The victory was decisive; it at once destroyed all chance of forming an anti-Maratha coalition, and restored Maratha prestige.' Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 253: 'in November 1761 a large Jaipur army was defeated by Malhar Rao Holkar in the battle of Mangrol.'

events.text: Battle of Sialkot (1761): Charat Singh's Sukerchakia Misl beat off a Durrani force under Jahan Khan at Sialkot — the first of two Sikh–Afghan actions at the town.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Charat Singh, Menander Singh — Timur Shah Durrani, Sardar Jahan Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Suan (Helsa): on Shah Alam’s third Bihar campaign Colonel Carnac defeats the imperial army six miles west of Bihar city on 15 January 1761 and captures Jean Law and his Frenchmen; the emperor then treats with the English.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mughal Empire (Shah Alam II) with Jean Law’s French
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Law and his officers captured, Shah Alam sues for terms and visits Carnac at Gaya
events.commanders: John Carnac — Shah Alam II, Jean Law, Kamgar Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 542: 'The end came on 15th January 1761, when at the village of Suan (6 miles west of Bihar city) Col. Carnac defeated the imperialists and captured Law and his French officers.' HCIP VIII p. 344: 'On 15 January, 1761, Carnac inflicted a severe defeat on the Shahzada.'

events.text: Haidar Ali becomes master of Mysore: after surviving Khande Rao's cannonade of 12 August 1760 and a Maratha blockade at Bangalore, Haidar besieges Srirangapatna; the king surrenders Khande Rao and Haidar rules as the Wodeyars' regent.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 454: 'On 12 August, 1760, a cannonade was opened from the ramparts of the fort of Seringapatam on Haidar's residence ... When Haidar besieged Seringapatam, the King made an abject surrender and handed over Khande Rao.' Menon p. 243 dates Haidar's ascent 'As soon as Haider Ali ascended the throne of Mysore (1761)'.

events.text: Madhavrao I becomes Peshwa: after Panipat and Balaji Rao's death, his second son Madhavrao, aged sixteen, is made Peshwa, with his uncle Raghunathrao as regent and the real ruler.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 201: 'Madhav Rao, the second son of Balaji Baji Rao, was placed on the Peshwa's gadi in his seventeenth year; Raghunath became Regent and the de facto ruler of the State.'

events.text: Peshwa Balaji Bajirao (Nanasaheb) dies — five months after Panipat, where his son and his cousin were killed.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 197: 'Shortly after hearing the result of the battle of Panipat Balaji Rao Peshwa died on 23 June, 1761.'

events.text: Sadashivrao Bhau dies — Commander of the Maratha army, killed at the third battle of Panipat with the Peshwa’s heir Vishwasrao.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 343: 'The wounded lion turned at bay and struck three or four of his assailants with his spear before he was killed and his head cut off and carried away by his slayers. Thus perished Sadashiv Rao Bhau'; p. 341: '§ 20. Death of Vishwas Rao'

events.text: Suraj Mal takes Agra fort: after Panipat the Jat raja besieges the old Mughal capital and its garrison opens the gates on 12 June 1761; its artillery and treasure are carried off to Bharatpur and Dig, and the Jat kingdom reaches its greatest extent.
events.belligerents: Bharatpur vs Mughal Empire (garrison of Agra fort)
events.outcome: Bharatpur victory; the qiladar surrendered Agra fort for a lakh of rupees and five villages
events.commanders: Suraj Mal — qiladar Fazil Khan
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 443-444: '§ 10. Suraj Mal captures Agra fort, June 1761... the qiladar opened the gates on 12th June 1761, on being promised one lakh of Rupees in cash and five villages.'

events.text: Tarabai dies — Rajaram's queen, who led the Maratha war against Aurangzeb and later opposed Shahu and the Peshwas.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 122: 'the aged Tarabai, Chhatrapati Rajaram's wife also died ten years later on December 9, 1761.'

events.text: Third Battle of Panipat: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeats the Marathas, who suffer a crippling blow
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 828: '1761, January 14 Ahmad Shah Abdali, defeats the Maratha army at the third battle of Panipat (pp. 44, 125, 132, 137, 146, 194-97).'; Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 274: '§16. How Shuja-ud-daulah was won over to Abdali’s side'; II contents: 'death of Vishwas Rao, 341—Bhau’s last charge and death, 342'
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire, Rohilkhand (Rohillas), Awadh
events.outcome: Durrani victory; the Maratha army destroyed, Vishwas Rao and Sadashivrao Bhau killed, Holkar and Sindhia contingents fled
events.commanders: Sadashivrao Bhau; Vishwasrao; Maratha chiefs under Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao — Ahmad Shah Durrani; Najib-ud-Daula; Shuja-ud-Daula

events.text: Battle of Alegaon: The Battle of Alegaon was fought between Nizam Ali Khan of Hyderabad and Raghunathrao of the Maratha Empire against Madhavrao I of the Maratha Confederacy.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Peshwa Madhavrao I) vs Raghunathrao's faction, Hyderabad, Janoji Bhonsle
events.outcome: Hyderabad and Raghunathrao victory; the young Peshwa, beaten in two battles in November 1762, submitted to his uncle and was confined, and Raghunathrao ceded Daulatabad, Shivneri, Asirgarh and Ahmadnagar to Nizam Ali
events.commanders: Madhavrao I — Nizam Ali Khan, Raghunathrao
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 202: 'Raghunath ... received active assistance from Nizam Ali and Janoji Bhosle. In November, 1762, the Peshwa's army was defeated in two battles ... He surrendered to Nizam Ali several districts including the forts of Daulatabad, Shivneri, Asirgarh and Ahmadnagar.' Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II chronology p. 463: 'Madhavrao being defeated at Alegaon submits to Raghunathrao and is confined.'

events.text: Battle of Harnaulgarh: The Battle of Harnaulgarh was fought between the Durrani Empire and the Sikh Misls of Dal Khalsa in 1762.
events.belligerents: Sikh Misls vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Charat Singh — Zain Khan Sirhindi
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Kup (the Vadda Ghallughara): Ahmad Shah, marching by forced stages from Lahore, caught the Sikh army near Kup, six miles north of Maler Kotla, on 5 February 1762 and pursued it all day; some ten thousand Sikhs were killed.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II pp. 485–486: 'Early in the forenoon of 5th February, Zain Khan's vanguard ... fell in with the Sikhs near the village of Kup (6 miles north of Maler Kotla) ... In the course of this running fight, some ten thousand Sikhs were slain and the day is still remembered by them as that of the Ghallu-ghara or great scrimmage.'
events.belligerents: Durrani (Afghan) Empire, Maler Kotla vs Sikh misls
events.outcome: Durrani victory; the Great Massacre (Vadda Ghallughara) of the Sikhs
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani — Sikh Confederacy leaders including Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and Charat Singh

events.text: Battle of Pipli Sahib: The Battle of Pipli Sahib, also known as Battle of Amritsar, was fought by the Sikh Misls and the Durrani Empire.
events.belligerents: Dal Khalsa vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Disputed, see Result
events.commanders: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Charat Singh, Jassa Singh Ramgarhia — Ahmad Shah Abdali
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Uruli: the Nizam invades after Panipat and ravages the country up to Toka. His army is routed at Uruli near Poona in January 1762, but the regent Raghunathrao grants him lenient terms.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Nizam's army suffered a clear defeat
events.commanders: Raghunathrao, Madhavrao I — Nizam Ali, Salabat Jang
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 201: 'Skirmishes extending over several months were followed by a decisive battle in January, 1762, in which the Nizam's army suffered a clear defeat ... the Regent ... conciliated the defeated enemy by granting him very favourable terms.' Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II chronology pp. 463–464: 'Nizam Ali occupies Chas and comes to Uruli where he is routed.'

events.text: Battle of the Ravi Ford: The Battle of the Ravi Ford took place on 12 December 1762 between Afghans and Sikhs on the Ravi River.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Sikh Misls
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani — Unknown
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Durrani reconquest of Kashmir: Ahmad Shah sent an army guided by Ranjit Dev of Jammu against Sukhjivan, the diwan who had thrown off Durrani authority; after a first repulse the second expedition took him prisoner and annexed Kashmir again.
events.belligerents: Durrani (Afghan) Empire, Jammu hill states vs Kashmir (Sukhjivan)
events.outcome: Durrani victory; Sukhjivan captured, Kashmir re-annexed
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II pp. 488–489: 'Abdali set himself to recover Kashmir from Sukhjivan Ram Khatri ... A later expedition achieved complete success, Sukhjivan was defeated and taken prisoner, and Kashmir annexed to the Durrani empire.'

events.text: Nizam Ali takes power in Hyderabad: he deposes his brother Salabat Jang (a chronology dates this July 1761), confines him on 7 July 1762 and has him killed in September 1763.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas II p. 337: 'Salabat Jang could not hold his own against Nizam Ali, who first put him into confinement on 7th July 1762, and later put him to death on 16th September 1763.' Sardesai II chronology p. 463 dates 'Nizam Ali deposes Salabat Jang' to 1761, July 6. HCIP VIII p. 122: 'Nizam Ali rose to power about 1760'.

events.text: The Anglo-Manipur treaty: Jai Singh’s envoy Haridas Gossain agrees with Verelst at Chittagong (14 September 1762) on an offensive and defensive alliance against Burma — Manipur’s first treaty with the Company; the relief column turned back sick.
events.source: HCIP IX p. 1027: 'The terms of the alliance were settled on 14th September, 1762. This was the first formal agreement between the Government of Manipur and the British Government of India ... The British contingent, however, suffered from rain and disease and had to return without achieving any success.'

events.text: Battle of Rakshasbhuvan: the Nizam and Janoji Bhonsle had sacked Poona in May 1763. Madhavrao I wins Janoji over, then defeats Nizam Ali's army under Vithal Sundar on the Godavari on 10 August 1763. Peace follows on 25 September.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Nizam's army under Vithal Sundar defeated and peace made in September 1763
events.commanders: Peshwa Madhavrao I, Damaji Gaekwad — Vithal Sundar (for Nizam Ali)
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 202: 'In May, 1763, Nizam Ali plundered Poona ... On August 10, 1763, a portion of Nizam Ali's army under the command of Vithal Sundar was defeated by the Peshwa in the battle of Rakshasbhuvan. Peace was concluded on September 25, 1763'; p. 244: 'defeated the Nizam signally at Rakshasbhuvan in August, 1763'; p. 284 (Damaji's horse 'materially contributed to the final victory').

events.text: Battle of Sialkot (1763): on 12 November 1763 Charat Singh, now joined by the Bhangi sardars, again defeated Jahan Khan's Durrani force at Sialkot — the second and larger action there.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl, Bhangi Misl vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Charat Singh, Jhanda Singh Bhangi, Gujjar Singh Bhangi — Sardar Jahan Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Thrissur: The Battle of Thrissur took place at Thrissur in 1763 between the forces of the Kingdom of Travancore and the Zamorin of Calicut.
events.belligerents: Travancore, Cochin vs Calicut (Zamorin)
events.outcome: Travancore victory; the Zamorin's forces are driven out of Cochin, and the Zamorin sues for peace and pays Rs 1,50,000
events.commanders: Marthanda Pillai Eustachius De Lannoy — Zamorin Raja
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 234: 'The Zamorin's forces were driven out of Cochin territory. The Zamorin himself sued for peace ... In 1763 the Zamorin himself paid a visit to the Travancore Raja ... to pay Rs. 1,50,000 as indemnity'.

events.text: Battle of the Hindan: Suraj Mal, marching on Delhi against its Rohilla regent Najib-ud-Daula, is ambushed while crossing a ravine by the Hindan near Ghaziabad on 25 December 1763 and killed; his army withdraws in the night.
events.belligerents: Najib-ud-Daula (Rohilla) vs Bharatpur
events.outcome: Najib-ud-Daula victory; Suraj Mal shot and cut down by Rohilla musketeers in ambush, the Jat army retreated
events.commanders: Najib-ud-Daula — Suraj Mal (killed)
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 451: 'It was the 25th of December... in crossing a nala left behind by the river, he fell into an Afghan ambuscade and was shot down with most of his companions by the Ruhela musketeers lying concealed among the jhau bushes.'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 829: '1763, December 25 Death of Suraj Mal Jat in a contest with Najib-ud-daulah on the bank of the Hindaun'

events.text: Conquest of Bednur: Haidar takes the Keladi (Ikkeri) capital in the name of a pretender, renames it Haidar-Nagara and ends the Nayaka state; the loot finances his rise and brings him to the borders of Kerala.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs Ikkeri (Keladi) Nayak
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Bednur falls (c. third week of January 1763) and the Keladi Nayaka kingdom is annexed
events.commanders: Haidar Ali — Rani Virammaji
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore II p. 470 (block 443): 'bestowed on Bednur the new name of Haidar-Nagara ... Bednur fell, as we have seen, about the third week of January 1763'. HCIP VIII p. 455: 'After the conquest of Bednur was completed in the name of the boy-king, Haidar declared him an impostor'.

events.text: Revolt of Muhammad Yusuf Khan: the Company's commandant of Madurai and Tinnevelly rebels against Nawab Muhammad Ali and is besieged in Madurai; he appeals in vain to Haidar and is hanged in 1764.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs Muhammad Yusuf Khan (Madurai)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the revolt fails and Yusuf Khan is hanged (1764)
events.commanders: Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah and Company officers — Muhammad Yusuf Khan
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore II p. 518 (block 485): 'Muhammad Yusuf Khan, who commanded Madura in the English interests and had rebelled against them and been, in consequence, closely invested by them at Madura'; p. 248 n. (block 243): 'Yusuf Khan proved a rebel and was hanged in 1764' (OCR '1784'). Menon p. 234: 'The rebellion of Yusuf Khan failed as a result of the help rendered to the Nawab by the English.'

events.text: Suraj Mal dies — Killed in a Rohilla ambush by the Hindan, aged fifty-five, 'at the height of his greatness'; the Jat raja who made Bharatpur the strongest Hindu power near Delhi.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 453: 'Thus perished Suraj Mal at the height of his greatness at the age of fifty-five.'

events.text: The Company’s war with Mir Qasim: after Ellis seizes Patna (June 1763) the Company restores Mir Ja‘far and routs Mir Qasim’s Western-trained army at Katwa, Gheria and Udaynala, takes Monghyr and storms Patna; Mir Qasim, after murdering Gurgin Khan, the Seths and his English prisoners, flees to Awadh.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Bengal (Nawab) — Mir Qasim
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Mir Qasim deposed and driven into Awadh, Mir Ja‘far restored
events.commanders: Thomas Adams — Mir Qasim, Gurgin Khan, Samru
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 349: 'The Nawab’s army was routed at Katwa, at Murshidabad and at Udaynalla and the English then laid siege to Monghyr ... he caused Gurgin Khan, his Armenian Commander-in-Chief, the Seths and then his English prisoners, to be murdered in succession, and when the English army carried Patna by storm, Mir Qasim escaped into Awadh.'

events.text: The Sannyasi–Fakir rebellion: armed bands of Hindu sannyasis and Muslim fakirs (Majnu Shah, Bhawani Pathak) raid Company factories and revenue posts across north Bengal and Bihar for a generation, until Hastings and his successors put them down.
events.belligerents: Sannyasis and Fakirs (Majnu Shah, Bhawani Pathak) vs East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the bands suppressed by c. 1800
events.commanders: Warren Hastings — Majnu Shah, Musa Shah, Bhawani Pathak
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire I p. 104: the Marathas 'showed the way for the organised looting of Bengal and Bihar to the up-country robber bands calling themselves sannyasis and faqirs, whom it required the genius of a Warren Hastings to suppress.' Dates 1763–1800 and leaders web-only; library silent on the details.

events.text: Battle of Buxar: the Company beats Mir Qasim, Awadh and the Mughal emperor together, winning the Diwani of Bengal
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 115: 'The two armies met at Buxar on 22 October, 1764. It resulted in Shuja-ud-daulah’s crushing defeat ... It confirmed British supremacy over Bengal and Bihar'; p. 349: 'Before the battle Mir Qasim had been imprisoned and deprived of his possessions by Shuja-ud-daulah.' Books disagree on the date: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 545: 'crushing defeat at Buxar (23 October 1764)'.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mughal Empire, Awadh & Mir Qasim of Bengal
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Shuja-ud-daulah’s 'crushing defeat' leaves Awadh and Shah Alam at the Company’s mercy — Mir Qasim, already stripped by Shuja, took no real part
events.commanders: Hector Munro and East India Company forces — Shah Alam II, Shuja-ud-Daula and Mir Qasim

events.text: Battle of Chenab: The Battle of Chenab was fought in early 1764 between the forces of the Durrani Empire, led by Ahmad Shah Durrani, and the combined armies of several Sikh Misls.
events.belligerents: Sikh Confederacy vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Charat Singh Sukerchakia, Hari Singh Bhangi, Jassa Singh Ramgarhia — Ahmad Shah Durrani, Jahan Khan Popalzai, Wazir Shah Wali Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Qarawal: The Battle of Qarawal was fought between the Sikhs under the command of Charat Singh against the Afghan forces led by Ahmad Shah Abdali and his Kalat ally Mir Nasir Khan I.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire, Khanate of Kalat vs Sukerchakia Misl
events.outcome: Afghan victory
events.commanders: Ahmad Shah Durrani, Nasir Khan, Gahram Khan — Charat Singh
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Rattihalli: Peshwa Madhav Rao draws Haidar out of his chosen position and surrounds him; Haidar retreats to Anavatti, is beaten again in December, and must pay tribute and give up Savanur and Gooty lands.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Haidar 'sustained a severe loss involving the flower of his army', then defeated again at Anavatti and forced to pay 28 lakhs
events.commanders: Peshwa Madhav Rao I — Haidar Ali
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore II p. 497: 'Haidar was not only foiled in all his objects, but also sustained a severe loss involving the flower of his army.' HCIP VIII p. 455: 'Haidar Ali was defeated in an engagement at Ratehalli ... on 3 May, 1764 ... a treaty was concluded by which Haidar paid 28 lakhs as tribute'.

events.text: Battle of Sirhind
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 492: 'then attacked Sarhind in a body 40,000 strong (December 1763.) ... The faujdar of Sarhind, at the head of a small impoverished army, came out of the city and was defeated and slain, with the loss of his baggage and armament. The Sikhs, flushed with victory, entered Sarhind, and "looted and totally devastated it".' Sarkar dates the attack December 1763; the decisive fight is usually put in January 1764.
events.belligerents: Sikh misls vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire (Zain Khan, faujdar of Sarhind)
events.outcome: Sikh victory; Zain Khan defeated and slain, Sarhind sacked
events.commanders: Sikh Confederacy leaders including Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Baba Ala Singh and allied misldars — Zain Khan Sirhindi / Durrani governor

events.text: Jawahir Singh's siege of Delhi: to avenge his father, Jawahir Singh besieges Najib-ud-Daula in Delhi with Malhar Holkar's Marathas, Sikh bands and Naga mercenaries (November 1764 – February 1765); Holkar's double-dealing and his own captains' collusion force him to make peace.
events.belligerents: Bharatpur, Maratha Empire (Malhar Rao Holkar), Sikh misls vs Najib-ud-Daula (Rohilla)
events.outcome: Najib-ud-Daula victory; Delhi held despite famine, and Jawahir Singh made peace in February 1765
events.commanders: Jawahir Singh, Malhar Rao Holkar — Najib-ud-Daula
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 461: 'The first battle took place on 15th November'; p. 467: 'At last Jawahir realized that he had nothing to hope for from the faith of Malhar, the prestige of Imad, or the arms of the Sikhs and Nagas... Negotiations for peace were set on foot on 4th February'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 830: '1765, February Jawahir Singh Jat makes peace with Najib Khan Rohilla'

events.text: Kandyan–Dutch War: the Company reached and burned Kandy but could not hold it. The Treaty of Batticaloa in 1766 gave the Dutch the entire coastline and left the kingdom landlocked.
events.source: BharatRajya research pass, Sri Lanka (see scripts/add_srilanka_battles.py)
events.belligerents: Kandy under Kirti Sri Rajasinha vs the Dutch East India Company
events.outcome: Kandy keeps its independence and loses its coast

events.text: Siege of Rohtas (1764): The Siege of Rohtas took place in 1764 when Sikh leaders Charat Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl and Gujjar Singh of the Bhangi Misl laid siege to the Rohtas Fort.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl, Bhangi Misl vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Charat Singh Sukerchakia, Gujjar Singh Bhangi — Sarbuland Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Sikh attacks on Delhi: Sikh attacks on Delhi were a number of attacks and raids carried out by the Sikhs on the Mughal capital of Delhi in the second half of the 18th century.
events.belligerents: Sikh Confederacy, Rohillas (from 1787), Co-belligirents vs Mughal Empire, Rohillas (until 1787), Maratha Confederacy (1784-1788)
events.outcome: Sikh victory; plunder of Mughal, Rohilla and Rajput territories.
events.commanders: Leaders:, Baghel Singh, Jassa Singh Ahluwalia — Leaders:, Shah Alam II
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Kora: after Buxar, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and his Maratha ally Malhar Holkar are finally defeated by the Company's army under Fletcher (3 May 1765); Awadh falls under British control and Shah Alam II takes refuge with the English at Allahabad.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Awadh, Maratha Empire (Malhar Rao Holkar)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Shuja-ud-Daula's last army dispersed and Awadh occupied
events.commanders: Sir Robert Fletcher — Shuja-ud-Daula, Malhar Rao Holkar
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 115: 'After running from one place to another he was finally defeated at the battle of Kora on 3 May 1765... Awadh fell completely under British control.'; chronology p. 830: 'The allies of exile Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-daulah and Malhar Rao Holkar are finally defeated at Kora by the English army under Sir Robert Fletcher'

events.text: Mir Ja‘far dies — The commander whose defection decided Plassey, twice made Nawab of Bengal by the Company (1757–60, 1763–65).
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 350: 'Mir Ja‘far who was old and very ill died in February 1765.'

events.text: The Sikhs take Lahore: as soon as Ahmad Shah turned home, the Bhangi chiefs Lahna Singh and Gujar Singh, with Sobha Singh, entered Lahore and divided the city between them; the chiefs then struck the Khalsa coin at Amritsar.
events.belligerents: Sikh misls (Bhangi) vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire (Kabuli Mal, governor of Lahore)
events.outcome: Sikh victory; Lahore held by the Sikh chiefs until Ranjit Singh
events.commanders: Lahna Singh, Gujar Singh, Sobha Singh — Kabuli Mal
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 225: 'On the occasion of Baisakhi at Amritsar, both Lahna Singh and Gujar Singh planned the occupation of Lahore ... They occupied Lahore jointly.' Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II pp. 494–495 puts it in 1764, right after Abdali left: 'the three Sikh leaders Lehna Singh, Gujar Singh and Sobha Singh attacked Lahor. The masterless city capitulated ... the three chiefs divided the city between them.' Books differ on the year (Gupta 1765, Sarkar 1764).

events.text: The Treaty of Allahabad and the Diwani: Shah Alam II’s farman of 12 August 1765 grants the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa; the treaty of 16 August restores Awadh to Shuja-ud-daulah less Kora and Allahabad (given to the emperor) and Chunar.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 547: 'the Emperor, by a farman signed on 12th August ... granted them the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa (the last subah now comprising the Midnapur district only.)' HCIP VIII p. 116: 'By the Treaty of Allahabad dated 16 August, 1765, all the territories of Shuja-ud-daulah were restored to him, with the exception of the districts of Kora and Allahabad ... Chunar which was retained by the English.' (Milestone M496 carries the Diwani; the event layer has no row for it.)

events.text: The Treaty of Allahabad with Awadh (16 August 1765): Clive restores Shuja-ud-Daula to Awadh minus Kora and Allahabad (given to Shah Alam II), keeps Chunar, puts Banaras under Balwant Singh and takes fifty lakhs indemnity and a defensive-treaty charge — the start of Awadh's subordination to the Company. (The same month's diwani farman is milestone M496.)
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 830: '1765, August 16 The treaty of Allahabad concluded between Nawab Shuja-ud-daulah and the English, terms being (1) restoration of all the territories held by the Nawab with the exception of Allahabad and Kora districts given to the emperor, (2) Chunar to be retained by the English'

events.text: Battle of Dholpur: Jawahir Singh's Jats, with Sikh allies, defeat Raghunath Rao's Maratha army on the Chambal (13–14 March 1766) and occupy Dholpur.
events.belligerents: Bharatpur, Sikh misls vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Bharatpur victory; the Maratha army defeated and Dholpur occupied, several Maratha commanders captured
events.commanders: Jawahir Singh — Raghunath Rao's generals
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 831: '1766, March 13/14 The combined Jat-Sikh army under the leadership of Jawahir Singh defeats the Maratha army at the battle of Dholpur and occupy Dholpur (p. 217)'; p. 831: 'Jawahir Singh Jat concludes peace with Raghunath Rao by surrendering Maratha commanders captured in March, 1766'

events.text: Battle of Multan (1766): The Battle of Multan was an indecisive engagement fought in December 1766 by the forces of the Bhangi Misl, led by Jhanda Singh Bhangi and Ganda Singh Bhangi.
events.belligerents: Bhangi Misl vs Bahawalpur State
events.outcome: Inconclusive territorial division agreed by treaty
events.commanders: Jhanda Singh Bhangi, Ganda Singh Bhangi — Mubarik Khan, Shuja Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Haidar takes Calicut: Mysore's army, joined by the Ali Raja of Cannanore, overruns Kolathunad, Kottayam and Kadathanad and enters Calicut; the Zamorin, unable to pay a crore of mohurs, blows up his palace and dies in it.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Arakkal vs Calicut (Zamorin), Kolathunad
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Calicut occupied and the Zamorin dies by self-immolation
events.commanders: Haidar Ali, Ali Raja — Zamorin of Calicut
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 244: 'The Mysorean army thereupon entered Calicut. The Zamorin sent the members of his family to Ponnani, blew up his palace and committed self-immolation.' Kareem, Kerala under Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan p. 32: 'He set his palace on fire and was burnt to death'.

events.text: Malhar Rao Holkar dies — At Alampur near the Chambal, founder of the house of Holkar and for thirty years the Maratha power in Hindustan.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 831: '1766, May 20 Death of Malhar Rao Holkar at Alampur (pp. 146, 217, 255, 269).'

events.text: Maratha–Sikh clashes: The Maratha–Sikh clashes of 1766–1798 were a series of intermittent conflicts between the Maratha Empire and the Sikh Confederacy, primarily in Northern India.
events.belligerents: Maratha Confederacy, Mughal Empire, Rohillas (till 1787) vs Sikh Confederacy, Patiala state, Rohillas(from 1787)
events.outcome: Sikh victory Maratha failure to subdue the Cis-Sutlej states
events.commanders: Mahadaji Shinde, Rane Khan, George Thomas — Sahib Singh of Patiala, Bibi Sahib Kaur, Raja Bhag Singh
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Mysorean invasion of Malabar: The Mysorean invasion of Malabar (1766–1792) was the military invasion of the Malabar region of Kerala, including the territories of the Zamorin of Calicut.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Arakkal vs Calicut (Zamorin), Kolathunad, Cochin, Travancore, East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Mysore's quarter-century in Kerala ends with Malabar ceded to the Company in 1792
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 248: 'By the treaties of Seringapatam ... Tipu formally ceded Malabar to the British ... Thus the Mysorean attempts for about a quarter of a century to establish hegemony over Kerala ultimately ended only in the establishment of British supremacy.'

events.text: Battle of Changama: the first action of the First Anglo-Mysore War (2 September 1767) — Colonel Smith meets the combined army of Haidar and Nizam Ali at the Changama pass.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Hyderabad
events.outcome: Inconclusive — HCIP: Smith 'won a nominal victory ... It was on the whole a very indecisive affair'; the confederates got into the Karnatak regardless
events.commanders: Joseph Smith — Haidar Ali, Nizam Ali
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 458: 'In the first battle of the war, Colonel Smith won a nominal victory over Haidar Ali and Nizam Ali at Changama. It was on the whole a very indecisive affair.' Hayavadana Rao III synopsis (block 27) and index p. 47: 'the action at Changama, September 2, 1767'.

events.text: Battle of Maonda and Mandholi: The Battle of Maonda and Mandholi was fought between the Rajput rulers of Jaipur and the Jat rulers of Bharatpur in 1767 in Rajasthan.
events.belligerents: Jaipur vs Bharatpur
events.outcome: Jaipur victory; the Jat army fled at the first shock and abandoned its artillery and baggage, though Sombre's and Madec's battalions saved Jawahir Singh — who claimed a 'most Pyrrhic victory'
events.commanders: Madho Singh — Jawahar Singh
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 478-479: 'the Jaipur horse... at last threw themselves sword in hand on the Jat army, which fled away at the first shock... Jawahir had saved himself and the men of his army and claimed the victory; but it was a most Pyrrhic victory... Madho Singh followed up his success'. BOOKS DISAGREE: HCIP VIII chronology p. 832: '1767, December 14 Jawahir Singh wins a pyrrhic victory over Jaipur troops in the battle of Maonda'

events.text: Battle of Tiruvannamalai: on 26 September 1767 Smith defeats the Mysore–Hyderabad army at Trinomalee; soon after, Nizam Ali leaves the war and makes terms with the Company.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Hyderabad
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Nizam Ali withdraws from the war
events.commanders: Joseph Smith — Haidar Ali, Nizam Ali
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 458: 'The next engagement was at Trinomali, where also the confederates were defeated. Thereupon Nizam Ali withdrew from the conflict.' Hayavadana Rao III synopsis (block 27): 'The action at Tiruvannamalai, September 26, 1767'.

events.text: Fall of Kirtipur: after failing in 1757 and 1764, Prithvi Narayan Shah’s Gorkhas take the hill town guarding Kathmandu in 1767, opening the Valley to conquest.
events.belligerents: Nepal (Gorkha, Prithvi Narayan Shah) vs Malla (Kathmandu Valley)
events.outcome: Nepal victory; Kirtipur surrenders and its defenders are mutilated in reprisal
events.commanders: Prithvi Narayan Shah, Surapratap Shah — Jaya Prakash Malla’s garrison
events.source: web-only; library silent on Nepal’s unification (HCIP IX p. 235 only notes 'the newly founded Gurkha kingdom of Nepal which extended from Sikkim to the borders of Kashmir'). Famous and uncontested; it matters because it opened the Kathmandu Valley.

events.text: First Anglo-Mysore War
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 457-458: Haidar 'won the Nizam over and persuaded him to join an offensive alliance against the British ... The panick-stricken Madras Government was induced to sign a treaty on 4 April, 1769'. Rao III p. 141 is more guarded: the treaty 'gave away more than what it secured for Mysore'.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Hyderabad
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Haidar appears before Madras and the Company accepts the Treaty of Madras (April 1769) on mutual restitution and a defensive alliance
events.commanders: East India Company commanders; Peshwa Madhavrao I; Nizam Ali Khan; Nawab Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah — Hyder Ali of Mysore

events.text: Siege of Ambur: The siege of Ambur was conducted by a combined force of Mysorean and Hyderabadi troops under the command of Hyder Ali against the town of Ambur in southern India.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab) vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Hyderabad
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Calvert's garrison holds until Smith's relief on 7 December 1767
events.commanders: Harry Calvert — Hyder Ali
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. ~62-63 (blocks 79-80): 'the frequent sallies that Captain Calvert, with his 500 sepoys ... made from the fort, prevented him from attempting to take it by storm ... the British colours still flying on the morning of the 7th of December'.

events.text: Sikh conquest of Rawalpindi (1767): The Sikh conquest of Rawalpindi (1767) was the occupation of Rawalpindi by forces of Gujjar Singh Bhangi during the winter of 1767.
events.belligerents: Bhangi Misl vs Gakhars, Awans, Janjuas
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Gujjar Singh Bhangi, Sahib Singh Bhangi, Milkha Singh Thepuria — Sultan Muqarrab Khan of Pharwala, Karmullah Khan of Dhani, Mansur Khan of Gheb
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Dhodap: Madhavrao I defeats his uncle Raghunathrao and Govindrao Gaekwad's contingent at Dhodap on 10 June 1768. Raghunathrao is captured and held in the Shaniwar Wada.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Peshwa Madhavrao I) vs Raghunathrao's faction and Govindrao Gaekwad
events.outcome: Peshwa Madhavrao I victory; Raghunathrao taken captive, Govindrao Gaekwad taken prisoner
events.commanders: Peshwa Madhavrao I — Raghunathrao, Govindrao Gaekwad
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 204: 'battle was fought and won by the Peshwa on June 10, 1768. The fort was captured. Raghunath was taken to Poona and confined in the Shaniwar Wada'; p. 284: 'At the battle of Dhodap in 1768, a Gaikwar contingent under Damaji's son Govind Rao, fought against the Peshwa and was defeated.'

events.text: Battle of Ooscota: Battle of Ooscota was a military engagement fought during the First Anglo-Mysore War, in which the Marathas intervened to aid the British.
events.belligerents: Murari Rao of Gooty, East India Company vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: Murari Rao victory — Haidar's night attack on Murari's camp at Hoskote (24 August 1768) beaten off, and Haidar withdraws his cavalry
events.commanders: Murari Rao — Hyder Ali
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 77-78: 'On the night of the 24th, Haidar made a disposition for the attack of Murari's camp ... he did not think proper to renew the attack, and withdrew his cavalry. While Haidar's loss in this injudicious attempt was not inconsiderable'. (Wilks dates it 22 Aug, Robson 24 Aug.)

events.text: Conquest of the Kathmandu Valley: Prithvi Narayan Shah enters Kathmandu during Indra Jatra (September 1768), then takes Patan and Bhaktapur (1769), ending Malla rule and making Kathmandu the Gorkha capital.
events.belligerents: Nepal (Gorkha, Prithvi Narayan Shah) vs Malla (Kathmandu Valley)
events.outcome: Nepal victory; the three Malla kingdoms fall and Nepal is unified under the Shah dynasty
events.commanders: Prithvi Narayan Shah — Jaya Prakash Malla, Tej Narsingh Malla, Ranjit Malla
events.source: web-only; library silent (HCIP IX p. 235 notes only 'the newly founded Gurkha kingdom of Nepal'). Famous and uncontested (1768–69); it is the founding of the Nepal the atlas shows.

events.text: Damaji Gaekwad dies — the ablest of the Gaekwads, who expelled the Mughal nawabs and brought nearly all of Gujarat under Maratha rule.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 284: 'Damaji died on 18 August, 1768 ... By far he was the ablest of the Gaikwar family. He brought practically the whole of Gujarat, including Kathiawar under his rule'.

events.text: Jawahir Singh dies — Assassinated, the son of Suraj Mal who besieged Delhi and fought Jaipur at Maonda; his death began the decline of Bharatpur.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 832: '1768, July Jawahir Singh Jat is assassinated (p. 219).'; Sarkar III p. 2: 'When Jawahir Singh’s tempestuous career ended in an appropriately violent death (June 1768)' (month differs)

events.text: Maratha siege of Udaipur: hired by the pretender Ratan Singh against Maharana Ari Singh II, Mahadji Sindhia (joined briefly by Tukoji Holkar) sat down before Udaipur in May 1769, then dropped the pretender and sold peace to the Rana for 64 lakhs.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia), Holkar (Indore State) vs Udaipur (Mewar)
events.outcome: Scindia and Holkar victory; the Rana buys off the siege with an indemnity settled at 64 lakhs
events.commanders: Mahadji Sindhia, Tukoji Holkar — Ari Singh II
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 519: 'Early in May 1769, Mahadji Sindhia marched from Ujjain to Udaipur in order to back the cause of Ratan Singh'; p. 520: 'it was reported from Mahadji's camp that the contribution from Udaipur had been settled at 64 lakhs.' Sarkar (p. 518) rejects Tod's story of a battle on the Sipra near Ujjain in January 1769.

events.text: Moamoria rebellion: The Moamoria rebellion (1769–1805) was an 18th-century uprising in the Ahom kingdom of present-day Assam that began as a power struggle involving the Moamorias (Mataks).
events.belligerents: Moamarias (Mataks) vs Ahom Kingdom
events.outcome: Severe weakening of the Ahom kingdom; near-end of the Paik system.
events.commanders: Ragha Moran Ramananda Naharkhora Saikia Govinda Gaonburha Pitambardev Sarbananda Singha Bharath Singha — Sunyeophaa Suhitpangphaa Suklingphaa Ghanashyam Burhagohain Purnanada Burhagohain Kirti Chandra Borbarua
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: The Treaty of Kanakapur: Madhavrao I, with the Nizam as his ally, plunders Nagpur and Berar. On 23 March 1769 Janoji Bhonsle submits, gives up territory worth 8 lakhs and agrees to serve as a loyal vassal.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 204: 'The Peshwa plundered Nagpur, captured several forts and ravaged Berar. Peace was concluded at Kanakapur (at the confluence of the Manjra and the Godavari) on 23 March, 1769. Janoji Bhosle surrendered territories worth 8 lakhs and agreed to perform the duties of a loyal vassal.'

events.text: The Treaty of Madras: after a dash of 130 miles in three and a half days, Haidar camps at St Thomas' Mount and the Madras Government signs peace on 3–4 April 1769 — mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 458: 'he appeared before the gates of Madras. The panick-stricken Madras Government was induced to sign a treaty on 4 April, 1769, that provided for mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance.' Hayavadana Rao III p. 107: 'on the 3rd April, a treaty was executed ... that there should be perpetual peace and friendship' (Rao, p. 109 n.: Haidar signed on the 4th).

events.text: Battle of Sonkh: hired by Ranjit Singh in the Jat succession war, the Marathas under Ramchandra Ganesh and Mahadji Sindhia defeat the Bharatpur raja Nawal Singh near Sonkh (6 April 1770) — the first blow in the decline of Jat power.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Ranjit Singh (Jat claimant) vs Bharatpur (Nawal Singh)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Nawal Singh defeated
events.commanders: Ramchandra Ganesh, Mahadji Sindhia — Nawal Singh
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 833: '1770, April 6 The Marathas defeat Nawal Singh, Jat ruler, near Sonkh (p. 220)'; Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III contents: 'Marathas hired by Ranjit, 8—Nawal S. defeated at Sonkh, 9'

events.text: Najib-ud-Daula dies — Near Hapur on 31 October 1770; the Rohilla foot-soldier who rose to rule Delhi as regent for a decade and helped Abdali win Panipat.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire II p. 415: 'He had only reached the district of Hapur, when death overtook him on 31 October... Thus ended the career of the most powerful personality in India during these ten years.'

events.text: Raid of Panipat (1770): The Raid of Panipat (1770) was a raid on 4 January 1770 by the Sikh forces led by Jassa Singh Ahluwalia against the Mughal forces led by Zabita Khan.
events.belligerents: Dal Khalsa vs Kingdom of Rohilkhand, Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Indecisive
events.commanders: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Baghel Singh — Najib ad-Dawlah, Zabita Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

HCIP VIII p. 357: 'one of the worst tragedies of human history befell Bengal. This was the Bengal famine of 1770 in which nearly a third of the population is said to have been swept away. The absence of a government, properly speaking, and the action of self-seeking men in cornering grains, intensified the severity of the famine.' (Chronology p. 833: '1769-70 A terrible famine visits Bengal'.) The 'ten million' figure attributed to Hastings is web-only.
events.text: The Bengal famine of 1770: Failed rains in 1768-69 and the Company’s revenue demand together kill perhaps a third of the population of Bengal and Bihar - the figure of ten million is Hastings’s own.

Battle of Moti Talav (Chinkurali): Trimbak Rao catches Haidar's retreating army in the hills eleven miles from Srirangapatna; an exploding tumbril sets off a panic and the Maratha horse cut the square to pieces. Haidar and Tipu barely escape.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Haidar loses his artillery, stores and equipment, but Srirangapatna holds
events.commanders: Trimbak Rao Pethe — Haidar Ali, Tipu
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 187-188 (blocks 183-184): 'The action at Chinkurli ... March 6 ... The rest was a scene of unresisted slaughter at the hands of the enemy's Pindaris'. HCIP VIII p. 456: 'defeated Haidar completely in the battle of Chinkurli or Moti Talao on 5 March, 1771 ... Haidar lost his entire equipment'. Dates differ: Rao 6 March; HCIP p. 423/456 5 March, p. 213 7 March 1771.

events.text: Capture of Delhi (1771): In 1771, the forces of the Maratha Empire led by Mahadaji Shinde captured Delhi from the Rohillas and installed the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II on the throne of Delhi.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Najib-ud-Daula (Rohilla)
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Zabita Khan, René-Marie Madec, Walter Reinhardt — Mahadji Scindia, Visaji Krushna, Mirza Najaf Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 833: '1771, February 10 Mahadji Sindia captures Delhi and requests Shah Alam to return to his capital (pp. 221, 255, 367).'; Sarkar III contents: 'Delhi captured by Marathas 1771, 29'

events.text: Ahmad Shah Durrani dies — founder of the Afghan empire, eight times invader of India and victor of Panipat, at Murgha in the hills near Qandahar.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 400: 'Here he died at Murgha on 14 April, 1772.' Footnote: 'Some writers place Ahmad Shah's death in June, 1773 ... Delhi Chronicle, p. 250, says that Ahmad Shah Durrani died on April 14, 1772.' (Coordinates: Qandahar, where he is buried; Murgha itself is not located in the book.)

events.text: Battle of the Purana Qila: when Shah Alam II defies them over Zabita Khan, the Marathas under Visaji Krishna and Tukoji Holkar defeat the imperial army of Najaf Khan and Madec below the Old Fort of Delhi (17 December 1772); the emperor submits, makes Zabita Mir Bakhshi and grants them Kora and Allahabad.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the imperialists shut up in Delhi and the emperor forced to accept Maratha terms
events.commanders: Visaji Krishna, Tukoji Holkar — Mirza Najaf Khan, René Madec, Hisam-ud-daulah
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 69: '§15. Battle of Purana Qila... the decisive engagement came off on Friday the 17th of December... superior generalship, even more than superior numbers, decided the issue against him'; p. 73: 'But it was decisive.'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 834: '1772, December The Marathas (Holkar and Visaji Krishna) compel Shah Alam II to confer the office of Mir Bakshi on Zabita Khan'

events.text: Madhavrao I dies — At Theur, of consumption, aged twenty-seven; the Peshwa who rebuilt Maratha power after Panipat.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 222: 'Madhav Rao died a premature death on 18 November, 1772.' (Theur and the cause of death remain web-only.)

events.text: Ram Mohan Roy is born — At Radhanagar in Hooghly; the reformer of the Brahmo Samaj.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: Siege of Kunjpura (1772): The siege of Kunjpura was a 14-day siege in April to May 1772 by Sikh forces led by Sahib Singh against the Mughal coalition forces led by Mughal Ali Khan.
events.belligerents: Dal Khalsa vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Baghel Singh, Sahib Singh, Dyal Singh Majithia — Mughal Ali Khan, Dilawar Ali Khan, Sheikh Kabir
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Barsana: Mirza Najaf Khan's new-model imperial army, the first in Upper India to face European-trained sepoys on both sides, destroys the Jat army of Nawal Singh and Sombre between Sahar and Barsana (30 October 1773); Kotban falls and Agra is recovered for the emperor.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire (Mirza Najaf Khan) vs Bharatpur (Nawal Singh, Sombre's battalions)
events.outcome: Mughal Empire victory; decisive defeat of the Jat army, Nawal Singh fled
events.commanders: Mirza Najaf Khan, Najaf Quli Khan — Nawal Singh, Walter Reinhardt 'Sombre'
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 98-101: '§6. Battle before Barsana; Jat disaster. Fall of Kotban. After skirmishes for ten days, the decisive battle was fought on 30th October, midway between Sahar and Barsana'; p. 101 running head 'Decisive defeat of Jat army'

events.text: Capture of Thanjavur (1773): a Company army takes Tanjore on 17 September 1773 and hands it to Nawab Muhammad Ali; Raja Tulaji is deposed until the Directors order his restoration in April 1776.
events.belligerents: Carnatic (Arcot Nawab), East India Company vs Thanjavur (Maratha)
events.outcome: Carnatic victory; Tanjore annexed to the Nawab's dominions until restored to Tulaji on 11 April 1776
events.commanders: Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah, Company officers — Raja Tulaji
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 39 n. (block 31; running head of p. 40 follows the note): 'It was seized by Md. Ali on 17th September 1773 and restored to Raja Tulaji on 11th April 1776 by a special order from the Authorities in England.' Hayavadana Rao II p. 657: 'Tanjore was taken and given to Muhammad Ali in 1773'.

events.text: Peshwa Narayanrao murdered — killed at Poona in a plot laid by his uncle Raghunathrao. The ministers then formed the Barbhai regency against Raghunathrao.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 256: 'Narayan Rao ... was murdered in August 1773. It was soon discovered that his uncle Raghunath and his wife were the prime movers behind the plot'; chronology p. 834: '1773, August 30'.

events.text: The Company expels the Bhutanese from Cooch Behar: after Bhutan carries off the Cooch Behar raja (1772), a small Company force drives the Bhutanese out and takes the fort of Buxa; Cooch Behar accepts Company protection.
events.belligerents: East India Company and Cooch Behar vs Bhutan (Deb Raja)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Bhutanese driven from Cooch Behar and Buxa taken
events.commanders: Captain John Jones — Deb Raja Zhidar
events.source: HCIP IX p. 1020: 'In 1772, the Bhutanese invaded Cooch Behar and carried off the Raja ... The Cooch Behar ruling family solicited British aid. A small British force drove the Bhutanese out of Cooch Behar and captured the fort of Buxa.' (The 1773 date of the fighting is from its sequence; the book gives only 1772 for the invasion.)

events.text: British capture of Thana: on 28 December 1774 a Bombay expedition seizes Thana on Salsette from the Marathas, without authority from Calcutta. It is the opening move of the first Anglo-Maratha war.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Thana and Salsette captured
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 52: 'Thana was captured on 28th December ... according to which the capture of Thana was unauthorized.'

events.text: Hafiz Rahmat Khan dies — Regent of the Rohillas, killed fighting at Miranpur Katra as Awadh and the Company conquered Rohilkhand.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 118: 'The decisive battle was fought at Miranpur Katra six days later. Hafiz Rahmat Khan was killed fighting bravely.'

events.text: Rohilla War: Awadh, backed by the British, annexes Rohilkhand — Hafiz Rahmat Khan is killed at Miranpur Katra (23 April 1774)
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 118: 'The combined forces of Shuja-ud-daulah and the English marched into Rohilkhand on 17 April, 1774. The decisive battle was fought at Miranpur Katra six days later. Hafiz Rahmat Khan was killed fighting bravely... their province became a part of the Awadh kingdom.'
events.belligerents: Awadh, East India Company vs Rohilkhand (Rohillas)
events.outcome: Awadh–Company victory — the Rohilla country annexed

events.text: The first Anglo-Bhutan treaty (25 April 1774): on the Panchen Lama’s intercession Hastings makes peace with the Deb Raja; Bhutan’s tribute for Falakata passes to the Company and Bhutanese caravans may trade duty-free to Rangpur.
events.source: HCIP IX p. 1020: 'As a result of his intercession a treaty was made between the Government of India and Bhutan on 25th April, 1774. The tribute of five Tangan horses, which had been paid by Bhutan to the Cooch Behar Raja for the province of Falakata, was transferred to the East India Company.'

events.text: Bajirao II born — son of Raghunathrao, the last Peshwa.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III, chronology to ch. III (block 48 of the archive.org text, between printed pp. 59 and 65): '1775, Jan. 10 ... Raghunathrao's son Bajirao born.' HCIP VIII p. 488 has him installed 'at the age of twenty-one on December 5, 1796'.

events.text: Battle of Adas (Anand Mogri): on 17 February 1775 the Barbhai regency's army under Haripant Phadke routs the ex-Peshwa Raghunathrao and Govindrao Gaekwad near Wasad on the Mahi. Raghunathrao flees to Surat and the English.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Barbhai regency) vs Raghunathrao's faction and Govindrao Gaekwad
events.outcome: Maratha Empire victory; Raghunathrao's army utterly routed, his artillery and standard taken
events.commanders: Haripant Phadke — Raghunathrao, Govindrao Gaekwad
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III pp. 49–50: 'Haripant waited till the 17th February, when a severe action was fought in which the stars rewarded Haripant with victory. R'rao's army was utterly routed'; note: 'This battle is variously known after the several villages of the region, Napar, Anand-mogri and Adas'. HCIP VIII p. 286: 'defeated at Anand Mogri near Aras on 17 February, 1775'. (A second action on nearly the same field, 18/28 May 1775, Sardesai III p. 51 calls 'not decisive for either party'; that is the one usually called 'Arras'.)

events.text: Battle of Pachgaon: The Battle of Pachgaon was fought on 26 January 1775 for accession to the throne of the Nagpur Kingdom in central India.
events.belligerents: Sabaji Bhonsle vs Mudhoji Bhonsle
events.outcome: Mudhoji Bhonsle victory; Sabaji Bhonsle killed
events.commanders: Sabaji Bhonsle — Mudhoji Bhonsle Muhammad Yusuf Gardi
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 835: '1775, January 26 The battle of Panchgaon fought between Mudhoji Bhosle and Sabaji Bhosle in which Sabaji is killed.'

events.text: Battle of Pathankot (1775): The Battle of Pathankot, also known as the Battle of Dinanagar, took place in 1775 near Awankha in pargana Dina Nagar.
events.belligerents: Kanhaiya Misl, Sukerchakia Misl, Ahluwalia Misl vs Bhangi Misl, Ramgarhia Misl, Dogra Flag of Jammu and Kashmir Jammu
events.outcome: Near collapse of the Bhangi Misl
events.commanders: Jai Singh Kanhaiya, Haqiqat Singh Kanhaiya, Jassa Singh Ahluwalia — Ganda Singh Bhangi, Charat Singh Bhangi, Gujjar Singh Bhangi
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: First Anglo-Maratha War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs East India Company
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Maratha leadership under Madhavrao II, Nana Fadnavis and Mahadji Scindia — Warren Hastings; British EIC commanders including Goddard and Popham

events.text: Maharaja Nandakumar is hanged at Calcutta — The former diwan who accused Warren Hastings of taking bribes was tried for forgery by the new Supreme Court and executed.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 374: 'Nandkumar was tried by the Supreme Court, and a jury entirely consisting of Eurasian inhabitants of Calcutta under English law which was of doubtful application at the time in India, and was sentenced to death on the charge.' HCIP VIII chronology p. 835: '1775, May Nandkumar executed on forgery charges' (the hanging is usually dated 5 August 1775).

events.text: Prithvi Narayan Shah dies — The Gorkha king who conquered the Kathmandu Valley (1768–69) and founded unified Nepal; he died at Nuwakot in January 1775.
events.source: web-only; library silent on Prithvi Narayan Shah. Famous and uncontested; the founder of the Nepal state the atlas shows.

events.text: Shuja-ud-Daula dies — Nawab-Wazir of Awadh, Abdali's ally at Panipat and the Company's enemy at Buxar; after him Awadh became 'a dependency of the East India Company'.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 119: 'Shuja-ud-daulah died on 26 January, 1775, and was succeeded by his eldest son Asaf-ud-daulah. Awadh, for all practical purposes, became a dependency of the East India Company.'

events.text: The Treaty of Surat: on 6 March 1775 Raghunathrao buys Bombay's military help to regain the Peshwaship. He promises to cede Bassein, Salsette and other islands, and parts of Gujarat. The treaty sets off the first Anglo-Maratha war.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 286: 'At Surat Raghunath Rao concluded a treaty with the English on 6 March, 1775 ... and to cede in perpetuity Bassein with its dependencies, Salsette and other islands, the districts of Jambusar, Olpad and part of Ankalesar.'

events.text: Battle of Saunshi: The Battle of Saunshi was fought between the Kingdom of Mysore and the Maratha Empire in 1777.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Haidar's general Muhammad Ali routs the Marathas at Saunshi
events.commanders: Konher Rao, Padurang Rao — Hyder Ali, Muhammad Ali
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 247-248: 'came up with the Mahrattas at Saunsi (ten miles north of Savanur) and found them drawn up to offer him battle'; index: 'opposes and puts to rout the Mahrattas at Saunsi (Nov. 1776), 247-248'. The row's 1777 comes from Wikipedia.

events.text: Fall of Dig: Najaf Khan starves the great Jat fortress of Dig; Ranjit Singh flees on the night of 29 April 1776, the fort and city are sacked, and the Jat state is reduced to Bharatpur and a few districts.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire (Mirza Najaf Khan) vs Bharatpur (Ranjit Singh)
events.outcome: Mughal Empire victory; Dig taken after six weeks' blockade, the last defenders of the citadel killed
events.commanders: Mirza Najaf Khan, Himmat Bahadur — Ranjit Singh
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 125: '§ 15. Fall of Dig. In six weeks famine completed its work in that crowded den. Finally, in the night of 29th April 1776, Ranjit Singh himself fled away with the remnant of his troops'; HCIP VIII p. 160 places the final submission at Bharatpur c. February 1778

events.text: The Treaty of Purandar: Calcutta repudiates the Surat treaty and makes peace with the Poona regency in March 1776. Bombay does not honour it, and war resumes in 1778.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 835: '1776, March Treaty of Purandhar to secure a general peace between the E.I. Company and the Marathas.' p. 286: the Supreme Government 'declared the treaty concluded with Raghoba (Raghunath Rao) invalid and the Maratha war as impolitic, dangerous, unauthorized and unjust'.

events.text: Mir Qasim dies — The able Nawab of Bengal (1760–63) who tried to rule free of the Company, lost at Buxar and died a wanderer near Delhi.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 349: 'he was allowed to escape from the battle-field, led a wandering life for some years till he met with his end near Delhi in 1777. Thus ended the last efforts of a Bengal prince to maintain his independence of English control.'

events.text: Siege of Nargund (1778): The siege of Nargund took place in 1778 when troops from the Sultanate of Mysore attempted to capture the town of Nargund, a possession of the Maratha Confederacy.
events.belligerents: Maratha Confederacy vs Mysore
events.outcome: Mysore victory
events.commanders: Vyankatrao Bhave — Hyder Ali
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Pondicherry (1778): on news of the Anglo-French war, Munro besieges the French capital from 8 August; it falls on 18 October, and the Company moves on Mahe — the step that drives Haidar into the Second Mysore War.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs French India
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Pondicherry surrenders in October 1778
events.commanders: Sir Hector Munro — French garrison
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. ~309 (block 285): 'Pondicherry, held by the French, was besieged by the English (8th August to 18th October 1778). On the fall of Pondicherry in October'.

events.text: Siege of Rasulnagar: The Conquest of Rasulnagar, also known as the Siege of Rasulnagar, was led by Maha Singh of the Sukerchakia Misl, with support from Jai Singh of the Kanhaiya Misl.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl, Kanhaiya Misl vs Chattha tribe
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Maha Singh, Jai Singh Kanhaiya — Pir Muhammad Chattha
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Abdul Ahad's Patiala campaign: Abdul Ahad's Patiala campaign was a Mughal expedition led by Abdul Ahad Khan Majd-ud-Daulah with Prince Mirza Jahan Shah Farkhunda Bakht against the Cis-Satluj Sikh chiefs.
events.belligerents: Mughal Empire, Sikh auxiliaries vs Patiala State, Trans-Satluj Sikhs
events.outcome: Patiala–Sikh victory
events.commanders: Mughal Commanders:, Abdul Ahad Khan Majd-ud-Daulah, Prince Mirza Jahan Shah Farkhunda Bakht — Cis-Sutlej Sikhs:, Amar Singh of Patiala, Maha Singh
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Rohtas (1779): The Battle of Rohtas took place somewhere in December 1779, between Timur Shah Durrani and the Bhangi Misl.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Bhangi Misl
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Timur Shah Durrani, Zangi Khan — Unknown
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Wadgaon: The Battle of Wadgaon was fought between the Maratha Confederacy and the British East India Company near Vadgaon Maval village in Maharashtra.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs East India Company
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Bombay army advancing on Poona with Raghunathrao was surrounded near Wadgaon and signed the Convention of Wadgaon (16 January 1779), agreeing to surrender Raghunathrao and give up Salsette
events.commanders: Mahadji Scindia, Nana Phadnavis — Colonel Cockburn, John Carnac (Bombay committee)
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 256: 'The English force ... was almost overwhelmed, and concluded on 16 January, 1779, the convention of Wadgaon, agreeing to the surrender of Raghunath Rao, evacuation of Salsette and other islands ... Mahadji Sindia was the architect of this debacle of English arms at Wadgaon.'

events.text: Siege of Chitradurga: Haidar's second siege of the Nayaka fortress (1778–79) ends when the Jarimale chiefs and the fort's Muslim corps go over to him; the Palegar Madakari (Medekere) Nayaka is taken and the state annexed (the Obavva story belongs to this siege).
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs Chitradurga (Nayaka)
events.outcome: Mysore victory; the fort capitulates in March 1779 and Chitradurga is annexed
events.commanders: Haidar Ali — Madakari Nayaka
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 259-260 (blocks 243-244): 'the fort, overwhelmed by the superior numbers of the Mysore military, capitulated at last in March 1779'.

events.text: Siege of Patiala (1779): The siege of Patiala was a 7-day siege fought between the Sikh forces led by Raja Amar Singh and Mughal forces led by Abdul Ahad Khan.
events.belligerents: Patiala vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Patiala-Sikh victory
events.commanders: Raja Amar Singh, Tara Singh Ghaiba, Jassa Singh Ahluwalia — Abdul Ahad Khan, Prince Farkhunda Bakht
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Tellicherry: The siege of Tellicherry was a military embargo that happened in Thalassery.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Kottayam vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), Kolathunad, Kadathanad
events.outcome: East India Company victory; relieved by Abington in 1781, Tellicherry holds, and Mahe is retaken on 9 January 1782
events.commanders: Major John Cotgrave, Major William Abington, Pazhassi Raja — Sardar Ali Khan Sahib
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 246: 'the troops of Sirdar Khan laid siege to Tellicherry both from sea and land (October 1780). The siege lasted for 18 months ... Tellicherry was saved and Mahe was recaptured on 9th January 1782.'

C. Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III pp. 333-337 (narrative of Perambakam, 10 Sept 1780) and p. 591 (block 516): 'intercepted by Haidar when on the point of junction at Perambakam, and annihilated (10th September)'
events.text: Battle of Pollilur: Haidar Ali and Tipu intercept Colonel Baillie’s column at Perambakam, marching from Guntur to join Munro at Conjeeveram, "and annihilated" it on 10 September; the worst defeat the Company had yet suffered in India. Munro fell back on Madras. Hayavadana Rao III p. 516.
events.belligerents: Mysore (Haidar Ali, Tipu Sultan) vs East India Company (Baillie, Munro)
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Baillie’s force destroyed and its survivors taken to Srirangapatna

events.text: Battle of Shujabad (1780): The Battle of Shujabad took place in February 1780, during the Afghan–Sikh Wars.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Sikh Misls
events.outcome: Afghan victory
events.commanders: Timur Shah Durrani, Muzaffar Khan — Jassa Singh, Gujjar Singh Bhangi, Haqiqat Singh Kanhaiya
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Capture of Gwalior (1780): in the first Anglo-Maratha war, Captain Popham escalades and surprises Mahadji Sindhia's fortress of Gwalior on 3 August 1780 — an exploit Hastings called nearly equal to Plassey.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Gwalior fort taken by surprise
events.commanders: William Popham — Sindhia's garrison
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 256: 'Col. Popham surprised the fort of Gwalior on 3 August, 1780 and Hastings called it the most gallant enterprise nearly equal in its advantage to the battle of Plassey.'

events.text: Ranjit Singh is born — son of Mahan Singh, chief of the Sukerchakia misl; usually placed at Gujranwala on 13 November 1780, but Gupta argues for 13 December 1780 (2 Maghar) at Badrukhan in Jind, his mother's home.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs V p. 6: '2nd Maghar fell on 13 December, 1780, which is the correct date of Ranjit Singh's birth'; pp. 6–7: 'It is generally believed that Ranjit Singh was born in his father's home at Gujranwala. This assertion is against facts ... Atar Singh Bhadauria ... says that "Ranjit Singh was born in Pind Badrukhan".'

events.text: Second Anglo-Mysore War
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 457-461.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), French India vs East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
events.outcome: Inconclusive — Treaty of Mangalore (11 March 1784): mutual restitution of conquests and prisoners, a peace Englishmen 'regarded ... as humiliating'
events.commanders: Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan of Mysore — British EIC commanders including Eyre Coote; Warren Hastings; Maratha participation/alliance varies by phase

events.text: Siege of Arcot (1780): after destroying Baillie, Haidar renews the siege of the Nawab's capital on 19 September; Arcot capitulates in November and the Payanghat is overrun.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs East India Company, Carnatic (Arcot Nawab)
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Arcot capitulates (November 1780)
events.commanders: Haidar Ali, Tipu — Company and Nawab's garrison
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 300-301 chapter synopsis (block 278): 'Haidar's movements ; renews the siege of Arcot, September 19, 1780; capitulation of Arcot, November 28, 1780 ; reduction of the Karnatic-Payanghat' (the vol. synopsis at block 9 reads 'November 23').

events.text: Siege of Bassein (1780): Goddard besieges Bassein from November 1780, and Visaji Pant surrenders it in December. The Maratha relief commander, Ramchandra Ganesh, is killed the same day.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Bassein surrendered
events.commanders: General Thomas Goddard, Colonel Hartley — Visaji Pant, Ramchandra Ganesh
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 107: 'the garrison was so hard-pressed that Visaji Pant surrendered Bassein to Goddard on 12 December. It was a severe blow to Maratha pride'. Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 222 gives 'Goddard took Bassein on 11th December'. The two books differ by a day.

events.text: Siege of Vellore: The siege of Vellore was an intermittent series of sieges and blockades conducted during the Second Anglo-Mysore War by forces of the Kingdom of Mysore.
events.belligerents: British East India Company vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Unknown — Hyder Ali
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Storming of Ahmedabad (1780): General Goddard and Fateh Singh Gaekwad, allied by the treaty of Kandila, take Ahmedabad by assault on 15 February 1780 and hand it to the Gaekwad.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Fateh Singh Gaekwad vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Ahmedabad taken by assault
events.commanders: General Thomas Goddard, Fateh Singh Gaekwad — the Peshwa's garrison
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 286: 'the allies marched on Ahmadabad and took it by assault on 15 February, 1780, whereupon it was delivered to Fateh Singh.' Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 222: 'Goddard captured Ahmadabad on 15th Feb. 1780'.

events.text: Action near Sipri: after being surprised at Kolaras in March, Mahadji Sindhia harries Camac's and Muir's column and defeats it near Sipri (Shivpuri) on 1 July 1781, leading to the truce of October 1781 and the Treaty of Salbai.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia) vs East India Company
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Company force defeated near Sipri, truce on 'no gain, no loss' terms in October
events.commanders: Mahadji Sindhia — Col. Camac, Col. Muir
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 257: 'Sindia improved his position by constantly harassing the enemy’s flanks and inflicting a defeat on 1 July, near Sipri. On 13 October, 1781 a temporary truce was effected between Mahadji Sindia and Col. Muir on terms of no gain, no loss to either party.'

events.text: Battle of Porto Novo: on 1 July 1781 Eyre Coote turns Haidar's entrenched position on the coast and routs his army — the Company's first great recovery after Pollilur.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; 'Haidar's defeat was thus complete'
events.commanders: Eyre Coote, James Stuart — Haidar Ali, Tipu, Lally
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 356: 'in a quarter of an hour his whole army was dispersed ... Haidar's defeat was thus complete'. HCIP VIII p. 459: 'It was a great tactical victory for the British, but it had no important strategic effects.'

events.text: Battle of Sholinghur: Coote attacks Haidar's army posted in the Sholinghur pass on the Vellore road; after a heavy cannonade Haidar's army flees towards Kaveripak, and Vellore is relieved.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; 'Haidar's forces precipitately fled from the field'
events.commanders: Eyre Coote — Haidar Ali, Tipu, Lally
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. ~362 (block 331): 'by evening victory again declared for the English. Haidar's forces precipitately fled from the field of action towards Kaveripak' (Rao: 27 September 1781; HCIP VIII p. 459: 'Solingar (27 October)').

events.text: Goddard's Bor Ghat campaign: Goddard marches on Poona by the Bor Ghat and is held at Khandala by Haripant Phadke, the Patwardhans and Tukoji Holkar. After three months of harassment he retreats to Bombay with heavy losses.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs East India Company
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Goddard's army forced back to Bombay with about 3,000 killed and wounded
events.commanders: Haripant Phadke, Tukoji Holkar — General Goddard, Colonel Hartley
