events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 108: 'Constant skirmishing continued for three months, February to April, below the ghats, in which the Marathas inflicted several defeats and losses upon the enemy ... Goddard found himself isolated at Khandala ... went back to Bombay suffering severe losses ... three thousand men dead and wounded'.

events.text: Second Battle of Pollilur: Coote fights Haidar on the field of Baillie's disaster and forces him to retire.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Haidar's forces retreat from the field
events.commanders: Eyre Coote — Haidar Ali
events.source: Hayavadana Rao III index p. 1306 (block 1142): 'takes part in the battles of Pallilore (Aug. 27) and Sholinghur (Sept. 27) forcing Haidar's forces to retreat from the field, 360-363'. HCIP VIII p. 459: 'Coote defeated Haidar on two other occasions in the second battle of Pollilore (27 September)'. Dates differ: Rao 27 Aug, HCIP 27 Sept 1781.

events.text: Siege of Negapatam: The siege of Negapatam was the first major offensive military action on the Indian subcontinent following the arrival of news that war had been declared.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Great Britain vs Dutch Republic, 22x Sultanate of Mysore
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Hector Munro, Edward Hughes — Reynier van Vlissingen, 22x Hyder Ali
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Annagudi (Braithwaite's defeat): Tipu and Lally surround Colonel Braithwaite's detachment near Kumbakonam on 17–18 February 1782; after twenty-six hours of fighting it is destroyed and Braithwaite taken.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu), French India vs East India Company
events.outcome: Mysore victory; the English detachment 'completely defeated' and Braithwaite captured
events.commanders: Tipu, Lally — John Braithwaite
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 371: 'The action lasted for the space of twenty-six hours, when the English detachment was completely defeated'. HCIP VIII p. 459: 'Col. Braithwaite ... was surprised and cut down by an army led by Tipu. Braithwaite was taken prisoner.'

events.text: Haidar Ali dies — In his camp at Narasingarayanpet near Chittoor, on 7 December 1782, of a cancer; Tipu took the throne. Hayavadana Rao III p. 357.
events.source: C. Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 393-394 (block 357): 'Haidar breathed his last in his camp at Narasingarayanpet, near Chittoor, on the 7th of December 1782, at the age of sixty.' HCIP VIII p. 460: 'on 7 December, Haidar died'.

events.text: Mirza Najaf Khan dies — Regent of the empire and victor of Barsana and Dig; 'with him departed the last hope of the Mughals in India'.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 227: 'after lingering in bed for months the regent passed away on 6th April. With him departed the last hope of the Mughals in India.'; HCIP VIII p. 257: 'Mirza Najaf Khan, the emperor’s Regent, died on 6 April, 1782'

HCIP VIII p. 257: 'The temporary truce of 1781 was spelt out in a formal treaty of seventeen articles at Salbai on 17 May, 1782... Mahadji Sindia agreed to be “the mutual guarantee of both parties”... The English surrendered Raghunath Rao... and all the territories occupied by them except Salsette and two other islands near Bombay.'
events.text: The Treaty of Salbai: Mahadji Scindia mediates the peace that ends the first Anglo-Maratha war; the Company keeps Salsette, gives back everything else, and gets twenty years of peace with Poona.
Battle of Delhi
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Sikh Confederacy vs Mughal Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Sikh Confederacy leaders Baghel Singh, Jassa Singh Ahluwalia and Jassa Singh Ramgarhia — Shah Alam II / Mughal authorities at Delhi

events.text: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia dies — commander of the Dal Khalsa from 1748, the foremost Sikh chief of the misl age.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs IV p. 283: 'Jassa Singh Ahluwalia died in October, 1783.' p. 13: '[Kapur Singh] placed it [the Dal Khalsa] under the command of Jassa Singh Ahluwalia.' (Place not given; coordinates are his seat, Kapurthala.)

events.text: Maratha Conquest of Gwalior and Gohad: The Maratha conquest of Gwalior and Gohad is the military conflict between Maratha Confederacy and Kingdom of Gohad.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia) vs Gohad (Jat Ranas)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Mahadji Sindhia stormed Gwalior fort (31 July 1783) and seized Gohad and Rana Chhatra Singh (25–26 February 1784)
events.commanders: Mahadaji Scindia, Rane Khan, Ambaji Ingale — Rana Chatrajit
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 273: 'he had crushed his persistent rival in North Malwa, Rana Chhatra Singh of Gohad, by storming Gwalior fort (31 July 1783) and seizing Gohad and the Rana’s person (25 Feb. 1784.)'; HCIP VIII p. 258: 'Gwalior fort was reoccupied on 31 July, 1783 and Gohad was reduced on 26 February, 1784'

events.text: Raghunathrao dies — the ex-Peshwa (Raghoba), whose bid for the Peshwaship brought on the first Anglo-Maratha war.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 127: 'Raghunathrao returned to Kacheshvar in the vicinity of Kopargaum and there expired on 11 December 1783 at the age of 48.'

events.text: Siege of Bednore: The siege of Bednore was a battle of the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs East India Company
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Tipu invests Bednur and forces Mathews's army to capitulate
events.commanders: Richard Matthews — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 460: 'Tipu now advanced with his full force, invested Bednur and compelled the British to capitulate. It is said that safe conduct was promised to the British but Tipu violated the terms.'

events.text: Siege of Cuddalore: The siege of Cuddalore was a siege attempt by British troops against a combined French and Mysorean garrison at the fortress of Cuddalore in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Great Britain British East India Company Hanover vs Sultanate of Mysore, Kingdom of France
events.outcome: Inconclusive
events.commanders: James Stuart, Edward Hughes, Christoph August von Wangenheim — Marquis de Bussy-Castelnau, Bailli de Suffren, Sayed Sahib
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Mangalore: The siege of Mangalore was conducted during the Second Anglo-Mysore War by Tipu Sultan and forces of the Kingdom of Mysore against a British East India Company garrison.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs East India Company
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Campbell's garrison capitulates on 30 January 1784 and is shipped to Tellicherry
events.commanders: John Campbell — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 460: 'Tipu besieged Mangalore and the siege lasted from 20 May, 1783 to 30 January, 1784. Campbell, who defended the place capitulated on condition that the English garrison should be transported to Tellicherry.'

events.text: The Talpurs supplant the Kalhoras in Sindh: the Baluchi Talpur family ousted the Kalhora rulers and divided Sindh among branches at Hyderabad, Khairpur and Mirpur, nominally under the Durrani crown.
events.source: HCIP IX, British Paramountcy p. 202: 'At the end of the eighteenth century Sindh, nominally a part of the Durani kingdom in Afghanistan, was ruled by a Baluchi tribe called Talpuris who had ousted the Kaloras in 1783.'

events.text: Mahadji Sindhia made Regent of the Empire: at Halena on 4 December 1784 Shah Alam II appoints Mahadji Wakil-i-Mutlaq (Regent Plenipotentiary), having three days earlier named the Peshwa Naib-i-Munaib and Bakhshi-ul-mamalik with Sindhia as his permanent agent — Maratha control of the Delhi court.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 293-294: '§ 3. Mahadji Sindhia is created Commander-in-chief and Supreme Regent of the Empire... Here next day another darbar was held at which Shah Alam conferred on Mahadji Sindhia the highest possible post in the imperial Government, namely that of Regent Plenipotentiary (Wakil-i-mutlaq)'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 837: '1784, November Mahadji Sindia attains supreme power in Delhi'

events.text: The Bara Imambara of Lucknow: Asaf-ud-Daula’s famine-relief work, the vaulted hall unsupported by beams, with the labyrinth above it.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: The Treaty of Mangalore: after Mangalore's garrison capitulates, Macartney's Madras Government makes peace with Tipu on 11 March 1784 on mutual restitution of conquests and prisoners — a treaty Englishmen regarded as humiliating.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 460: 'There was to be a mutual restitution of conquests. The prisoners were to be restored. The Treaty was signed on 11 March, 1784.' p. 461: 'the Treaty of Mangalore and the treaty itself were regarded by Englishmen as humiliating'.

events.text: Battle of Achal: The Battle of Achal, also known as the Battle of Randpura, was fought in Achal, near Batala, in 1785 by the Sukerchakia Misl, Ramgarhia Misl and Sansar Chand.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl, Ramgarhia Misl, Kangra State vs Kanhaiya Misl
events.outcome: Sukerchakia-Allied victory
events.commanders: Maha Singh, Jassa Singh, Sansar Chand — Jai Singh, Gurbaksh Singh
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Maratha-Mysore War
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 461-462: 'The generally accepted opinion was that Tipu concluded a successful campaign by an inglorious peace. But Malet ... thought that the treaty was highly advantageous to Tipu.'
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Hyderabad vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: Inconclusive — Tipu won the field (Adoni, Savanur, Bahadur Benda) but by the Gajendragad peace (March 1787) he paid arrears of tribute, ceded Badami and restored Adoni, Kittur and Nargund; Malet thought the treaty 'highly advantageous to Tipu'
events.commanders: Peshwa Madhavrao II; Nana Fadnavis; Tukoji Holkar and Mahadji Scindia — Tipu Sultan of Mysore

events.text: Siege of Nargund (1785): The second siege of Nargund was a siege conducted by Tipu Sultan, the Sultan of Mysore, in Nargund in 1785.
events.belligerents: Maratha Confederacy vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: Mysore victory
events.commanders: Vyankatrao Bhave — Burhanudhin
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Savanur: The Battle of Savanur occurred between the Kingdom of Mysore and Maratha Empire.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Mysore vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Mysore victory
events.commanders: Tipu Sultan — Hari Pant
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Adoni: The siege of Adoni was a military conflict that occurred between the forces of Tipu Sultan of the Kingdom of Mysore and the Maratha Confederacy.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs Hyderabad, Maratha Empire
events.outcome: Mysore victory; the confederates relieve Adoni but then evacuate it, and it falls to Tipu
events.commanders: Raghunath Rao, Hari Pant, Arastu Jah — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 461: 'Tipu could not carry the place by assault and had to raise the siege as the confederates marched to its relief. But as no arrangements had been made for a prolonged campaign ... the confederates evacuated the place which fell into the hands of Tipu.'

events.text: Battle of Lalsot: The Battle of Tunga was a battle fought by the Rajput kingdoms of Jaipur and Jodhpur against the Marathas under Mahadji Scindia over the collection of taxes.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) vs Jaipur, Jodhpur (Marwar), Ismail Beg's Mughal troops
events.outcome: Inconclusive — the battle at Tunga (28 July 1787) 'had no decisive result' (Sarkar III p. 380), but the emperor's Hindustani battalions deserted Mahadji Sindhia and he retreated to Dig: 'almost a second Panipat' for him (HCIP VIII p. 260), a strategic success for Jaipur and Jodhpur
events.commanders: Mahadji Shinde, General de Boigne, Khande Rao Hari — Pratap Singh of Jaipur, Bhim Singh
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 380: 'Thus the battle of Tunga,—miscalled that of Lalsot,—"though sanguinary, had no decisive result."' p. 387: '§11. The retreat from Lalsot, 1-9 Aug. 1787.' Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 256: 'fought an indecisive pitched battle at Tunga (also called Lalsot) in July 1787. The Rajputs claimed it as a great victory ... Within a few days he retreated from the Jaipur territory.' HCIP VIII p. 260: 'The battle of Lalsot against Rajput combination turned out to be almost a second Panipat on account of the desertion of the emperor's Hindustani battalions ... He himself retreated to the protection of the Jat Raja's fortress of Dig.'

events.text: Siege of Bahadur Benda: The siege of Bahadur Benda occurred when the forces of Mysore led by Tipu Sultan besieged Bahadur fort in 1787.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: Mysore victory
events.commanders: Hari Pant — Tipu Sultan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Agra (1788): Rana Khan's Maratha–Jat army, with De Boigne's and Lesteneau's battalions, destroys Ismail Beg's army at Bagh Dehra outside Agra on 18 June 1788, after Ghulam Qadir has left him to defend his own Doab lands; Agra fort is relieved.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia), Bharatpur vs Mughal Empire (Ismail Beg)
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Ismail Beg's army 'ceased to exist as an instrument of war', he swam the Jamuna wounded
events.commanders: Rana Khan, Benoît de Boigne, Lesteneau — Ismail Beg
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 423-425: 'In the fateful morning of the 17th of June'... 'Ismail Beg’s defeat was complete and irretrievable. His army ceased to exist as an instrument of war.'; HCIP VIII p. 261: 'Sindia’s forces once more took the field and this time destroyed Ismail Beg’s army on the plains of Agra (18 June, 1788)'; chronology p. 837 gives 17/18 June

events.text: Battle of Chaksana: The Battle of Chaksana was fought between the Mughal Empire and the Maratha Confederacy in 1788.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia) vs Najib-ud-Daula (Rohilla) — Ghulam Qadir, with Ismail Beg's Mughal troops
events.outcome: Rohilla–Mughal victory (Ghulam Qadir and Ismail Beg); the Maratha cavalry broke and De Boigne's battalions covered the withdrawal
events.commanders: Mahadaji Shinde — Isma'il Beg
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 261: 'At Chaksana, eight miles from Bharatpur, the two armies met (April 1788). The Maratha cavalry cracked before the furious onslaught of the Musalman chiefs, but the day was saved by De Boigne’s battalions; the Maratha army withdrew'; chronology p. 837: 'Sindia’s army is defeated at the battle of Chaksana by the Rohillas'

events.text: Capture of Delhi (1788): The Capture of Delhi took place in 1788 between the forces of Ghulam Qadir Rohilla supported by Mirza Ismail Beg, and the Marathas under Mahadji Shinde on behalf of Shah Alam II.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia) vs Najib-ud-Daula (Rohilla) — Ghulam Qadir, with Ismail Beg
events.outcome: Maratha victory; Mahadji Sindhia occupied Delhi on 2 October 1788 and restored Shah Alam II on 16 October; Ghulam Qadir fled and was captured on 31 December
events.commanders: Ghulam Qadir, Mirza Ismail Beg — Mahadji Scindia, Ali Bahadur, Rane Khan
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 838: '1788, October 2 Mahadji Sindia occupies Delhi (p. 399). 1788, October 16 Shah Alam II is reinstated on the Delhi throne by the Marathas (p. 399). 1788, December 31 Ghulam Qadir captured'

events.text: Ghulam Qadir blinds Shah Alam II: the Rohilla Ghulam Qadir, with Ismail Beg, seizes Delhi (30 July 1788), deposes Shah Alam II for Bidar Bakht and, hunting the palace treasure, gouges out the old emperor's eyes on 10 October; princes and princesses die of starvation before Mahadji Sindhia retakes the city.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire III p. 453: '§ 8. Shah Alam blinded... On 10th October, in a frenzy of vindictiveness and avarice, Ghulam Qadir had needles driven through the eyes of Shah Alam.'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 837-838: '1788, July 30 Ghulam Qadir and Ismail Beg jointly take possession of Delhi... 1788, August 1 Ghulam Qadir deposes Shah Alam II and installs Bidar Bakht' (HCIP dates the atrocities to August, Sarkar the blinding to 10 October)

events.text: Ghulam Qadir dies — The Rohilla who blinded Shah Alam II, captured by Mahadji Sindhia's men, blinded in his turn and put to death near Mathura.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 838: '1788, December 31 Ghulam Qadir captured (p. 262)... 1789, March 3 Ghulam Qadir put to death (p. 399).'; Sarkar IV p. 9: '3rd March the Ruhela’s eyes were dug out and sent in a casket to Shah Alam'

events.text: Third Anglo-Mysore War
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 463-465.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Maratha Empire, Hyderabad, Travancore vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory, with the Marathas and Hyderabad; by the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792) Tipu surrenders half his territory
events.commanders: Lord Cornwallis and British EIC; Peshwa Madhavrao II/Nana Fadnavis; Nizam Ali Khan; Dharma Raja of Travancore — Tipu Sultan of Mysore

events.text: Tipu's attack on the Travancore Lines: Tipu's first assault on the Nedumkotta on 29 December 1789 is thrown back; on 15 April 1790 he breaks through, takes Cranganore, Ayakotta, Alangad and Parur and reaches Alwaye, but withdraws when the Company declares war — the cause of the Third Mysore War.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs Travancore
events.outcome: Mysore victory; the Lines are breached in April 1790 after the December 1789 repulse, but Tipu withdraws from Kerala
events.commanders: Tipu Sultan — Dharma Raja (Karthika Tirunal Rama Varma), Raja Kesava Das
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 248: 'Tipu attacked the Travancore Lines on the 29th December 1789 ... On the 15th April 1790 the Travancore Lines were breached and Travancore troops were put to flight.' HCIP VIII p. 463: 'Tipu's first attack on Travancore lines failed ... His next attack came in April, 1790.'

events.text: Battle of Merta: Sindhia's army under De Boigne defeats the Jodhpur army in Marwar. Bijay Singh of Jodhpur came to terms with Mahadji Sindhia the following January.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) vs Jodhpur (Marwar)
events.outcome: Scindia victory; De Boigne's brigades break the Rathor army; Jodhpur comes to terms, January 1791
events.commanders: Benoît de Boigne; Bijay Singh of Jodhpur
events.source: The Maratha Supremacy (HCIP VIII), printed p. 838 (chronology). Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 256: 'the decisive blow which he struck against Jodhpur in the battle of Merta (September 1790) disturbed the balance of power in Hindustan.'

events.text: Battle of Patan: Mahadji Sindhia's brigades under Benoît de Boigne break the Rajput confederacy of Jaipur and Jodhpur, with the Mughal contingent of Ismail Beg, on the plain at Patan. It is the victory that reverses the indecision of Lalsot three years earlier and opens Rajputana to Maratha tribute.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) vs Jaipur, Jodhpur (Marwar), Ismail Beg's Mughal troops
events.outcome: Scindia victory; the Rajput confederacy broken (20 June 1790)
events.commanders: Benoît de Boigne, Gopal Rao Bhau; Ismail Beg
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV ch. 38. Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 256: 'Ismail Beg and Bijay Singh of Jodhpur had assisted Pratap Singh of Jaipur in the battle of Tunga. These three allies again joined their forces and challenged Sindhia, but De Boigne's battalions crushed them in the battle of Patan (20 June, 1790).'

events.text: Siege of Darwar: The Siege of Darwar was a 29 week siege of the fort at Dharwad in 1790 and 1791, then near the frontier, between the Kingdom of Mysore and the Maratha Empire.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, East India Company vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: Anglo-Maratha victory
events.commanders: Parushram Patwardhan, John Little, Charles Frederick — Badr ul-Zaman Sahib
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Koppal: The Siege of Koppal was conducted during the Third Anglo-Mysore War by forces of the Nizam of Hyderabad under the command of Mahabat Jung.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Mysore vs Hyderabad, British East India Company
events.outcome: Anglo-Hyderabadi victory
events.commanders: Tipu Sultan — Mahabat Jung, Hugh Montgomery
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Sodhra: The Siege of Sodhra was a siege fought between the Sukerchakia Misl under Mahan Singh and the Bhangi Misl under Sahib Singh Bhangi of Gujrat.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl vs Bhangi Misl
events.outcome: Bhangi victory
events.commanders: Mahan Singh, Ranjit Singh — Sahib Singh Bhangi, Karam Singh Dulu
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Arakere (Karighatta): Cornwallis, marching on Srirangapatna, drives Tipu from his position on 15 May 1791 — but with his army starving he abandons the siege five days later and falls back on Bangalore.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Tipu withdraws into Srirangapatna, but Cornwallis gives up the attack on 20 May
events.commanders: Lord Cornwallis — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 464: 'In an action at Arikera Tipu could not maintain his ground and had to withdraw to Seringapatam.' Hayavadana Rao III p. 785-787 synopsis (block 683): 'Tipu opposes the English at Karighatta ... the English victory on the 15th ... Lord Cornwallis relinquishes the attempt against Seringapatam, May 20, 1791'.

events.text: Battle of Shimoga: The Capture of Shimoga, a town and fortress held by forces of the Kingdom of Mysore, occurred on 3 January 1792, after a preliminary battle.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, East India Company vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: Anglo-Maratha victory
events.commanders: Parshuram Bhou, John Little — Reza Sahib
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Capture of Hooly Honore: The Capture of Hooly Honore, a town and fortress held by forces of the Kingdom of Mysore, occurred on 21 December 1791, after two days of siege.
events.belligerents: Maratha Confederacy, British East India Company vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: Maratha-British victory
events.commanders: Parshuram Bhou, John Little — Unknown
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Nepalese conquest of western Sikkim: the Gorkhas invade Sikkim in 1791 and by 1793 hold all its territory south and west of the Tista.
events.belligerents: Nepal vs Kingdom of Sikkim (Namgyal)
events.outcome: Nepal victory; Sikkim west of the Tista annexed until restored by the Company in 1817
events.commanders: — Tenzing Namgyal
events.source: HCIP IX p. 1065: 'the only important event after that seems to be a Nepalese invasion in 1791. Two years later, during the Sino-Napalese war, the Nepalese firmly established themselves in the Sikkim territory, lying to the south and west of the river Tista.'

events.text: Siege of Bangalore: The Siege of Bangalore was a siege of the town and fortifications of Bangalore during the Third Anglo-Mysore War by forces of the British East India Company.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Kingdom of Great Britain vs Kingdom of Mysore
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Charles Cornwallis — Tipu Sultan (outside the lines), Sipahdar Sahib (lower fort), Buhadur Sahib (upper fort)
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Coimbatore: The Siege of Coimbatore was a siege conducted by forces of the Kingdom of Mysore against a garrison of British East India Company and Travancorean troops.
events.belligerents: Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu) vs East India Company, Travancore
events.commanders: Tipu Sultan — John Chalmers
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 464: 'His siege train having been destroyed, Cornwallis ... fell back to Bangalore. Tipu recaptured Coimbatore.'
events.outcome: Mysore victory; Tipu recaptures Coimbatore after Cornwallis's retreat

events.text: Siege of Goorumconda: The Siege of Goorumconda was a series of conflicts fought at Goorumconda, a hill fort northeast of Bangalore, during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Mysore vs Hyderabad, British East India Company
events.outcome: Anglo-Hyderabadi victory
events.commanders: Shezada Hyder Ali — Mahabat Jung, Captain Read
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Nundydroog: The Siege of Nundydroog was conducted by British Indian forces under the command of General Charles Cornwallis in October 1791, during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
events.belligerents: Kingdom of Mysore vs East India Company
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Tipu Sultan — Charles Cornwallis
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Savendroog: The Siege of Savendroog was conducted by British East India Company forces under the command of General Charles Cornwallis in December 1791, during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
events.belligerents: Sultanate of Mysore vs East India Company
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Tipu Sultan — General Charles Cornwallis
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: The Nepal–Tibet war and the Chinese invasion of Nepal: after Gorkha raids into Tibet, a Qing army drives the Gurkhas back and advances to within a few miles of Kathmandu, forcing a peace; China tightens its grip on Tibet and closes the passes to India.
events.belligerents: Qing China and Tibet vs Nepal
events.outcome: Qing victory; Nepal accepts peace and quinquennial tribute to Peking
events.commanders: Fuk’anggan — Bahadur Shah (regent), Damodar Pande
events.source: HCIP IX p. 1059: 'in 1791-1792 when war broke out between Nepal and Tibet, leading to the intervention of China. A Chinese army supported the Tibetans in driving back the Gurkhas from Tibet and advancing within a few miles of the capital of Nepal.' HCIP IX p. 1021: 'in 1792, when the Gurkhas of Nepal invaded Tibet and a Chinese army drove them out ... they closed all the passes of Tibet to natives of India.'

events.text: Dundiya rebellion: The Dundiya rebellion was a late 18th century uprising against the Ahom kingdom in the Borphukan's domain.
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Seringapatam (1792): The 1792 siege of Seringapatam was a battle and siege of the Mysorean capital city of Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) at the end of the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Hyderabad, Maratha Empire vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; after the Sultan's redoubt falls, Tipu offers terms and surrenders half his dominions
events.commanders: Charles Cornwallis, Robert Abercromby, Parshuram Bhou — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 464-465: 'When the most important of his redoubts, called the Sultan's redoubt, was taken by Cornwallis ... Tipu offered terms. Half of his territory he surrendered'.

events.text: The Treaty of Seringapatam: Tipu cedes half his dominions to the Company, the Marathas and the Nizam — Malabar, Dindigul and Baramahal to the Company — frees Coorg and pays 3.3 crores (preliminaries 22 February, definitive treaty 18 March 1792).
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 464-465: 'Half of his territory he surrendered, to be divided equally among the three allies ... The British got Baramahal, Dindigul, as also Malabar. Tipu had also to give independence to the Raja of Coorg'. Hayavadana Rao III p. 922 (block 795): 'the Definitive Treaty of Seringapatam (March 18, 1792)'.

events.text: Battle of Lakheri: De Boigne's brigades and Sindhia's cavalry routed Tukoji Holkar's army (with Dudrenec's battalions) at the Lakheri pass on 1 June 1793, settling the Sindhia–Holkar rivalry in Rajputana in Sindhia's favour.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) vs Holkar (Indore State)
events.outcome: Scindia victory; Holkar 'knocked out of the Rajput ring', Jaipur passes under Sindhia's control
events.commanders: Benoît de Boigne, Gopal Bhau, Lakhwa Dada — Tukoji Holkar's army under Malhar Rao, Dudrenec
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV p. 50: 'by the middle of 1793, Holkar had been knocked out of the Rajput ring, in consequence of Sindhia's victory at Lakheri (1st June) and the Jaipur State came under Sindhia's control.' Battle narrative pp. 93–94. Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 256: 'The Sindhia-Holkar rivalry reached its climax in the battle of Lakheri (June 1793). Holkar's defeat decided the political issue in favour of Sindhia.'

events.text: First Pazhassi revolt: Kerala Varma Pazhassi Raja of Kottayam, passed over when the Company leased Kottayam to his uncle, stops the revenue and wages guerrilla war from Wynad; on 18 March 1797 Major Cameron's column is cut to pieces in the Periya pass and the Company treats.
events.belligerents: Pazhassi Raja (Kottayam) vs East India Company
events.outcome: Pazhassi victory; the Kurumbranad lease is cancelled and the Raja accepts a pension of Rs 8,000
events.commanders: Kerala Varma Pazhassi Raja — Col. Dow, Major Cameron, Jonathan Duncan
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 261: 'On March 18, 1797, a contingent of 1,100 men under Major Cameron was ambushed and cut to pieces ... truce with the Pazhassi Raja became a matter of political expediency ... The agreement with the Kurumbranad Raja was cancelled'.

HCIP VIII p. 479: 'Special attention must be devoted to Cornwallis’ Permanent Settlement of Bengal land revenue ... Cornwallis, faced with a country in ruins, decided on Permanent Settlement making the zamindars or rent collectors permanent land-owners. The settlement secured for the Company a fixed amount of revenue.' HCIP IX p. 374 gives the date: 'the Permanent Settlement of 1793'.
events.text: The Permanent Settlement: Cornwallis fixes the land revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa for ever and makes the zamindars its proprietors; the cultivators become their tenants.
Battle of Dhai Ali: The Battle of Dhai Ali was fought between Captain Welsh of the East India Company and the Moamorias led by Bharath Singha, reinforced by a contingent of troops sent to his aid.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Ahom Dynasty vs Moamorias
events.outcome: British/Ahom Victory
events.commanders: Captain Welsh, Gaurinath Singha — Bharath Singha, Godha Barbarua
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Mardanpur: The Battle of Mardanpur was fought between the Sikh forces of Patiala state led by Bibi Sahib Kaur and the Maratha forces led by Lakshmi Rao.
events.belligerents: Patiala vs Maratha Confederacy
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Bibi Sahib Kaur, Sardar Tara Singh Ghaiba, Raja Bhag Singh — Lakshmi Rao, Ghanta Rao, Anta Rao
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Mahadji Scindia dies — At Wanowrie near Pune, of a fever; the Maratha who had held Delhi and its emperor.
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 839: '1794, February 12 Death of Mahadji Sindia at Vanawadi (near Poona) (pp. 263, 407).'

events.text: Battle of Kharda: The Battle of Kharda also called the Battle of Khurla, took place in 1795 between the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Maratha Empire, in which the Nizam was defeated.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs Hyderabad
events.outcome: Maratha victory; the Nizam, shut up without food or water in Kharda fort, sought a cease-fire (13 March) and by the treaty of 10 April 1795 ceded territory worth about 32 lakhs including Daulatabad and gave up his minister Azim-ul-Umara
events.commanders: Parashuram Bhau Patwardhan, Scindia's army under Jivba Bakhshi, Tukoji Holkar, Raghuji Bhonsle — Nizam Ali, Azim-ul-Umara
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 446: 'the final battle took place on 11 March, 1795 ... Sindia's forces forced back the Nizam's troops. The Nizam took shelter in the small fort of Kharda ... the Nizam realised the futility of resistance and requested for a cessation of hostilities'; p. 447: 'Territories yielding an annual revenue of about 32 lakhs ... including the fort of Daulatabad, were to be ceded to the Peshwa.'

events.text: Gaurinath Singha dies — The Ahom king of the Moamaria rebellion, restored by Captain Welsh’s expedition; after him the Buragohain Purnananda ruled Assam in fact.
events.source: HCIP IX p. 127: 'After the death of king Gaurinath Singh in A.D. 1795, the Bura Gohain, Purnananda, murdered his rival, the Bar Barua, and placed on the throne his own nominee Kamaleswar Singh'; its note 2 (p. 144): 'Bhuyan, p. 429; Banerjee gives the date as 1794.' Acharyya p. 131 lists his reign as ending 1794.

events.text: Invasion of Ceylon (1795): The British take Dutch Ceylon — Trincomalee, Batticaloa, Jaffna, Mullaitivu and Mannar fell through the autumn, and Colombo surrendered on 15 February 1796.
events.source: BharatRajya research pass, Sri Lanka (see scripts/add_srilanka_battles.py)
events.belligerents: Britain vs the Batavian Republic
events.outcome: Ceylon passes to Britain

events.text: Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah dies — the Company's Nawab of Arcot since the Carnatic wars, whose debts to Company servants drew the Company ever deeper into the Carnatic.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 484: 'Muhammad Ali died in October, 1795 and Umdat-ul-Umara succeeded him.'

events.text: Peshwa Sawai Madhavrao dies — from a fall from a palace window in Poona, seven months after Kharda.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 263: 'The Peshwa from whom he derived support, accidentally fell down from a palace window or committed suicide (27 October, 1795).'

events.text: Action near Sardhana: Bapuji Sindhia, Sindhia's amil of Saharanpur, attacks a Rohilla raiding force near Sardhana and, after a very long action, totally defeats and disperses it; the Rohilla leader Umar Khan and his son are killed and a standard taken. The Resident judged it unlikely the Rohillas would again 'raise commotion in the Doab'.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) — Bapuji Sindhia, amil of Saharanpur — vs Rohilla raiders under Umar Khan
events.outcome: Sindhia victory; Umar Khan and his son killed; Rohilla incursions into the upper Doab end
events.commanders: Bapuji Sindhia; Umar Khan (killed)
events.source: William Palmer, Resident with Sindhia, to Sir John Shore, Governor-General, from Lakhwa Dada's camp, 24 October 1796 — letter no. 40 in Jadunath Sarkar (ed.), Daulat Rao Sindhia and North Indian Affairs (Poona Residency Correspondence). Facsimile supplied by the Scindia Research Centre, Gwalior, September 2026. A Resident's dispatch six days after the action; the amil's own report is its source.

events.text: Bajirao II becomes Peshwa: after Sawai Madhavrao's death, Raghunathrao's son is installed on 5 December 1796, aged twenty-one, by Nana Phadnavis with the consent of Scindia, Holkar, the Bhonsle and the Nizam.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 488: 'He was installed as the Peshwa at the age of twenty-one on December 5, 1796, by Nana Phadnis with the consent of the great feudatories of the State—Sindia, Holkar, Bhosle and the Nizam.'

events.text: Battle of Amritsar (1797): during Shah Zaman's occupation of Lahore the Sikhs, some fifty thousand strong, fought the Durrani army at Amritsar on 12 January 1797 and drove it back to the gates of Lahore.
events.belligerents: Sikh misls vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory; the Durrani army gave way and was pursued to Lahore; Shah Zaman soon withdrew to Afghanistan
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs III p. 76 ('Shah Zaman defeated at Amritsar'): 'It commenced at 8 o'clock in the morning on the 12th January ... Both the armies thus continued for nearly four hours, when the Durrani army gave way. They "were pursued by the Scikhs to the very entrance of Lahore."'

events.text: Battle of Gujrat (1797): Ahmad Khan Shahanchi Bashi, Shah Zaman's governor at Rohtas, surprised the Sikh chiefs near Gujrat on 29 April 1797 and drove them into the fort, but was shot dead from its walls; his army broke and was pursued to the Jhelum.
events.belligerents: Sikh misls vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory; the Durrani governor killed and some 3,000 Afghans slain or wounded
events.commanders: Sahib Singh Bhangi, Milkha Singh and others — Ahmad Khan Shahanchi Bashi
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs III pp. 85–86: 'In the hailstorm of balls and bullets Ahmad Khan was struck dead. The Durrani troops finding themselves leaderless sought safety in flight. They were hotly pursued by the Sikhs as far as the banks of the Jhelum ... nearly 3,000 Afghans were slain and wounded.'

events.text: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 466: 'He had no allies to help him. The Nizam's army did not play much effectual part on the British side and the Peshwa's troops were not there to help the British.' Sardesai III p. 360: 'Wellesley resented the Peshwa's refusal to join in his war against Tipu Sultan'.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Hyderabad vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Tipu killed at Srirangapatna on 4 May 1799 and his dynasty ended
events.commanders: Lord Wellesley; General George Harris; Arthur Wellesley; Nizam Ali Khan and allied Indian forces — Tipu Sultan of Mysore

events.text: Hyderabad's subsidiary alliance: on 1 September 1798 Wellesley binds Nizam Ali to a subsidiary alliance, and a British force replaces the Nizam's French-officered corps.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 449: 'Immediately on his arrival Wellesley bound the Nizam with the subsidiary alliance on 1 September, 1798, and substituted his French force with that of the British.'

events.text: Karthika Tirunal Rama Varma, the Dharma Raja of Travancore, dies — forty years king, host to the refugees of the Mysore invasions, builder of the Nedumkotta and patron of Kathakali.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 237: 'When the Raja passed away in 1798 after a long reign of 40 years he was already 74 years old.'

events.text: Shah Zaman's last invasion: the Durrani king re-entered the Punjab in the autumn of 1798 and sat at Lahore, but could not bring the Sikhs to battle or to submission, and retired from the Punjab in January 1799 — the last invasion of India from the north-west.
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs III p. 97 ('The Shah enters India'): 'Shah Zaman left Kabul early in September, and reached Peshawar by the end of the month'; p. 117: '27. Shah Zaman retires from the Panjab. From the 1st to the 3rd January, 1799, the Shah held repeated conferences ...'. Preface: 'The last Muslim invasion of India took place in 1799.'

events.text: Battle of Fatehpur (1799): The Battle of Fatehpur was fought in March 1799, in present-day Sikar district of India, between the Maratha Kingdom of Gwalior and the Rajput Kingdom of Jaipur.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) — Vaman Rao with George Thomas — vs Jaipur
events.outcome: Scindia victory; George Thomas's corps routs the Jaipur army; the Rajputs lose over 2,000, Thomas 300
events.commanders: Sawai Pratap Singh, Rora Ramji Khawas, Rawat Megh Singhji Rajawat — Vamana Rao, General George Thomas
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV pp. 229–230 ('§10 Battle of Fathpur, February 1798'): 'The rout of the enemy was complete ... On that long and bloody day, the Rajput casualties exceeded 2,000, while Thomas lost 300 men.' Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 257: 'In 1799 the Marathas, assisted by George Thomas ... invaded Jaipur territory and defeated the Rajputs in the battle of Fatehpur.' Both books give the victory to the Maratha side; they differ on the year (Sarkar February 1798, Bakshi 1799).

events.text: Battle of Malavalli: on 27 March 1799 Harris's main army, with the Nizam's contingent under Arthur Wellesley, beats Tipu's attempt to stop its march on Srirangapatna.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Hyderabad vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Tipu falls back on his capital
events.commanders: George Harris, Arthur Wellesley — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 466: 'Tipu was defeated by Stewart at Sedasere and by Harris at Malavally. He was driven to the defences of his capital'. Hayavadana Rao III index (block 1203): 'action at between the English and Tipu as described by Gen. Harris (March 27, 1799), 974-977'.

events.text: Battle of Pattankudi: the Raja of Kolhapur, leading his army in person, defeats the Peshwa's general Parashuram Bhau Patwardhan near Pattankudi on 16 September 1799. Parashuram Bhau is mortally wounded.
events.belligerents: Kolhapur vs Maratha Empire (Patwardhan army)
events.outcome: Kolhapur victory; Parashuram Bhau Patwardhan totally defeated and mortally wounded
events.commanders: Raja Shivaji of Kolhapur — Parashuram Bhau Patwardhan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 238: 'near the village of Pattankudi he encountered the Kolhapur forces headed by the Raja himself when he suffered a total defeat and was mortally wounded (16 September, 1799).'

events.text: Battle of Sedaseer: the Bombay army under Stuart, advancing from the west coast, repulses Tipu's attack in the Coorg hills early in March 1799.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Tipu repulsed
events.commanders: James Stuart — Tipu Sultan
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 466: 'Tipu was defeated by Stewart at Sedasere and by Harris at Malavally.' Hayavadana Rao III p. ~1069 (block 916, contemporary letter): 'the repulse he met at Sedaseer (about 20 days before)'.

events.text: Fall of Srirangapatna; Tipu Sultan dies defending Mysore
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 466: 'the siege was begun on 17 April and the assault was made on 4 May, 1799. Tipu fell fighting bravely.'
events.belligerents: East India Company, Hyderabad vs Mysore Sultanate (Hyder Ali & Tipu)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Srirangapatna stormed on 4 May 1799 and Tipu killed
events.commanders: Lord Wellesley; General George Harris; Arthur Wellesley; Nizam Ali Khan and allied Indian forces — Tipu Sultan of Mysore

events.text: Maratha–Rajput Wars: Maratha–Rajput Wars refers to a series of conflicts between the Maratha Confederacy and the various Rajput states in the eighteenth century.
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire (Scindia and Holkar) vs Jaipur and Jodhpur (Marwar)

events.text: Ranjit Singh takes Lahore: with Rani Sada Kaur's Kanhaiya troops, the Sukerchakia chief entered Lahore through the Lahori Gate on 6 July 1799 and received the fort from Chait Singh on 7 July — the foundation of the Sikh monarchy.
events.belligerents: Sukerchakia Misl (Ranjit Singh), Kanhaiya Misl vs Sikh misls (Bhangi chiefs of Lahore)
events.outcome: Sukerchakia victory; Lahore occupied, Chait Singh and Mohar Singh allowed to retire
events.commanders: Ranjit Singh, Rani Sada Kaur — Chait Singh, Mohar Singh
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs V p. 30: 'Occupation of the Fort, 7 July, 1799 ... Chait Singh opened negotiations through Sada Kaur. He was permitted to retire in peace'; pp. 35–36: 'Ranjit Singh's occupation of Lahore formed an important landmark in the history of the Panjab. This event marked the beginning of the downfall of the independent chiefs on the one hand, and the establishment of a monarchy on the other.'

events.text: Thanjavur ceded: by treaty with Wellesley, Raja Serfoji II hands his whole territory except the fort to the Company and becomes a pensioned titular king.
events.source: HCIP IX (British Paramountcy) p. 82: 'By a treaty concluded in 1799 with Lord Wellesley, Raja Sarfoji of Tanjore transferred the whole of his territory, except the fort, to the British Government.' HCIP VIII p. 626: 'Tanjore was annexed in 1799'.

events.text: The Hawa Mahal of Jaipur: Sawai Pratap Singh’s screen of 953 windows for the women of the court.
events.source: Wikipedia (web-only; to be promoted to a book citation)

events.text: The Poligar Wars: the Company's attempt to end the palaiyakkarars' armed power in Tinnevelly, Madurai, Ramnad and Sivaganga provokes risings — Kattabomman of Panjalamkurichi (1799), then the Marudu brothers' league (1800–01) — ended by the disarming proclamation of 1 December 1801.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Tamil poligars (Panjalamkurichi, Sivaganga and allied palayams)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the poligars' military power suppressed and the southern districts disarmed
events.commanders: Company forces — Veerapandiya Kattabomman, Maruthu Pandiyar brothers, Oomaithurai
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 628: 'The so-called Palegar War of 1799-1801 was marked by a recrudescence of anarchy and followed by their final suppression. Government, by a proclamation of 1 December, 1801, suppressed the use of all weapons of defence'. (Names of leaders: web-only; library silent.)

events.text: The Wodeyars restored: by the Partition Treaty (22 June) Tipu's lands are shared out; the five-year-old Krishnaraja Wodeyar III is installed on 30 June with Purnaiya as Dewan, and the Subsidiary Treaty of 8 July lets the Company garrison Mysore.
events.source: Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 1088: 'The Brahmans having fixed upon the 30th June as the most auspicious day for placing His Highness Sri Krishnaraja Wodeyar on the musnad of Mysore'; p. 1090 (block 934): 'Under the Subsidiary Treaty, concluded on 8th July 1799'. HCIP VIII p. 466: 'The Wodiyars ... were restored to a portion of the dominions'.

events.text: Tipu Sultan dies — Killed at the water-gate of Srirangapatna on 4 May 1799 as the British stormed the breach. Hayavadana Rao III p. 881.
events.source: C. Hayavadana Rao, History of Mysore III p. 1024 (block 881; running head '1024 HISTORY OF MYSORE'); HCIP VIII p. 466: 'Tipu fell fighting bravely.'

events.text: Veerapandiya Kattabomman dies — the palaiyakkarar of Panjalamkurichi who defied the Company's tribute demands; hanged at Kayathar on 16 October 1799.
events.source: web-only; library silent — HCIP VIII p. 628 names only 'The so-called Palegar War of 1799-1801'. The hanging at Kayathar in October 1799 is uncontested and he is the best-known figure of the Tamil resistance.

events.text: Battle of Malpura: Lakhwa Dada's army — Pohlmann's brigade of De Boigne's corps, Dudrenec's Holkar brigade and a Kota battalion — broke Sawai Pratap Singh's Jaipur army and its Rathor cavalry from Jodhpur on 16 April 1800, despite a Rathor charge that rode down Dudrenec's brigade.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia), Holkar (Indore State) contingent vs Jaipur, Jodhpur (Marwar)
events.outcome: Scindia victory; Jaipur's guns, camp and baggage lost; Pratap Singh pays 25 lakhs for peace
events.commanders: Lakhwa Dada, Pohlmann, Dudrenec — Sawai Pratap Singh, Sawai Singh (Jodhpur horse)
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV p. 159: 'Lakhwa struck a decisive blow at the Rajput army. Battle of Malpura, 16 April 1800.' Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 257: 'A decisive battle fought at Malpura in April 1800 ... 74 out of 80 pieces of cannon brought into the field were lost, together with the entire camp, baggage and warlike stores ... He made peace on payment of 25 lakhs (May 1800).'

events.text: Nana Fadnavis dies — At Pune; "with him departed all the wisdom and moderation of the Maratha government".
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 840: '1800, March 13 Death of Nana Phadnis'; p. 516 lists among the losses of the decade 'Nana Phadnis on 13 March, 1800'.

events.text: Rising of Dhondia Wagh: the Mysore adventurer raids the Dharwar country and kills Dhondopant Gokhale near Kittur; hunted by Arthur Wellesley and the Patwardhans, he is killed fighting near Bellary on 10 September 1800.
events.belligerents: East India Company, Maratha Empire vs Dhondia Wagh
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Dhondia killed with six hundred followers
events.commanders: Arthur Wellesley, the Patwardhans — Dhondia Wagh
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 362: 'he was compelled to stand an action at Bhanu near Bellary on 10th September 1800, when he was killed fighting along with six hundred followers.'

events.text: Second Pazhassi revolt: when the Company claims Wynad under the 1799 partition, Pazhassi Raja's Nairs, Kurichiyas and Mappilas fight a guerrilla war (Panamaram fort taken in 1802) until Baber's Kolkars corner the Raja, who is shot dead on 30 November 1805.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Pazhassi Raja (Kottayam)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the Raja killed and the resistance collapses
events.commanders: Arthur Wellesley, Col. Stevenson, T. H. Baber — Pazhassi Raja, Talakkal Chandu, Edachena Kunkan
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 261: 'In 1800 the Raja again rose in revolt ... The immediate cause ... was the British move to take possession of Wynad'; p. 263: 'On the 30th November 1805 the Raja was shot dead ... The death of the Pazhassi Raja symbolised the collapse of the resistance movement.'

events.text: Battle of Indore (1801): three months after Yashwantrao Holkar took Ujjain, Daulatrao Scindia's army under Sarje Rao Ghatge defeats him at Indore on 14 October 1801 and scatters his forces.
events.belligerents: Gwalior (Scindia) vs Holkar (Indore State)
events.outcome: Scindia victory; Yashwantrao Holkar defeated and his forces scattered
events.commanders: Sarje Rao Ghatge — Yashwantrao Holkar
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 491: 'Yashwant Rao, however, suffered a defeat at the hands of Sarza Rao Ghatge on 14 October, 1801'; chronology p. 841: '1801, October 14 Daulat Rao Sindia attacks Indore and scatters the forces of Holkar'.

events.text: Battle of Ujjain: The Battle of Ujjain took place on 18 July 1801 near Ujjain between the rival factions of the Maratha Empire.
events.belligerents: Holkar (Indore State) vs Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: Holkar victory; Yashwantrao Holkar captured Ujjain on 18 July 1801
events.commanders: Yashwantrao Holkar — Scindia's officers
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 491: 'near Satwas, Captain Brownrigg, another officer of Sindia, defeated Yashwant Rao on 4 July, 1801. Yashwant Rao redeemed his honour by the capture of Ujjain on July 18, 1801'; chronology p. 841: '1801, July 18 Yashwant Rao Holkar captures Ujjain.'

events.text: The Carnatic annexed: Wellesley declares the Nawab a public enemy on Tipu's papers; on Umdat-ul-Umara's death (15 July 1801) his nephew Azim-ud-daula accepts the title and a pension, and the Company takes over the whole civil and military government.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 526: 'Umdat-ul-Umara died on 15 July, 1801 ... the offer was made to a nephew of the deceased Nawab, Azim-ud-daulah. He accepted ... and the whole civil and military administration was taken over by the British.'

events.text: The Marudu brothers (Periya and Chinna Marudu) die — the Sivaganga leaders of the 1800–01 poligar league and its Tiruchirappalli proclamation; hanged at Tiruppattur on 24 October 1801.
events.source: web-only; library silent — HCIP VIII p. 628 records only the Palegar War of 1799-1801 and its end in the proclamation of 1 December 1801. The execution is uncontested and they are the war's central figures.

events.text: The Treaty of Lucknow (1801): under pressure from Wellesley, Nawab-Wazir Saadat Ali Khan signs a new subsidiary treaty in November 1801 ceding Rohilkhand, Gorakhpur and the lower Ganga–Jamuna Doab — about half his kingdom — to the Company.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 524: 'The unfortunate Nawab had to yield, “a passive, helpless and reluctant obedience”. In November 1801 a new subsidiary treaty was signed by which he ceded what are now known as Gorakhpur and Rohilkhand divisions, besides the lower portion of the Ganga-Jamuna Doab.'

events.text: Baroda's subsidiary alliance: by the convention of Cambay (March 1802) and the treaty of 6 June 1802, Anandrao Gaekwad accepts a British subsidiary force of 2,000 sepoys and cedes Dholka, Nadiad, Vijapur and Kadi to pay for it.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 290: 'entered into a convention with him at Cambay in March, 1802 by which Raoji agreed to receive a subsidiary force of two thousand sepoys ... He had already (6 June 1802) entered into a subsidiary alliance with the East India Company'.

events.text: Battle of Poona: The Battle of Pune took place on 25 October 1802 near Pune between the states of the Maratha Confederacy.
events.belligerents: Holkar (Indore State) vs Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: Holkar victory; Yashwantrao defeated the Peshwa's and Scindia's armies at Hadapsar and Bajirao II fled Poona for the coast
events.commanders: Yashwantrao Holkar, Amrutrao — Baji Rao II, Daulat Rao Sindhia
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 492: 'Yashwant's victory over Sindia's general Sadashiv Bhaskar in the plains of Hadapsar on 25 October, 1802 ... The Peshwa fled from Poona ... Yashwant Rao Holkar's triumph at Hadapsar drove the Peshwa into the arms of the English.'

HCIP VIII p. 492: 'the treaty of Bassein which was "constructed after the latest and most approved model of subsidiary alliances". It was signed before the commencement of the New Year and ratified by the Governor-General on March 18, 1803. By this treaty, the Peshwa agreed to receive from the Company on a permanent basis no less than 6,000 regular native infantry'.
events.text: The Treaty of Bassein: Peshwa Bajirao II, driven from Poona by Holkar, accepts a subsidiary alliance with the Company at Bassein; Scindia and Bhonsle refuse it, and the second Anglo-Maratha war begins.
Battle of Argaon: The Battle of Argaon took place on 29 November 1803, between the British under the command of Major-General Arthur Wellesley and the forces of the Bhonsles of Berar.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Nagpur (Bhonsle), Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the Bhonsle's army decisively defeated
events.commanders: Arthur Wellesley, James Stevenson, Nizam Ali Khan — Raghuji II, Daulat Sindhia
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 496: 'Wellesley's and Stevenson's combined army decisively defeated Bhosle at Argaon on 29 November, 1803. Bhosle's troops behaved with conspicuous gallantry.'

events.text: Battle of Assaye: Wellesley's outnumbered force narrowly beats Scindia's Marathas — his 'finest battle'
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Gwalior (Scindia), Nagpur (Bhonsle)
events.commanders: Arthur Wellesley — Gopal Rao Bhau, Vithal Pant Bakhshi
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the combined army of Scindia and Bhonsle was beaten, but at a cost of 663 European and 1,778 Indian casualties
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 495: 'On 23 September, 1803, in the hotly contested battle of Assaye ... the combined army of Sindia and Bhosle led by Gopal Rao Bhau and Vithal Pant Bakhshi was soundly beaten by Arthur Wellesley ... achieved at an enormous cost of men (663 Europeans and 1,778 Indian killed or wounded).'

events.text: Battle of Delhi (1803): The Battle of Delhi or Battle of Patparganj took place on 11 September 1803 during the Second Anglo-Maratha War, and involved British East India Company troops of the Bombay Army.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Bourquien's corps of Perron's army broken at Patparganj and driven into the Jamuna, and Shah Alam II passed under British protection
events.commanders: Gerard Lake — Daulat Scindia, Louis Bourquin, Sardar Wable
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV p. 292-293: 'It was a splendid victory; it completed the work begun at Aligarh by destroying Perron’s entire field army'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 841: '1803, September 11 The English army defeats Sindian forces at the battle of Delhi (pp. 266, 496).'

events.text: Battle of Laswari: The Battle of Laswari took place on 1 November 1803 near Laswari village, Alwar.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; 'the annihilation of the whole of the regular forces in Sindhia’s service', at a cost of 822 British casualties
events.commanders: Gerard Lake — Ambaji Ingle, Raghuji II, Daulat Sindhia
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV p. 306: 'The battle of Laswari ended in “the annihilation of the whole of the regular forces in Sindhia’s service commanded by French officers,” as Lake justly claimed after his victory... On the British side 822 men were “killed and wounded”'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 842

events.text: Capture of Gawilghur: Gawilghur in western India was captured by British East India Company forces under the command of Sir Arthur Wellesley on 15 December 1803, during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Nagpur (Bhonsle)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Gawilgarh stormed on 15 December 1803
events.commanders: Arthur Wellesley — Beni Rajput
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 496: 'Arthur and Stevenson captured Gawilgarh on December 15, 1803'; p. 248: the Treaty of Deogaon left the Raja 'the country ... south of the Narnalla and Gawilgarh hills'.

events.text: Fall of Agra (1803): Lake storms Sindhia's seven battalions outside Agra on 10 October and the fort, Sindhia's northern capital with its arsenal and 22 lakhs of treasure, surrenders on 18 October.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Agra fort surrendered on 18 October with all its stores
events.commanders: Gerard Lake — Col. George Hessing, Col. Sutherland
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV p. 294-295: '§7 The fall of Agra, 18th October... the fort was surrendered to the English on the 18th and all the immense wealth and armament within it fell into the victors’ hands' (OCR of the scan is damaged; the section heading is clear); HCIP VIII chronology p. 842: '1803, October 18 The English capture Agra (p. 496)'

events.text: First Kandyan War: a British force occupied a deserted Kandy in February, was destroyed by disease and guerrilla attrition, and the garrison that surrendered on 24 June was massacred, the sick killed in the hospital afterwards. No pitched battle was fought. The received British account of the massacre is now under scholarly revision in Sri Lanka.
events.source: BharatRajya research pass, Sri Lanka (see scripts/add_srilanka_battles.py)
events.belligerents: Britain under Hay Macdowall vs the kingdom of Kandy
events.outcome: British defeat; Kandy independent for another twelve years

events.text: Nizam Ali Khan (Asaf Jah II) dies — ruler of Hyderabad since the 1760s, who lost at Rakshasbhuvan and Kharda and accepted the subsidiary alliance of 1798.
events.source: Sardesai, New History of the Marathas III p. 352: 'During the seven years of Nizam Ali's illness (he died on 6th August 1803)'.

events.text: Second Anglo-Maratha War
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire vs East India Company
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Daulat Rao Scindia, Raghoji II Bhonsle and Yashwantrao Holkar; Peshwa Baji Rao II's alignment changed after Bassein — British EIC commanders Arthur Wellesley and Gerard Lake

events.text: Shah Alam II passes under British protection: after the battle of Patparganj the blind emperor invites Lake into Delhi; Lake's audience on 16 September 1803 ends Maratha control of the Mughal throne.
events.source: Sarkar, Fall of the Mughal Empire IV p. 293-294: '§6 Shah Alam II comes under British protection, 16th September... “The descendant of the great Akbar and Aurangzib was found blind and aged, stripped of authority and reduced to poverty”'; HCIP VIII chronology p. 841: '1803, September 16 Shah Alam seeks British protection.'

events.text: Siege of Ahmednagar: The siege of Ahmednagar was the first battle of the Second Anglo-Maratha War fought between the Maratha Confederacy and the British East India Company.
events.belligerents: British Empire, East India Company vs Maratha Empire
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Arthur Wellesley — Daulat Rao Scindia
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Siege of Aligarh: The siege of Aligarh, also known as the Battle of Aligarh, was fought between the Maratha Confederacy and the British East India Company during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire, Gwalior (Scindia)
events.outcome: British victory
events.commanders: Gerard Lake, James Skinner — Pierre Cuillier-Perron
events.source: HCIP VIII chronology p. 841: '1803, September 4 The English army led by Lake defeats Sindia’s forces at Aligarh (pp. 266, 496).'; Sarkar IV contents: 'Lake routs Perron, 281—storms Aligarh fort, 283'

events.text: The Treaty of Deogaon: after Assaye, Argaon and Gawilgarh, Raghuji II Bhonsle of Nagpur cedes Cuttack (Orissa) and all his land west of the Wardha, and accepts a British Resident.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 248: 'by the treaty of Deogaon concluded on 17 December, 1803. By the treaty the Raja was stripped of the province of Orissa and of the country west of the Wardha'; p. 496 dates it 19 December 1803. The two pages of the same book differ on the day.

events.text: The Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (30 December 1803): Daulat Rao Sindhia cedes everything between the Jamuna and the Ganges and north of Jaipur, Jodhpur and Gohad, with Broach and Ahmadnagar, and renounces control of the Mughal emperor.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 497: 'the treaty of Surji Anjangaon on 30 December, 1803. He recognised the treaty of Bassein and surrendered his territories between the Yamuna and the Ganga and all those situated to the north of Jaipur, Jodhpur and Gohad... and he renounced his control upon the Mughul emperor.'

events.text: Battle of Deeg: The Battle of Deeg, fought on 13 November 1804, took place outside Deeg, now in the Bharatpur district of Rajasthan, India.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Maratha Empire, Holkar (Indore State), Bharatpur
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Holkar's infantry defeated outside Dig on 13 November and the fortress captured on 23 December 1804
events.commanders: John Fraser, William Monson — Jaswantrao Holkar, Ranjit Singh
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 498: 'The latter suffered a reverse at Dig on 13 November, 1804... Ranjit Singh assigned the fort of Dig to Holkar... Dig was captured on 23 December, 1804'

events.text: Battle of Farrukhabad: The Battle of Farrukhabad, also called the Battle of Fatehgarh, was an engagement during the Second Anglo-Maratha War fought by forces of the East India Company.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire, Holkar (Indore State) vs East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Yashwant Rao Holkar routed by Lake's cavalry at Farrukhabad on 17 November 1804
events.commanders: Jaswantaro Holkar — Gerard Lake
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 498: 'Holkar himself was routed by Lake at Farrukhabad on 17 November, 1804, and was compelled to turn to Ranjit Singh, the Raja of Bharatpur, for supplies of money and arms.'

events.text: Battle of Khurbura: Pradyumna Shah of Garhwal falls fighting the Gorkha invasion
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: Garhwal Kingdom vs Nepal
events.outcome: Nepal victory; Pradyumna Shah falls and Garhwal stays under Gorkha rule until 1815

events.text: Battle of Mukandwara Pass: The Battle of Mukandwara Pass, also known as the Battle of Mokandra Pass or Monson's Retreat, was fought from 8 to 10 July 1804 by forces of the Indore Maharaja.
events.belligerents: Maratha Empire Indore State vs British Empire, East India Company Kota State
events.outcome: Maratha victory
events.commanders: Yaswantrao Holkar, Wahid Ali Khan, Bakshi Shankar — William Monson, Amar Sing, Afsal Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Vizagapatam
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: East India Company / United Kingdom vs France
events.outcome: French victory
events.commanders: British/EIC naval forces at Vizagapatam; exact local commander varies — French squadron under Charles-Alexandre Durand Linois

events.text: Pazhassi Raja dies — Kerala Varma of the Kottayam house, who fought the Company from the Wynad forests for twelve years; shot dead on 30 November 1805.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 263: 'On the 30th November 1805 the Raja was shot dead.'

events.text: Sakthan Thampuran dies — Rama Varma of Cochin (ruling in fact from 1769, crowned 1790), who broke the Nair nobility and centralised the state.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 241: 'Saktan Tampuran (1790-1805) ... he was in full charge of the administration of the State from 1769 onwards'.

events.text: Siege of Bharatpur (1805): The siege of Bharatpur took place between 2 January and 22 February 1805 in the Indian Princely state of Bharatpur, during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
events.belligerents: Bharatpur, Maratha Empire, Holkar (Indore State) vs East India Company
events.outcome: Bharatpur victory; Lake's assaults on the fort failed and the siege became a blockade, with 3,203 British casualties — though the Raja then sued for peace (April 1805), paying twenty lakhs and giving up Dig
events.commanders: Ranjit Singh, Jaswantrao Holkar — Gerard Lake
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 498-499: 'The siege of Bharatpur by Lake began on 7 January, 1805. Three attempts to take the fort by assault having failed, Lake converted the siege into a blockade... The Raja of Bharatpur, despite his success, realised he could not stand up to the British and sued for peace... He paid twenty lakhs'; HCIP IX p. 30: 'The fort of Bharatpur, which had defied four attacks of Lord Lake in 1805'

events.text: The Treaty of Mustafapur (21 November 1805): Cornwallis's peace with Daulat Rao Sindhia restores Gwalior fort and Gohad to him while he renounces all claims north of the Chambal.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 499: 'Daulat Rao Sindia concluded the treaty of Mustafapur with the Company’s Government on 21 November, 1805. Gohad and the fort of Gwalior were restored to him. But he renounced his claims on the territories north of the Chambal.'

events.text: The Treaty of Rajghat (Rajpurghat), 24 December 1805: pursued by Lake to the Beas, Yashwant Rao Holkar makes peace with the Company, renouncing his claims north of the Chambal and in Bundelkhand, ending the second Anglo-Maratha war.
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 499: 'Yashwant Rao was compelled to conclude the treaty of Rajpurghat with Lake on the banks of the Beas on 24 December, 1805.'; p. 149: 'Treaty of Rajghat (Dec. 24, 1805)'

events.text: Travancore's subsidiary alliance: a treaty negotiated by Velu Thampi makes Travancore a subsidiary ally paying Rs 8 lakhs a year and bound to take the Company's advice — the loss of its political freedom.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 258: 'A fresh treaty of alliance and friendship was concluded between the English and Travancore in 1805. Under this treaty Travancore became a subsidiary ally ... The treaty of 1805 which was negotiated by Velu Tampi Dalawa resulted in the loss of the political freedom of Travancore.'

events.text: Vellore Mutiny: sepoys of the Madras Army, provoked by orders against caste marks and beards and a new leather-cockaded turban, rise at Vellore, where Tipu's family lived, and kill many of the European garrison before the rising is crushed.
events.belligerents: Madras sepoys at Vellore vs East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory; the mutiny put down the same day (suppression: web-only; library silent)
events.commanders: — Col. Rollo Gillespie (web-only)
events.source: HCIP IX p. 428: 'the mutiny at Vellore in 1806. It was caused by what the sepoys regarded as an affront to their religion ... forbidding the men to wear the marks of caste upon their fore-heads, ordering them to shave off their beards'. HCIP IX p. 2: Bentinck 'recalled in 1807' over it.

events.text: Battle of Kasur: The battle of Kasur took place on 10 February 1807 between the Sikh Empire and the Afghan-appointed governor of Kasur, and was a part of the Afghan–Sikh Wars.
events.belligerents: Sikh Empire vs Kasur (Pathan chiefs Qutb-ud-din Khan and Nizam-ud-din's heirs)
events.commanders: Ranjit Singh, Jodh Singh, Hari Singh — Qutub ud Din
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs V p. 72: 'The battle was fought on 10 February, 1807. The Afghans were forced to take shelter in the fort ... Phula Singh and his Nihangs made a sudden dash into a breach ... Qutb-ud-din was captured. Kasur was annexed in March, 1807.'
events.outcome: Sikh Empire victory; Kasur fort stormed and the principality annexed, March 1807

events.text: Revolt of Velu Thampi and Paliath Achan: the chief ministers of Travancore and Cochin storm the Resident's house at Cochin (18 December 1808), attack Cochin, and Velu Thampi calls the people to arms in the Kundara Proclamation (11 January 1809); defeated at Quilon and deserted by his Raja, he kills himself.
events.belligerents: Travancore, Cochin vs East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Velu Thampi dies, Paliath Achan is deported, and Cochin becomes a subsidiary ally (6 May 1809)
events.commanders: Velu Thampi Dalawa, Paliath Achan — Col. Macaulay, Col. St. Leger
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 264: 'On the midnight of December 18, 1808, the Resident's house at Cochin was stormed ... proclamation dated ... (January 11, 1809)'; p. 265: 'By a treaty concluded on 6th May 1809 Cochin became a subsidiary ally of the British'.

events.text: Relief of Kangra: called in by Raja Sansar Chand, Ranjit Singh surrounded Amar Singh Thapa's Gorkha army that had besieged Kangra fort for three years and cut off its supplies; the Gorkhas withdrew and the Sikhs took the fort on 24 August 1809, ending Nepali expansion west of the Sutlej.
events.belligerents: Sikh Empire vs Nepal
events.outcome: Sikh Empire victory; Gorkhas raise the siege and retire, Kangra fort passes to Ranjit Singh
events.commanders: Ranjit Singh — Amar Singh Thapa
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs V pp. 68–69: 'Ranjit Singh surrounded the Gorkha army which had besieged the fort. He cut off their supplies completely ... Amar Singh raised the siege ... The Maharaja expelled Sansar Chand's men, and took possession of the fort on 24 August, 1809.'

Gupta, History of the Sikhs V p. 240: 'the Treaty was signed at Amritsar on 25 April, 1809'; p. 241, Article 1: 'the British Government will have no concern with the territories and subjects of the Raja to northward of the river Sutlej.'
events.text: The Treaty of Amritsar: Ranjit Singh and the Company fix the Sutlej as the boundary between them; the cis-Sutlej Sikh states pass under British protection, and the Punjab is his to the north of it.
Velu Thampi Dalawa dies — the Travancore minister who led the 1808–09 rising against the Company; cornered at Mannadi, he killed himself before capture.
events.source: Sreedhara Menon, Survey of Kerala History p. 265: 'Here, he was overpowered by the Raja's men but before they could capture him alive, the Dalawa committed suicide.'

events.text: Krishnakumari of Mewar dies — the sixteen-year-old princess whose hand Jaipur and Jodhpur had fought over was given poison by decision of the Mewar nobles, under pressure from Amir Khan.
events.source: Bakshi, Rajasthan through the Ages I p. 222: 'The nobles of Mewar held a conference and decided that disgrace to the royal family and the State could be avoided only by administering poison to Krishnakumari. The princess, then a girl of sixteen, took four cups of poison on 21 July, 1810.'

events.text: Battle of Anandpur (1812): The Battle of Anandpur was fought in 1812 by the Sikh forces led by Sodhi Surjan Singh and the Rajput forces of Kahlur led by Raja Mahan Chand.
events.belligerents: Sikh Empire vs Bilaspur State
events.outcome: Sikh victory
events.commanders: Ranjit Singh, Surjan Singh, Hukma Singh — Raja Chand
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Haidru (Attock): Diwan Mohkam Chand, bringing supplies to the Sikh garrison of Attock, beat Wazir Fateh Khan's Afghans and Dost Muhammad's ghazis near Haidru on the Indus on 9 July 1813; the Afghans fled across the river and Attock stayed Sikh.
events.belligerents: Sikh Empire vs Durrani (Afghan) Empire
events.commanders: Diwan Mohkam Chand — Wazir Fateh Khan, Dost Muhammad Khan
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs V pp. 101–102: 'His Ghazis and cavalry fled helter skelter towards the river ... As this battle was fought near the village of Haidru, it is called the battle of Haidru. It took place on 9 July, 1813 ... Ranjit Singh celebrated this victory by illuminating the cities of Lahore and Amritsar.' (Gupta gives 9 July; the row's text had 13 July.)
events.outcome: Sikh Empire victory; Fateh Khan's army driven across the Indus, Attock held

events.text: Battle of Hasan Abdal (1813): The Battle of Hasan Abdal took place on June 7, 1813, between the Sikhs led by Bhayya Ram Singh and Afghans led by Fateh Khan Barakzai at Hasan Abdal.
events.belligerents: Durrani (Afghan) Empire vs Sikh Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory; Bhayya Ram Singh's 500 men put to flight and Attock besieged
events.commanders: Fateh Barakzai — Bhayya Singh
events.source: Gupta, History of the Sikhs V pp. 99–100: 'Wazir Fatah Khan attacked Hasan Abdal on 7 June, 1813 with 2,000 Afghans. Ram Singh had only 500 horse and foot. About 50 men were killed on both sides. Ram Singh and his men took to flight.'

events.text: Anglo-Nepalese War: the Company invades the Gorkha empire on a front from the Sutlej to the Kosi; checked at Nalapani and Jaithak, it wins in Kumaon and at Malaun (1815) and at Makwanpur (1816), and the Treaty of Sugauli ends the war.
events.source: HCIP VIII pp. 531–532: 'The treaty of Sagauli signed in March 1816 made some modification in the terms concerning the cession of the Tarai ... this cession of Garhwal and Kumaon to the west of the Kali river drove a wedge of British territory between Sikh dominion on the one side and Gurkha dominion on the other.' HCIP IX p. 1025: 'the Anglo-Gurkha War which broke out in 1814 and was ended by the Treaty of Segowli on 4 March, 1816.'
events.belligerents: East India Company, Garhwal Kingdom, Patiala State, Kingdom of Sikkim vs Nepal
events.outcome: East India Company victory; by the Treaty of Sugauli (ratified 4 March 1816) Nepal cedes Garhwal and Kumaon west of the Kali and much of the Terai
events.commanders: Lord Moira / Francis Rawdon-Hastings; David Ochterlony; Garhwal's Sudarshan Shah; Patiala's Karam Singh; Sikkim ruler Tshudpud Namgyal — Nepalese leadership under Bhimsen Thapa; commanders Amar Singh Thapa and Balbhadra Kunwar

events.text: Battle of Baramulla (1814): The Battle of Baramulla was an engagement fought in 1814 during Ranjit Singh's expedition toward Kashmir.
events.belligerents: Sikh Empire vs Durrani Empire
events.outcome: Sikh victory The Sikh detachment later withdrew safely under negotiated terms
events.commanders: Ram Dayal, Dal Singh, Raja Khan — Mohammad Khan, Shakur Khan, Raja Khan
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Kashmir (1814): The Battle of Kashmir took place in 1814 after the battle of Attock.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire, Poonch, Rajouri vs Sikh Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Azim Khan, Ruhullah Khan, Raja Khan — Ranjit Singh, Diwan Dayal, Hari Nalwa
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Battle of Nalapani: the Gurkhas' epic stand at Kalanga opens the Anglo-Nepal War
events.belligerents: Nepal vs East India Company
events.outcome: East India Company victory at heavy cost; Gillespie killed in an impatient first assault, and after bombardment Balbhadra’s garrison broke out and escaped
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 531 (OCR partly garbled): 'The Gurkha commander, Balbhadra Singh, was a very intrepid soldier. Gillespie attempted an impatient assault, was killed ... bombardment was resorted to. The Gurkha commandant [evacuated] the place with the remnants of his garrison, escaping.'

events.text: Battle of Toshamaidan Pass: The Battle of Toshamaidan Pass was a military engagement that took place in June 1814 during the Sikh campaign to Kashmir.
events.belligerents: Durrani Empire vs Sikh Empire
events.outcome: Durrani victory
events.commanders: Ruhullah Khan, Aghar Khan — Sukh Dayal Sahu, Mazhar Ali
events.source: Wikipedia (category sweep, 2026-07)

events.text: Capture of East India Company ship Nautilus
events.source: Wikipedia: List of wars in the Indian subcontinent
events.belligerents: East India Company vs United States
events.outcome: American victory
events.commanders: East India Company ship Nautilus under Charles Boyce / EIC naval command — USS Peacock under Lewis Warrington

events.text: Second Kandyan War and the fall of Kandy: the Kandyan chiefs turned against Sri Vikrama Rajasinha and the British occupied the capital with little fighting. The Kandyan Convention of 2 March ceded the kingdom to the Crown - the end of some two thousand years of indigenous monarchy on the island, and the first time one power held all of it.
events.source: BharatRajya research pass, Sri Lanka (see scripts/add_srilanka_battles.py)
events.belligerents: Britain vs the kingdom of Kandy
events.outcome: Kandy annexed; the whole island under British rule

events.text: Siege of Malaun: Ochterlony, taking Ramgarh and the other Gurkha forts of the Sutlej hills one by one, forces Amar Singh Thapa to surrender Malaun (May 1815), ending Nepali rule west of the Kali.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Nepal
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Amar Singh Thapa surrenders Malaun and the Gorkha posts from the Sutlej to the Kali
events.commanders: David Ochterlony — Amar Singh Thapa, Bhakti Thapa
events.source: HCIP VIII p. 531: 'Ochterlony in the extreme west, however, succeeded in getting better of Amar Singh Thapa, the most celebrated of the Gurkha commanders. He succeeded in capturing two of the most important Gurkha forts' ... and 'compelled the Gurkha [commander Amar Singh] Thapa to surrender the strong fort of Malaun' (OCR partly garbled).

events.text: The Kumaon campaign: Gardner’s irregulars and Nicolls’s regulars push the Gorkhas back on Almora (April 1815) and force the surrender of Kumaon, although Hearsey’s column on the Kali is beaten and he is captured.
events.belligerents: East India Company vs Nepal
events.outcome: East India Company victory; Nepal surrenders the whole of Kumaon with its forts
